chapters.title: Chapter 301: The Coming Storm ...
paragraphs: Seraphina, Liana, and Seris were on the other three sides of the table. None of them had found time to rest since the Quest appeared.
First, Lian’s sudden attack on the Rootspire had happened.
Then the sound of the alarms.
Then the Main Quest appeared, warning about the awakening of a contaminated creature and the danger of The Black Silence entering Earth.
Rindo finally broke the silence. According to what he had understood, these girls knew.
"What exactly is the Corrupted Titan?"
His gaze moved among the three girls.
"The Quest talks about it as if everyone should know what we’re facing, but I had never even heard its name until today."
Seraphina looked at Seris for a moment, as if waiting for her to explain.
"We saw it inside the Giants’ Graveyard." Seris then answered calmly.
"You saw it?" Rindo frowned.
"She and Lian saw it." The young Pendragon nodded.
She curled her fingers around the chair’s handle.
The image of that vast space, the massive chains, and the creature sitting like a mountain in the darkness were still in her mind.
"Was it alive?"
"It was asleep. Almost."
"Was? Almost? I would appreciate a more precise explanation."
"Now I’m not sure. When we were there, the area around it was full of monsters. After we killed a few of them, their blood and energy were pulled toward the Titan." Seris kept her cold demeanor.
"The chains moved, and something around that creature reacted. It must have been The Black Silence."
She hadn’t fully reasoned out exactly what was happening like Lian, but she also knew many things.

"According to what we know, The Black Silence is a type of disaster that contaminates minds, causes bloodthirst and madness. The civilizations of this world fell that way, and living creatures turned into monsters." Seraphina explained. Worry could also be seen in her eyes.
Rindo thought about the Main Quest text.
[The Black Silence Calamity will gain access to Earth.]
"And according to the Quest, if we fail, that thing will enter Earth." He asked slowly, his voice full of urgency. If that was the case, they were doomed.
A brief silence formed.
Rindo stared at the Emberroot map, but the lines on the paper no longer had the same meaning.
A few minutes ago, their main problems were surviving in the Special Area and freeing the four prisoners.
Now the System had announced that a creature whose true power was unknown could gain access to their world.
He was still putting the information together when the council building’s door slammed open.
Everyone in the room immediately reacted. Seraphina drew her sword from its sheath.
Seris placed her hand on her sword’s hilt and turned her body toward the door.
Liana summoned Shadow Wolf from the chair’s shadow.
But the person who entered through the door was not a Cindari soldier.
Lian entered the building with burned and bloodied armor.
The broken chains were still hanging from his wrists and part of his chest. A deep line was on his side, and traces of black ash could be seen on his neck and face.
Behind him, Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian appeared.
And then Aren, with long gray hair, a weak body, and heavy chains dragging on the ground, entered the room.
No one spoke for a few seconds.
Seraphina was the first to lower her sword slightly. Her eyes moved over Lian’s face, his wounds, and then the three freed prisoners.
"You’re back?" Her tone was more a sign of disbelief than a question.
"You brought all of them? That fast? Only a few hours have passed." Liana looked at the group with a half-open mouth.
"It was a heroic rescue." Marcus said with a smile.
"Heroic, no. More like a complete destruction of the prison." Cassian said without losing his calm expression.
"That’s not a wrong definition." Ethan also nodded.
Rindo still hadn’t moved.
His gaze moved from Marcus to Ethan, from Ethan to Cassian, and then to the unknown gray-haired man.
Then it fixed on Lian again.
"You really broke through the Rootspire and came back here?"
Lian entered the room and preferred not to answer.
Rindo stared at him for a few moments. Before he could say anything, the city’s alarms changed.
A deeper and faster sound spread from inside Vhalaris’s roots.
All the building’s windows lit up with red light.
Outside, Ashfall Ward’s defensive veins began to glow, and the sound of several bridges closing was heard.
Rindo closed his eyes.
A long sigh came out from his nose.
"Really? Now we have to escape from an entire Cindari civilization? While dealing with a bigger problem?"
"Relax." Lian said.
"Relax?" His voice rose for the first time.
"You escaped from the city’s most secure prison. God knows how many people you killed. You freed four prisoners, and now the whole city is after us."
"When he puts it that way, it really sounds bad." Ethan whispered beside Marcus.
"Because it really is bad." Marcus answered quietly.
Seraphina sheathed her sword, but her angry gaze was still on Lian.
"I think you promised me you wouldn’t do anything crazy!"
"When did I promise that?" Lian asked in confusion. He didn’t remember such a thing.
"After you returned from the border city mission." Seraphina looked at his wounds.
"Well, this one wasn’t that dangerous."
"You really can never behave like a normal person?"
Seris, unlike the others, didn’t react strongly. Her gaze moved over the broken chains and battle marks for a moment.
Then a very small smile formed on her face.
"So you really did force your way out. I wish I had come too."
"What’s done is done, and I think we have bigger problems to deal with." Rindo placed his hand on his forehead.
Lian pointed at Aren.
"Before we decide what to do, I need to introduce someone."
All eyes fell on the gray-haired man.
Aren didn’t fully understand their conversation, but he followed their expressions and gazes.
Lian said.
"This is Aren. One of the humans from the previous Cycle. A native of the Ruined Realm.
The room’s atmosphere immediately changed.
Rindo lowered his hand from his forehead. Seraphina and Liana looked at Aren more carefully.
Cassian, Marcus, and Ethan also still didn’t know much of the information Lian had heard from Aren.
"Previous Cycle?" Rindo asked. He didn’t care as much about the "native of the Ruined Realm" part.
"That means he’s been here for twenty-five years?" He had heard about these 25-year cycles before.
"Twenty-five years here. Two hundred and fifty years in his own world." Lian answered calmly.
Even Seris lost control of her expression for the first time.
"Two hundred and fifty?"
Marcus furrowed his brows. Ethan put his smile aside.
"What do you mean?" Seraphina asked.
"Time here flows ten times slower?" Rindo frowned heavily.
"Unfortunately, yes."
"So when we return..." Marcus said quietly, but the meaning of his words was clear. Worry was also clear in his voice.
They had every right to be worried, and it made everyone think.

If they stayed here for just one year, it would be equivalent to ten years in their own world. In other words, when they returned, their friends might already have children, and an entire generation might have passed.
Even thinking about it was terrifying.
"Exactly. That’s why we need to finish our work and leave this place as soon as possible." Lian also nodded. He wanted to show them the urgency of the situation—that there was no time for nonsense.
"First, sit down." Rindo pointed at the chairs by the table.
Aren sat down with Marcus’s help.
His heavy chains fell to the floor with a loud clatter. Liana looked at the seals on his body for a moment.
"Can’t they be opened?"
"They’re directly connected to his Mana channels. If we break them wrong, he might die."
"Explain from the beginning." Then the student council president said.
Lian gathered everyone around the table.
Marcus and Cassian sat on both sides of Aren. Ethan stood, leaning his weapon against the wall.
Seraphina, Seris, and Liana were on the other side.
"The Forgotten Tree is drying up." He then began explaining the situation without introduction.
"The same tree mentioned in the Main Quest?" Rindo asked.
"Yeah."
Lian explained what Aren had told him in the cell, plus what he himself knew. The three girls already knew some of it, but the boys knew nothing.
The Forgotten Tree was not just a large tree or a sacred structure.
The water cycle of the three forests depended on it.
Its gradual drying had caused water levels to drop in the Forest of Giants, changed resources in Emberroot, and probably disrupted Glassthorn’s balance.
Then he explained about the Titan’s chains.
The Forgotten Tree’s power was connected to the structures that restrained the contaminated Titan. The weaker the tree became, the more the chains lost their power.
The Black Silence was not just a contaminated substance around or inside that creature.
It was a type of living disease or disaster that would spread throughout the entire world with the Titan’s complete awakening.
The same thing the System had threatened: if they failed the mission, it would enter their world...

chapters.title: Chapter 302: The Final Decision I
paragraphs: "So even if we didn’t kill those monsters, it would still wake up." Seris whispered.
"Yeah, we just fed it a little." Lian answered.
"Are you kidding?" Liana looked at him with frustration.
Selina had disappeared and there was no news of her.
A civilization was about to fall upon them while a tree that was very important was dying, and if they didn’t stop it, a disaster that could destroy the world would enter their world.
Was she the only one who understood the terrible depth of their situation? Why were Seris and Lian so calm?
They were practically in a situation that a few 18-year-old kids like them shouldn’t even be able to imagine!
The room’s space fell silent for a few moments. Of course, everyone knew how bad the situation was.
"Killing the monsters and spilling blood around it sped up the awakening process for a short time, but the main cause existed from before." In any case, Lian continued.
"The Forgotten Tree is dying, and until we understand why, the Titan will awaken sooner or later."
"Do the Cindari know about this?" Marcus asked.
"Yeah."
Lian explained that they had been moving their forces to the borders of the three forests for years.
The heavy deployment of soldiers at the Cindervein Passage, the increase in watchtowers, and the control of the paths between the forests were probably related to this issue.
"But that’s not all."
Lian looked at Aren.
"Those Cindari are looking for a way to enter the Ruined Realm."
"To attack?"
"To escape. This world is dying. The Cindari want to enter another world before its destruction and save themselves."
"So all this time they were looking for a way to escape from this world?" Marcus asked in disbelief.
"Yeah."
"And they probably kept us alive because they need Outsiders." Seraphina also whispered in disbelief.
"So from the beginning we weren’t guests, just tools." Ethan said angrily. He hadn’t liked those bastards from the start and knew they were definitely hiding something.
Rindo said nothing.
Among all the people in the room, this truth put the most pressure on him.
He had organized Ashfall Ward, negotiated with Maelor, accepted the city’s laws, and tried to prevent conflict between humans and Cindari.
When Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian were arrested, he had been forced to hand them over to save more than forty Awakeners.
All his decisions were based on the assumption that the Cindari were not their open enemies.
Maybe they were distrustful, maybe they didn’t treat them fairly, but Rindo had thought that as long as the humans followed the city’s laws, they would at least have temporary safety.
Now he realized that they might have never been accepted as a group of guests from the start.
They had gathered everyone in one area, allowed them to grow stronger.
Watched their movements.
And waited for them to find a way back to their world, so at the last moment they could betray them and use that path to go to their world.
"All this time they gathered us, watched us, and waited." Then he said bitterly.
"Wait... this means even they know they can’t stop the disaster... then how are we supposed to do it?" Liana reminded them of an important point.
And her words once again highlighted the severity of the situation.
"What should we do now?"
"We have two options." Lian looked at the city map. He placed his finger on the Vhalaris exit routes.
"First, everyone leaves the city right now and heads toward the Forgotten Tree."
"With our current numbers, that’s not possible." Rindo said without delay. Their numbers weren’t small, and besides the monsters roaming the forest, they would also have to escape from the Cindari.
Running and fighting the Cindari in the forest would be very difficult. Emberroot was practically their home, and they had a significant environmental advantage.
Rindo picked up the list of people to give a fuller explanation of what he meant.
"More than forty people are inside Ashfall. Several hunting groups are still outside the city."
"We have eleven wounded. Some people haven’t even reached Level 17." He tapped the list with his finger.
"If we move now, the group’s order will fall apart. The faster people will go ahead, and the weaker ones will fall behind."
"The Cindari know the paths better than we do. They’ll surround us from several directions and pick the group apart piece by piece."
"The city gates are also closed." Seraphina added another important point.
Rindo nodded.
"Even reaching the outside of the city would be a war in itself."
"So only one option remains." Lian said. He had expected this. His gaze fixed on the Ashfall map.
"We turn this place into our own fortress."
For a few seconds, no one said anything. As if they had some trouble understanding his words.
"We take over the entire city?" Seraphina asked to make sure she hadn’t misunderstood.
"No."
Lian pointed to the borders of Ashfall Ward. This section of the city was connected to the rest of Vhalaris by three main bridges, two narrow paths, and several high platforms.
The old design of the neighborhood made it possible to defend it with fewer forces than other areas.
"For now, just this section."
"I see. This place has limited gates and bridges." Cassian looked carefully at the map.
"The tall buildings around the square are also good for archers. If we want to build a fortress, it’s not hard." Marcus added.
"Taking a region is different from defending it." Rindo was still not convinced.
"First we clear the city’s military forces. We take the entrances, towers, and main paths. Then we turn Ashfall into our headquarters." Lian completed his explanation.
Of course, they would still have to clear the city of any threats.
"And what do we do with the Cindari who live here?" Seraphina asked.
"Ordinary people who don’t resist stay. Soldiers and commanders are naturally a different matter."
"Alive or dead?" Ethan smiled.
"That depends on them." Lian glanced briefly at him.
Rindo didn’t immediately object upon hearing the answer, but his expression grew harder.
He couldn’t allow the Awakeners to massacre all the Cindari in the area as soon as the conflict started.
Not only for ethical reasons, but also militarily, it would be a foolish move.
"Is it even possible?" Cassian asked. He still didn’t see this as simple. The number of enemies was greater than theirs.
"It depends on how many commanders are in the city. So far, the strongest people I’ve seen were around Level 30." Lian thought about the information he had gathered from recent battles.
"And how many like them are there?" Rindo looked at him.
"I don’t know."
"Great."
"Defeating all of them alone is a bit hard for me." Lian continued without paying attention to his sarcasm. Then he looked at Seris, Seraphina, and Liana.
"But with the help of those three, it should be possible."
Seris smiled slightly. Seraphina unstrapped her sword from her waist and placed it on the table.
Liana crossed her arms over her chest.
"I’m still angry at you, but whenever you need help, I’ll always help."
"And those three are also there." Lian pointed to Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian.
"I don’t need to be convinced for this part." Ethan laughed with pleasure.
"My shoulder isn’t fully healed yet, but I can fight." Marcus said.
Cassian was quieter, but whenever his team needed help, he was ready to give it, even if it meant his life.
"We have dozens of other Awakeners too." Lian smiled and looked at the buildings of Ashfall.
"After we take the area, what then?" Rindo asked. He was convinced they had no other choice. In any case, conflict was imminent.
"Then I, Seris, and Aren will head toward the Forgotten Tree." Lian answered quietly.
The plan was complete in his view. Besides, when he reached Level 20 and went through his first evolution, he doubted the Cindari would even be considered a threat anymore.
"Why just you and Seris?" Seraphina asked immediately.
"Because you need to stay here."
"Who decided that?" Seraphina’s eyebrows furrowed.
"I did."
For a moment, the pressure in the room increased, and Seraphina stepped toward Lian.
"You think because you broke out of a prison, you can make decisions for everyone now?"
"If I take all the main forces with me, Ashfall won’t last a single day." Lian answered without backing down.
Seraphina said nothing.
"You, Liana, Marcus, Ethan, Cassian, and Rindo need to stay here." He continued.
"If the Cindari take back the neighborhood, they’ll arrest or kill all the weaker Awakeners."
Then he pointed to Seris.
"Seris has seen the Titan and knows what we’re facing."
Then he looked at Aren.
"Aren also knows the information and the old paths، I have the map. The three of us will move faster."

"We take over the entire city?" Seraphina asked to make sure she hadn’t misunderstood.
"No."
Lian pointed to the borders of Ashfall Ward.
This section of the city was connected to the rest of Vhalaris by three main bridges, two narrow paths, and several high platforms.
The old design of the neighborhood made it possible to defend it with fewer forces than other areas.
"For now, just this section."
"I see.
This place has limited gates and bridges." Cassian looked carefully at the map.
"The tall buildings around the square are also good for archers.
If we want to build a fortress, it’s not hard." Marcus added.
"Taking a region is different from defending it." Rindo was still not convinced.
"First we clear the city’s military forces.
We take the entrances, towers, and main paths.
Then we turn Ashfall into our headquarters." Lian completed his explanation.
Of course, they would still have to clear the city of any threats.
"And what do we do with the Cindari who live here?" Seraphina asked.
"Ordinary people who don’t resist stay.
Soldiers and commanders are naturally a different matter."
"Alive or dead?" Ethan smiled.
"That depends on them." Lian glanced briefly at him.
Rindo didn’t immediately object upon hearing the answer, but his expression grew harder.
He couldn’t allow the Awakeners to massacre all the Cindari in the area as soon as the conflict started.
Not only for ethical reasons, but also militarily, it would be a foolish move.
"Is it even possible?" Cassian asked.
He still didn’t see this as simple.
The number of enemies was greater than theirs.
"It depends on how many commanders are in the city.
So far, the strongest people I’ve seen were around Level 30." Lian thought about the information he had gathered from recent battles.
"And how many like them are there?" Rindo looked at him.
"I don’t know."
"Great."
"Defeating all of them alone is a bit hard for me." Lian continued without paying attention to his sarcasm.
Then he looked at Seris, Seraphina, and Liana.
"But with the help of those three, it should be possible."
Seris smiled slightly.
Seraphina unstrapped her sword from her waist and placed it on the table.
Liana crossed her arms over her chest.
"I’m still angry at you, but whenever you need help, I’ll always help."
"And those three are also there." Lian pointed to Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian.
"I don’t need to be convinced for this part." Ethan laughed with pleasure.
"My shoulder isn’t fully healed yet, but I can fight." Marcus said.
Cassian was quieter, but whenever his team needed help, he was ready to give it, even if it meant his life.
"We have dozens of other Awakeners too." Lian smiled and looked at the buildings of Ashfall.
"After we take the area, what then?" Rindo asked.
He was convinced they had no other choice.
In any case, conflict was imminent.
"Then I, Seris, and Aren will head toward the Forgotten Tree." Lian answered quietly.
The plan was complete in his view.
Besides, when he reached Level 20 and went through his first evolution, he doubted the Cindari would even be considered a threat anymore.
"Why just you and Seris?" Seraphina asked immediately.
"Because you need to stay here."
"Who decided that?" Seraphina’s eyebrows furrowed.
"I did."
For a moment, the pressure in the room increased, and Seraphina stepped toward Lian.
"You think because you broke out of a prison, you can make decisions for everyone now?"
"If I take all the main forces with me, Ashfall won’t last a single day." Lian answered without backing down.
Seraphina said nothing.
"You, Liana, Marcus, Ethan, Cassian, and Rindo need to stay here." He continued.
"If the Cindari take back the neighborhood, they’ll arrest or kill all the weaker Awakeners."
Then he pointed to Seris.
"Seris has seen the Titan and knows what we’re facing."
Then he looked at Aren.
"Aren also knows the information and the old paths، I have the map.
The three of us will move faster."

chapters.title: Chapter 303: The Final Decision II
paragraphs: Seraphina was still dissatisfied.
"We’ll discuss it later." Lian finally said.
"I have no problem." Seris said quietly.
"Of course you don’t." Liana looked at her.
"The mission is dangerous, that’s why I have no problem, and it’s no place for children." Seris gave a short smile. This was the first time everyone could see her self-satisfied smile.
And that was enough to make Liana and Seraphina feel like exploding with anger.
"First, we need to hold Ashfall." Rindo placed his hand on the table. He looked at the district’s map again.
"Escape with the current population is almost impossible. If we can really hold this section, we’ll buy time to organize the groups and gather resources."
"And when forces from other Cindari cities arrive?" Cassian asked.
Rindo was silent for a moment. This was the biggest problem.
They might be able to defeat Vhalaris’s current forces, but they knew nothing about the number of other cities, their distance, or the strength of their armies.

"We don’t know how far the other cities are, but no matter how close they are, moving an army takes time. We only need a few days to reach the Forgotten Tree and find out what’s happening to it." Lian said instead.
"If we take Vhalaris, other Cindari will attack immediately." Cassian said.
"We don’t need to kill everyone. Only kill when necessary. Soldiers who surrender will be imprisoned. Commanders and high-ranking individuals will be kept alive." Rindo finally made his decision.
"Hostages." Marcus immediately understood the reason.
"Prisoners of war." The student council president nodded, his gaze still on the map.
"If other cities send forces, we can use Vhalaris’s commanders to buy time."
"They might not attack directly if Maelor or their other important people are in our hands."
"At least they’ll be forced to negotiate, or move slower." Cassian said.
"Those few days could make a big difference." Rindo nodded.
"It’s a good idea." Lian said. He also found no problem with it.
"Are you sure you can defeat them?" Then the student council president looked at him.
"As I said, alone it’s hard, but with the help of all of you and the other awakened ones, defeating the Cindari shouldn’t be a problem."
"Then everyone needs to know what they’re fighting for." Rindo took a deep breath.
He came out from behind the table and said to one of the temporary council members waiting outside the door.
"Gather all the Awakeners inside Ashfall in the central square."
"Everyone?" the man asked.
"Everyone. Hunters, wounded who can walk, guards, and support groups. No one should be left out."
The man nodded and quickly left. A few moments later, a different bell from the Cindari alarms rang in Ashfall Ward.
This bell was made by the humans themselves for gatherings and warnings. The sound echoed through the old buildings, and the doors of the residences opened.
The Awakeners came out of the medical center, warehouses, resting places, and watchtowers.
Some had not yet put on full armor. Some were fastening their weapons while running.
A few had bandages on their arms, heads, or legs.
The Main Quest had just appeared for everyone, and most of them still didn’t know what it meant.
They only knew the System had warned about the awakening of a Corrupted Titan and The Black Silence entering Earth.
In less than ten minutes, the central square was full. More than forty Awakeners gathered in front of the council platform.
The archers were on one side, the Warriors and Tanks on the other, and the Mages, Healers, and support groups in the back.
Rindo stood on the wooden platform.
Lian, Seraphina, Seris, Liana, Marcus, Ethan, Cassian, and Aren stood behind him.
Aren’s appearance immediately drew everyone’s attention.
A human man with gray hair and chains engraved with Cindari markings.
Murmurs began among the crowd.
"Who is he?"
"Was he brought from the prison?"
"Marcus and the others were really freed? What happened?"
Rindo raised his hand, and the murmurs gradually died down.
"Most of you have received the Main Quest."
No one answered, but their expressions confirmed it.
"Until a few minutes ago, we didn’t have complete information either." He pointed at Aren.
"This man is Aren. One of the humans who entered this Special Area in the previous Cycle, and as you might guess, he is a native of the Ruined Realm."
A new murmur formed.
Natives of the Ruined Realm were a surprise for everyone, and a previous Cycle? That even increased the shock and surprise among everyone.
Rindo let it continue for a few seconds and then said.
"The information we obtained from him and our own group’s investigations has clarified the true situation of this world." His tone became heavier.
"The Forgotten Tree is dying. The tree that is like the heart of this world."
"The water cycle of the three forests depends on it, and as the tree dries, the chains of the Corrupted Titan weaken. A very powerful giant that carries a type of disaster called The Black Silence."
"And if the Titan fully awakens, The Black Silence will contaminate this entire world."
"According to the Main Quest, after that, it will gain access to Earth. Anyone contaminated by The Black Silence, simply put, turns into a bloodthirsty zombie."
This time, complete silence fell. Even the Awakeners who had been listening with indifference until that moment changed their expressions.
"So the Main Quest is what you’re talking about?" a young man from the crowd asked.
"Yes. Our goal is to prevent the Corrupted Titan from awakening." Rindo answered.
"How?" a female archer in the second row asked.
"A group will be sent to the Forgotten Tree. They need to find out why the tree is drying and how to stop it."
"The Cindari have known about this disaster for a long time."
"They gathered us in Ashfall, monitored our movements, and were probably waiting for us to find a way out so they could also leave their own world."
"So they were using us?" one of the Awakeners shouted.
Anger grew among the crowd. Some Awakeners had never trusted the Cindari from the start.
Some had only accepted the rules for the group’s safety and Rindo’s decision.
Now hearing that they were being used as tools turned previous doubts into anger.
"You have two choices. You can stay with us and defend Ashfall Ward, or you can leave the city alone. No one is forced to fight."
A murmur arose among the crowd.
"The city’s army is much larger than ours."
"But if we escape alone, they’ll hunt us down in the forest.
The fear was real. They were not soldiers of an organized army.
They were a group of Awakeners who had gathered in Ashfall from different parts of the Special Area.
Some still had nightmares about seeing their comrades’ bodies in the forest.
A tall hunter stepped forward from the front row.
He was one of the people Rindo had sent forces to save a few days ago.
"I’ll stay." He raised his axe.
A few people looked at him, and he continued.
"If we escape the city, they’ll tear us apart in the forest. Here at least we have walls and forces."
"Those Cindari bastards have been trying to use us all this time." another person said.
"Why should we give Ashfall back to them?"
"Finally, someone understands." Ethan said with satisfaction.
"Don’t provoke them." Cassian looked at him.
"They’re already provoked enough."
A few more people raised their weapons.
"I’ll stay too."
"We’ll help."
"If the Titan enters Earth, there’s nowhere to run."
"I’m not a good fighter, but I can build Barriers." the female Mage who worked by the medical center said.
"I’ll treat the wounded." one of the Healers said.
Gradually, more voices of agreement were heard. The fear didn’t disappear, but anger, necessity, and the lack of a sure escape route made most of them decide to stay.
In the end, a large group of Awakeners raised their weapons.
"We won’t give Ashfall back to them!"
"Those Cindari bastards need to learn a lesson!" another person shouted.
The crowd’s voice echoed in the square. Rindo let out a quiet sigh of relief.
For a moment, the pressure on his shoulders lessened, but he didn’t let the crowd’s excitement turn into chaos, and he raised his voice.
"Everyone, arm yourselves and be ready."
The crowd fell silent.
"Warriors and Tanks will position themselves near the main entrances."
"Archers and Mages will take positions on the tall buildings."
"The wounded and support personnel will move to the central buildings."
"Healers will distribute the Potions, but no one is to use extra without orders."
Lian watched all these scenes calmly. The student council president of their academy was better at organizing and leading people than he had expected.
Much, much better.
In this short time, he had managed to gain the trust of the majority of the Awakeners present.
This man could be much more useful than he appeared...

chapters.title: Chapter 304: Humans Are Surrounded!
paragraphs: "All exit routes, basements, and secondary bridges must be checked."
"No one attacks without orders."
"Our goal is not to kill all the Cindari."
"Soldiers who surrender will be taken as prisoners."
"Only kill when necessary to protect yourselves or others."
"I didn’t like the last part, it would have been better to kill all of them," Ethan said under his breath.
"That’s why you’re not the commander," Marcus answered.
"The conflict could start at any moment, so from now on, Ashfall Ward is the humans’ defensive zone," Rindo continued.
The Awakeners scattered.
Some went toward the warehouses.
Some put on their full armor.
Groups positioned themselves at the entrances, and movement began on the rooftops.
Ashfall no longer looked like a temporary shelter.
Warriors placed boxes and metal plates as barriers on the bridges.
Mages marked suitable positions for using long-range Skills.
Summoners called their creatures near the entrances.
Healers prepared the central medical center.
The humans who had been monitored guests of Vhalaris until that moment were turning the district into their own fortress.
Rindo came down from the platform and returned to the council building.
When he entered the room, Lian, Seraphina, Seris, Liana, Marcus, Ethan, Cassian, and Aren were gathered around the table again.
"Everything is ready."
But before he could continue, the sound of Vhalaris’s alarms changed.
This time, the warning tone was shorter and harsher.
The red veins around Ashfall Ward lit up with more intensity.
From outside, the sound of bridges closing and defensive structures moving was heard.
Then the sound of footsteps began.
Not the sound of a few soldiers, but the sound of hundreds of armored feet moving on the bridges and surrounding streets.
One of the human guards rushed into the building, his breathing heavily elevated.
"President!"
"What happened?" Rindo turned toward him.
"All the district’s entrances are surrounded."
"They have placed forces on all three bridges, archers are on the towers, and they have brought two Ballistas facing the main entrance," the man continued.
"Of course they did," Rindo closed his eyes for a moment.
"They organized a siege this fast?" Lian moved away from the table.
"You beat their prison head and destroyed the Rootspire prison, a quick reaction is not strange," Cassian said.
"Finally, the interesting part begins," Ethan also smiled.
Seraphina fastened her sword to her waist, Liana summoned Shadow Wolf, and Seris went toward the door without a word.
The entire group left the council building.
The central square of Ashfall was no longer calm.
The Awakeners were taking formation according to Rindo’s orders.
Warriors and Tanks were behind the entrance barriers, archers were kneeling on the rooftops with arrows ready.
Mages stood at specific distances from each other so their Skills wouldn’t interfere.
Summoners kept their creatures in the alleys and beside the walls.
Healers prepared the central medical center.
On the other side of Ashfall’s border, the Cindari army could be seen.
The front line was made up of Rootbound Wardens.
Their black and gold armors shone under the red veins’ light.
Their tall shields covered almost the entire width of the main bridge.
Spearmen were behind them, archers were stationed on high platforms and surrounding buildings.
Two large Ballistas were placed on the main bridge.
Thick Mana bolts were forming inside their bodies, aimed directly at Ashfall’s inner square.
The Cindari forces had not come from only one side.
All three main entrances of the district were surrounded.
Even the narrow upper paths were under the soldiers’ control.
In the center of the army, Kael stood.
This time, he was not wearing light commander’s clothes or simple border armor.
Full battle armor covered his body.
Black and red plates were on his chest, shoulders, and legs, and his racial veins flowed throughout them.
The Ember Vanguard spear was in his right hand, a compressed and calm flame moving on its tip.
The veins on his face and neck were lit with intense light.
Anger was clear in his posture.
But behind that anger, something heavier also existed.
Disappointment.
In less than a day, he had brought Lian into Vhalaris as a guest.
Then he had been forced to fight him on the Rootspire bridge.
Now that same human had escaped from prison, freed the accused murderers and infiltrators, and fortified himself with dozens of Awakeners in Ashfall.
Kael struck his spear on the ground.
A wave of heat spread across the bridge.
His voice was amplified with Mana and heard throughout Ashfall Ward.
"Lian!"
All eyes turned toward Lian.
He calmly walked through the line of Awakeners and stood in front of the main entrance.
Seraphina, Seris, and Liana stood a few steps behind him.
Rindo came to the other side.
Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian were also ready.
Aren remained near the council building due to his weak body, but watched the scene from a distance.
He couldn’t help, so it was better if he didn’t cause trouble.
"You broke Vhalaris’s laws once," Kael fixed his gaze directly on Lian, and his voice echoed among the buildings.
"You attacked military zones, wounded our soldiers, and violated the Rootspire’s security."
The veins on his armor became brighter.
"But now you have attacked the Rootspire for a second time, freed military and classified prisoners."
"You destroyed the lowest part of the prison and killed many soldiers!"
The soldiers behind him gripped their weapons tighter, angry and furious that their comrades had been killed.
Lian said nothing for a few seconds.
During the escape, he had deliberately tried not to kill anyone.
But the battle was brutal.
In such a battle, it was normal for his enemies to be killed... so what was he supposed to do?
Wait for them to kill him? Of course not.
He had only defended himself.
"Aren’t you the border commander?" He then looked at Kael’s full armor and asked calmly.
Kael frowned, not understanding where this human was going with this question.
"Why haven’t you gone back to the border?"
"Are you forced to interfere in everyone else’s business?"
"Or is it that the city is short on soldiers, so they keep sending you?" Lian then added with sarcasm.

Two large Ballistas were placed on the main bridge.
Thick Mana bolts were forming inside their bodies, aimed directly at Ashfall’s inner square.
The Cindari forces had not come from only one side.
All three main entrances of the district were surrounded.
Even the narrow upper paths were under the soldiers’ control.
In the center of the army, Kael stood.
This time, he was not wearing light commander’s clothes or simple border armor.
Full battle armor covered his body.
Black and red plates were on his chest, shoulders, and legs, and his racial veins flowed throughout them.
The Ember Vanguard spear was in his right hand, a compressed and calm flame moving on its tip.
The veins on his face and neck were lit with intense light.
Anger was clear in his posture.
But behind that anger, something heavier also existed.
Disappointment.
In less than a day, he had brought Lian into Vhalaris as a guest.
Then he had been forced to fight him on the Rootspire bridge.
Now that same human had escaped from prison, freed the accused murderers and infiltrators, and fortified himself with dozens of Awakeners in Ashfall.
Kael struck his spear on the ground.
A wave of heat spread across the bridge.
His voice was amplified with Mana and heard throughout Ashfall Ward.
"Lian!"
All eyes turned toward Lian.
He calmly walked through the line of Awakeners and stood in front of the main entrance.
Seraphina, Seris, and Liana stood a few steps behind him.
Rindo came to the other side.
Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian were also ready.
Aren remained near the council building due to his weak body, but watched the scene from a distance.
He couldn’t help, so it was better if he didn’t cause trouble.
"You broke Vhalaris’s laws once," Kael fixed his gaze directly on Lian, and his voice echoed among the buildings.
"You attacked military zones, wounded our soldiers, and violated the Rootspire’s security."
The veins on his armor became brighter.
"But now you have attacked the Rootspire for a second time, freed military and classified prisoners."
"You destroyed the lowest part of the prison and killed many soldiers!"
The soldiers behind him gripped their weapons tighter, angry and furious that their comrades had been killed.
Lian said nothing for a few seconds.
During the escape, he had deliberately tried not to kill anyone.
But the battle was brutal.
In such a battle, it was normal for his enemies to be killed... so what was he supposed to do?
Wait for them to kill him?
Of course not.
He had only defended himself.
"Aren’t you the border commander?" He then looked at Kael’s full armor and asked calmly.
Kael frowned, not understanding where this human was going with this question.
"Why haven’t you gone back to the border?"
"Are you forced to interfere in everyone else’s business?"
"Or is it that the city is short on soldiers, so they keep sending you?" Lian then added with sarcasm.

chapters.title: Chapter 305: Battle With The Cindari Army I
paragraphs: With the echoing of Lian’s words, for a moment, a strange silence fell over the main bridge of Ashfall Ward.
Hundreds of Cindari soldiers stood on the other side of the barriers.

The tall shields of the Rootbound Wardens covered the entire width of the bridge. The tips of spears could be seen through the gaps in the defensive formation, and the archers stationed on the towers had their drawn strings aimed at Ashfall’s inner square.
Two massive Ballistas were also placed on the bridge’s central platform.
Thick Mana bolts were slowly forming inside their bodies, and their red tips were aimed directly at the gathering of Awakeners.
In front of them, Kael stood in full battle armor.
Lian’s question was neither loud nor said with anger, but the calmness in his voice made it more contemptuous than any insult.
As if hundreds of soldiers, three surrounded paths, and two Ballistas meant nothing.
As if Kael was just a commander who had forgotten his duty and returned late to his post.
His fingers tightened around the spear’s shaft, and a thin flame moved on the weapon’s tip.
"Because from the moment you entered this city, the real threat was no longer behind the border." His voice was amplified with Mana and echoed throughout Ashfall Ward.
Upon hearing the commander’s answer, the Cindari soldiers placed their shields more firmly on the ground.
The sound of spear butts hitting the pavement rose from three sides of the district.
The archers on the towers adjusted their arrows’ angles.

Behind Lian, the Awakeners also prepared themselves. More than forty people were stationed in the square and at Ashfall’s entrances, but only a few of them could directly resist the Rootbound Wardens.
Some had still not reached Level 15. Some had fresh wounds.
The number of Healers was limited, and most of the Potions had been stored for a possible escape or the Forgotten Tree mission.
If the battle turned into a prolonged war, the Cindari’s numerical and equipment advantage would gradually show itself.
Lian took his gaze off Kael and examined the field. The three main bridges were closed, the surrounding towers were under enemy control.
Archers, Mages, and Ballistas could deal heavy damage to the weaker Awakeners in the first few minutes.
It was not enough to defeat Kael to win.
He had to break the Cindari’s defensive line so quickly that their army would lose morale and command before a war of attrition could begin.
’It’s not hard. Better if I intervene first and after disrupting their order and organization, the other Awakeners can join in.’ He thought to himself.
If the Awakeners joined in from the start, their casualties would be high, and that was not something he wanted. He preferred to keep their casualties as low as possible.
It would be even better if they suffered no casualties at all.
Then Lian opened the Status panel before his eyes.
[Available Stat Points: 137]
He had obtained all his current stats points from killing monsters in the border passage between the two forests, and the rest from killing the Cindari.
He hadn’t needed to use them during this time, but for the current situation, the stronger he was, the better.
[Power: 693]
[Spirit: 450]
[Speed: 465]
[Mana: 965]
[Resistance: 508]
His gaze moved over the numbers for a moment.
His Mana was higher than all his other Stats.
Spirit was also at an acceptable level.
But the upcoming battle required raw power, explosive speed, and resistance against hundreds of attacks. Without hesitation, he chose to distribute the points.
[Power +67]
[Speed +35]
[Mana +10]
[Resistance +25]
[Confirm Allocation?]
Lian confirmed.
[Allocation Confirmed.]
A hot wave rose from the center of his body.
In the first moment, he felt the blood in his veins become heavier. Then the pressure was transferred to his muscles, bones, and joints.
The new power spread through his entire body like invisible energy. The muscles in his shoulders and arms contracted slightly.
His bones made a quiet sound for a moment and then settled more firmly than before.
The Mana flow in his channels became faster.
[Physical Strength: 760]
[Spirit: 450]
[Speed: 500]
[Mana: 975]
[Resistance: 533]
[Available Stat Points: 0]
’I can feel the wall again.’ For a moment he frowned. After increasing his stats, for a moment he could feel the existence of a wall.
The wall was getting closer and closer, nearer to him than ever.
’If my guess is correct, my limit is 4000 stats.’ Currently, the total of all his stats was over 3000.
And since he was finally feeling the limit and the wall, his guess was that his limit could be 4000 stats.
This number was insane. A five-star class awakened one’s limit was 2000 stats, but him? Twice that!
The pressure coming from Lian’s body had suddenly become heavier.
Not like the release of a Skill, not like a temporary power increase with a Potion, but as if his body had truly become stronger in the span of a few seconds.
Kael didn’t know how this change had happened, but his pride wouldn’t allow doubt to show on his face.
He pointed his spear at Lian.
"Lian, put down your weapon."
Then he took his gaze off him and fixed it on the Awakeners behind him.
"Hand over Marcus, Ethan, Cassian, and the classified prisoner."
Aren was leaning against the wall near the council building. The heavy chains were still around his body, and Marcus stood beside him to keep his balance in case of weakness.
"The rest of the Outsiders will not be punished if they surrender. This is your last chance. Hand over your weapons and surrender." It was clear their policy toward humans had changed.
They could no longer allow dangerous variables like humans to have weapons, and they had to disarm them by any means.
"You think we’re fools? Or do you think we’re afraid of that army behind you?" Lian stepped forward.
At that same moment, several archers lowered their arrows slightly, aiming directly at his chest.
Kael furrowed his brows.
"We will not surrender, and we will not hand over anyone." His gaze moved over the first line of soldiers.
"But about you Cindari, soldiers who put down their weapons will live."
A few of the Rootbound Wardens looked at each other for a moment.
Not because they were thinking of surrendering, but from sheer disbelief. They had surrounded Ashfall from three directions.
Their numbers were several times greater than the humans.
The Ballistas, towers, and the city’s defensive lines were also under their control.
But Lian spoke as if this army should beg him for mercy to survive.
"You are surrounded. You have neither numerical advantage nor environmental advantage. What makes you so delusional?" For a moment, Kael thought he was deliberately trying to provoke him.
"Numbers and environment aren’t always important. One against a dragon, hundreds of thousands of ants can’t do anything." Lian answered with the same calmness.
"What dragon?" The veins on Kael’s face became brighter. He didn’t know what a dragon was, but he felt they were being insulted.
"In your dictionary, its synonym is the contaminated Titan."
The commander’s face turned ugly. Now he understood that they were really being mocked! He lowered his spear.
"Fire!"
The sound of the Ballista locks being released rose from both sides of the bridge at the same time. The gathered Mana inside the machines was released with a red explosion.
Two massive bolts were fired from the platforms.
Each of them was taller than a human’s body and thicker than a mature tree trunk. Their surfaces were covered with compressed Mana veins, and the air around them burned in their path.
The target of both was not the first line of Awakeners.
They were moving directly toward Ashfall’s central square; where the Mages, wounded, and support forces were gathered.
"Barrier!" Rindo shouted.
The Mages raised their hands.
Several layers of Mana began to form in front of the square.
But the Barrier was not yet complete when blue lightning exploded among the human lines.
[Thunder Step]
Lian disappeared. A moment later, he appeared in front of the first Ballista bolt.
His feet were in the air, and the massive bolt was coming toward him with deadly speed.
[Thunder Calamity]
A deep roar rose from inside his body. Lightning spread from his right shoulder to his fingertips.
Thick veins of blue and white lightning twisted around his arm. The air around his fist trembled from the intensity of the energy, and the sound of thunder covered the city’s alarms for a moment.
Lian thrust his fist forward. His strike hit the bolt’s tip. The explosion of thunder and his fist lit up the sky above the bridge.
The impact wave reached the surrounding buildings and shook the nearby windows.
The bolt stopped in the air for a moment, then a thin crack started from its tip and continued to the end of its body.
Lightning entered the entire structure. The massive bolt exploded from the center and turned into hundreds of burned and molten pieces.
The Awakeners behind Lian only felt a warm wave pass over the incomplete Barrier.
But the second bolt was still approaching.
Before the pieces of the first bolt could fall to the ground, Lian activated Thunder Step again.
Blue light split in the air. He appeared on one of the wooden barriers at the main entrance.
He planted his left foot firmly on the surface and pulled his left fist back. This time, the lightning passed from his side and chest and gathered on his left hand.
The second strike hit the bolt’s body.
The explosion sound was even more intense than the first impact. The Ballista bolt bent in the middle.
Then the compressed energy inside it was released, and a wave of flame and lightning scattered around.
The Cindari soldiers raised their shields for a moment. Even Kael unconsciously stepped back.
Two weapons built to break city walls and kill massive War Beasts had been destroyed with bare fists.
All the Cindari unconsciously swallowed their saliva. It wasn’t just them; even the Awakeners were shocked and amazed...
What had they just witnessed?
A brief silence fell over the field. Lian landed on the ground. Lightning was still moving between his fingers, and his gaze was directly fixed on Kael.
"Now it’s my turn."

chapters.title: Chapter 306: Battle With The Cindari Army II
paragraphs: Lian started moving. At first his steps were slow, but with each step his speed increased.
The first row of Rootbound Wardens reacted immediately.
They placed their tall shields next to each other.
The ends of the shields locked into the stone floor and golden lines spread from one to another.
The commander of the row raised his sword.
"Rootwall formation!"
More than twenty soldiers released Mana at the same time. Golden light connected all the shields to each other.
For a moment, the row of soldiers was no longer a group of individuals. It became one solid wall.
Golden roots came out from under the shields and went into the stone floor of the bridge. Any hit that landed on one point would be split among all members of the formation.
This structure was built to stop high-level War Beasts and monsters that could break the city gates with a direct attack.
But unfortunately, they did not know that they were facing something more dangerous than any monster they had ever seen.
Lian did not slow down.
[Iron Fortress Charge.]
A dense gray pressure formed around his body.
His skin, muscles and bones became hard like the body of a moving fortress.
Then he released Thunder Calamity on that same structure. Lightning spread over his shoulders, arms and legs.
Lian’s body disappeared among blue light and gray pressure. His last step crushed the stone under his foot, and then he hit the center of Rootwall.
The sound of the explosion shook the whole bridge. A circular wave spread from the point of impact and sent dust, stone pieces and golden sparks into the air.
Rootwall lasted less than a second. The central shield bent in the middle.
The Rootbound Warden behind it did not even have time to scream. His body left the ground and crashed into three soldiers behind him.
Lightning transferred from the central shield to the side shields. The soldiers’ hands went numb. Some lost control of their Mana.
The golden roots connected to the ground tore one after another. The force of Iron Fortress Charge passed through the center of the formation.
The defensive line opened from the middle, like a wall broken by a huge hammer. The soldiers on both sides of the gap were thrown back in fear.
The shield that they had worked so hard to form, fell apart so easily.
Lian passed through them without stopping. The first spear came from the left toward his neck.
Predator’s Instincts sent the danger to his body before the blade reached halfway. A raw and instinctive feeling that showed the direction of death.
Lian moved his head a few centimeters to the side. The blade passed by his face and his right hand grabbed the spear’s shaft.
Thunder Calamity went from his palm into the weapon.
Electricity moved along the shaft and reached the soldier’s arms. The whole body of the Rootbound Warden shook.
His eyes went white for a moment and he fell to the ground without being killed.
Three soldiers charged at Lian from behind. He pulled his arm up and both soldiers lifted off the ground.
Their armored bodies spun in the air and crashed into the third one.
All three fell on top of each other.
Another Rootbound Warden with a heavy axe came from the right. The axe blade was covered in Mana.
The man brought the strike down with all his weight.
[Diamond Skin.]
Lian’s skin became hard. The axe hit his arm and the sound of metal hitting something harder than stone rose.
The blade only made a shallow scratch.
The Warden looked at his weapon in disbelief. He had just felt like he hit the hardest thing he had ever seen.
And that hesitation was enough. Lian’s thunderous fist hit the center of his chest.
The armor caved in and the soldier’s body was thrown back several meters, knocking two more soldiers to the ground with him.
The archers on the towers got the order to shoot. Dozens of Mana arrows moved toward Lian from three angles.
Predator’s Instincts warned him with a constant pressure all over his body.
Lian did not even look up.
[Thunder Step.]
Blue lightning exploded among the arrows. All the arrows passed through his previous location and hit the stone floor of the bridge.
He appeared on the platform of the first Ballista. The three Cindari crew members were still preparing the next arrow.
None of them had time to react. Lian placed his palm on the body of the device.
[Cataclysm Pulse.]
A compressed and invisible wave entered the Ballista’s structure. At first nothing was seen, but then thin lines formed on all the metal plates.
A moment later, the device exploded from the inside.
Gears, plates, and the Mana chamber were thrown in all directions.
The Ballista crew fell to the ground from the blast wave, but Lian had controlled the Skill’s intensity so it would not tear their bodies apart directly.
He caught one of the large curved plates of the device in the air. He held the plate in front of his body and moved from the platform toward the archer tower.
Arrows hit the temporary shield one after another. The metal cracked under the pressure, but Lian kept moving forward.
"My god, he really is a monster!" The Awakeners did not know if they should be happy or terrified.
They did not know that among them there was such a monster who was pushing back the entire Cindari army all by himself.
All their defensive lines were falling one by one, and he alone had changed the whole flow of the battle.
The motivation and confidence among all the Awakeners increased and cheers grew louder.
"Haha, with a fighter like this, we have nothing to fear!"
"We will be the final victors!"
Rindo also looked more relieved seeing Lian’s real power. The worries he had were slowly disappearing.
Of course, as much as they had become happy and relieved, their enemies had become more scared and their faces more ugly. Now they understood where that human’s arrogance came from.
He really was powerful! So powerful that he could go head to head with all of them!
At the same time, the rest of the Awakeners also entered the battle.
Seris moved from the right side of the bridge. Her sword spun among the Rootbound Wardens with cold and precise speed.
Each strike could target the neck or heart of the soldiers, but she changed the sword’s path according to Rindo’s decision.
Knees.
Wrists.
Shoulders.
And weapons.
Every Cindari that faced her lost the ability to continue fighting in less than a few seconds.
Seraphina stood in the center of the human line. Prismatic light moved on her blade.
Every time an arrow or ranged Skill came toward weaker Awakeners, she moved her sword.
Transparent and colorful layers formed in the air and changed the arrows’ path.
Some hit the ground. Some hit empty walls. And some returned toward the Cindari shields.
Liana had sent Shadow Wolf into the bridge’s shadow.
The huge wolf disappeared into the darkness of the floor and came out a few meters away from another soldier’s shadow.
Archers who thought they were safe at height suddenly saw black claws on their chest and shoulders.
Shadow Wolf did not kill them. It threw them to the ground with a heavy strike and crushed their weapons.
Marcus kept the Ashfall defensive line.
His injured shoulder did not move fully, but he still pushed back every soldier that came through the gaps with his shield and sword.
Cassian moved among the buildings and the edge of the square. He did not go into the most crowded part of the battle.
He found small commanders, message carriers, and Mages who were trying to keep the army’s formation together.
Every time one of them gave a new order, a sword from a blind spot hit their hand, foot, or shoulder.
But despite the presence of all of them, the real center of the field was Lian. Wherever the soldiers formed a dense line again, he went in.
Wherever a Barrier formed, Cataclysm Pulse broke it from the inside.
Wherever a commander tried to reorganize the soldiers, Thunder Calamity’s fist took him out of the field.
The Cindari still had the advantage in numbers, but they could not gather their main force at one point.
Because wherever Lian reached, it collapsed in a few seconds.
Seven Fire Mages gathered on the left side of the bridge. Their red robes flared up with Mana.
They raised their hands at the same time and threads of fire connected through their fingers to each other.
They had decided to eliminate the biggest threat at any cost! They had to kill that damned human!
[Sevenfold Ember Prison.]
Seven pillars of fire rose from the ground around Lian. The flames changed direction with his movement.
Every time he stepped toward one of the gaps, two pillars moved close together and blocked the path.
The heat increased quickly. The air inside the fiery prison became heavy.
Lian’s burnt armor started smoking again. He moved once to the right.
The flames blocked the path. He stepped back a second time. The pillars behind him shifted with a short delay and completed the ring again.
"How annoying," he frowned.
[Echo Adaptation.]
It activated in his mind.
This Skill did not give a ready answer. It also did not reveal the whole structure of the attack in one moment.
But it recorded the rhythm of the flames’ movement, the reaction time gap, and the pattern of repetition.
First wave.
Then second.
Lian noticed that when the pillars changed direction, they lost their stability for a fraction of a second.
The third wave began.
The flames moved to block the forward path. In that very short pause, Thunder Step activated.
Lightning passed through the fire. He came out of the fiery prison and appeared right in the center of the seven Mages’ circle.
He raised both fists.
Thunder Calamity gathered on both arms, and then he struck both fists to the ground at the same time.
Lightning spread over the bridge’s surface. Seven branches of electricity moved outward and entered the legs and bodies of the Casters.
All seven bodies shook at the same time and their focus broke. Sevenfold Ember Prison went out and the Mages fell to the ground one after another.
Lian deactivated Echo Adaptation. This short use was enough.
Kael watched the field from a distance and his face was ugly. He was furious. The first row was broken. One Ballista was destroyed.
The main Mages were out of the field. The archers could not shoot freely.
If Lian moved without any obstacle for a few more minutes, the entire siege force would collapse.
Kael grabbed the Ember Vanguard spear with both hands. The flames around the weapon became more dense.
It was time for him to intervene personally and remove the biggest threat.

sentences.text: Lian started moving.
At first his steps were slow, but with each step his speed increased.
The first row of Rootbound Wardens reacted immediately.
They placed their tall shields next to each other.
The ends of the shields locked into the stone floor and golden lines spread from one to another.
The commander of the row raised his sword.
"Rootwall formation!"
More than twenty soldiers released Mana at the same time.
Golden light connected all the shields to each other.
For a moment, the row of soldiers was no longer a group of individuals.
It became one solid wall.
Golden roots came out from under the shields and went into the stone floor of the bridge.
Any hit that landed on one point would be split among all members of the formation.
This structure was built to stop high-level War Beasts and monsters that could break the city gates with a direct attack.
But unfortunately, they did not know that they were facing something more dangerous than any monster they had ever seen.
Lian did not slow down.
[Iron Fortress Charge.]
A dense gray pressure formed around his body.
His skin, muscles and bones became hard like the body of a moving fortress.
Then he released Thunder Calamity on that same structure.
Lightning spread over his shoulders, arms and legs.
Lian’s body disappeared among blue light and gray pressure.
His last step crushed the stone under his foot, and then he hit the center of Rootwall.
The sound of the explosion shook the whole bridge.
A circular wave spread from the point of impact and sent dust, stone pieces and golden sparks into the air.
Rootwall lasted less than a second.
The central shield bent in the middle.
The Rootbound Warden behind it did not even have time to scream.
His body left the ground and crashed into three soldiers behind him.
Lightning transferred from the central shield to the side shields.
The soldiers’ hands went numb.
Some lost control of their Mana.
The golden roots connected to the ground tore one after another.
The force of Iron Fortress Charge passed through the center of the formation.
The defensive line opened from the middle, like a wall broken by a huge hammer.
The soldiers on both sides of the gap were thrown back in fear.
The shield that they had worked so hard to form, fell apart so easily.
Lian passed through them without stopping.
The first spear came from the left toward his neck.
Predator’s Instincts sent the danger to his body before the blade reached halfway.
A raw and instinctive feeling that showed the direction of death.
Lian moved his head a few centimeters to the side.
The blade passed by his face and his right hand grabbed the spear’s shaft.
Thunder Calamity went from his palm into the weapon.
Electricity moved along the shaft and reached the soldier’s arms.
The whole body of the Rootbound Warden shook.
His eyes went white for a moment and he fell to the ground without being killed.
Three soldiers charged at Lian from behind.
He pulled his arm up and both soldiers lifted off the ground.
Their armored bodies spun in the air and crashed into the third one.
All three fell on top of each other.
Another Rootbound Warden with a heavy axe came from the right.
The axe blade was covered in Mana.
The man brought the strike down with all his weight.
[Diamond Skin.]
Lian’s skin became hard.
The axe hit his arm and the sound of metal hitting something harder than stone rose.
The blade only made a shallow scratch.
The Warden looked at his weapon in disbelief.
He had just felt like he hit the hardest thing he had ever seen.
And that hesitation was enough.
Lian’s thunderous fist hit the center of his chest.
The armor caved in and the soldier’s body was thrown back several meters, knocking two more soldiers to the ground with him.
The archers on the towers got the order to shoot.
Dozens of Mana arrows moved toward Lian from three angles.
Predator’s Instincts warned him with a constant pressure all over his body.
Lian did not even look up.
[Thunder Step.]
Blue lightning exploded among the arrows.
All the arrows passed through his previous location and hit the stone floor of the bridge.
He appeared on the platform of the first Ballista.
The three Cindari crew members were still preparing the next arrow.
None of them had time to react.
Lian placed his palm on the body of the device.
[Cataclysm Pulse.]
A compressed and invisible wave entered the Ballista’s structure.
At first nothing was seen, but then thin lines formed on all the metal plates.
A moment later, the device exploded from the inside.
Gears, plates, and the Mana chamber were thrown in all directions.
The Ballista crew fell to the ground from the blast wave, but Lian had controlled the Skill’s intensity so it would not tear their bodies apart directly.
He caught one of the large curved plates of the device in the air.
He held the plate in front of his body and moved from the platform toward the archer tower.
Arrows hit the temporary shield one after another.
The metal cracked under the pressure, but Lian kept moving forward.
"My god, he really is a monster!" The Awakeners did not know if they should be happy or terrified.
They did not know that among them there was such a monster who was pushing back the entire Cindari army all by himself.
All their defensive lines were falling one by one, and he alone had changed the whole flow of the battle.
The motivation and confidence among all the Awakeners increased and cheers grew louder.
"Haha, with a fighter like this, we have nothing to fear!"
"We will be the final victors!"
Rindo also looked more relieved seeing Lian’s real power.
The worries he had were slowly disappearing.
Of course, as much as they had become happy and relieved, their enemies had become more scared and their faces more ugly.
Now they understood where that human’s arrogance came from.
He really was powerful!
So powerful that he could go head to head with all of them!
At the same time, the rest of the Awakeners also entered the battle.
Seris moved from the right side of the bridge.
Her sword spun among the Rootbound Wardens with cold and precise speed.
Each strike could target the neck or heart of the soldiers, but she changed the sword’s path according to Rindo’s decision.
Knees.
Wrists.
Shoulders.
And weapons.
Every Cindari that faced her lost the ability to continue fighting in less than a few seconds.
Seraphina stood in the center of the human line.
Prismatic light moved on her blade.
Every time an arrow or ranged Skill came toward weaker Awakeners, she moved her sword.
Transparent and colorful layers formed in the air and changed the arrows’ path.
Some hit the ground.
Some hit empty walls.
And some returned toward the Cindari shields.
Liana had sent Shadow Wolf into the bridge’s shadow.
The huge wolf disappeared into the darkness of the floor and came out a few meters away from another soldier’s shadow.
Archers who thought they were safe at height suddenly saw black claws on their chest and shoulders.
Shadow Wolf did not kill them.
It threw them to the ground with a heavy strike and crushed their weapons.
Marcus kept the Ashfall defensive line.
His injured shoulder did not move fully, but he still pushed back every soldier that came through the gaps with his shield and sword.
Cassian moved among the buildings and the edge of the square.
He did not go into the most crowded part of the battle.
He found small commanders, message carriers, and Mages who were trying to keep the army’s formation together.
Every time one of them gave a new order, a sword from a blind spot hit their hand, foot, or shoulder.
But despite the presence of all of them, the real center of the field was Lian.
Wherever the soldiers formed a dense line again, he went in.
Wherever a Barrier formed, Cataclysm Pulse broke it from the inside.
Wherever a commander tried to reorganize the soldiers, Thunder Calamity’s fist took him out of the field.
The Cindari still had the advantage in numbers, but they could not gather their main force at one point.
Because wherever Lian reached, it collapsed in a few seconds.
Seven Fire Mages gathered on the left side of the bridge.
Their red robes flared up with Mana.
They raised their hands at the same time and threads of fire connected through their fingers to each other.
They had decided to eliminate the biggest threat at any cost!
They had to kill that damned human!
[Sevenfold Ember Prison.]
Seven pillars of fire rose from the ground around Lian.
The flames changed direction with his movement.
Every time he stepped toward one of the gaps, two pillars moved close together and blocked the path.
The heat increased quickly.
The air inside the fiery prison became heavy.
Lian’s burnt armor started smoking again.
He moved once to the right.
The flames blocked the path.
He stepped back a second time.
The pillars behind him shifted with a short delay and completed the ring again.
"How annoying," he frowned.
[Echo Adaptation.]
It activated in his mind.
This Skill did not give a ready answer.
It also did not reveal the whole structure of the attack in one moment.
But it recorded the rhythm of the flames’ movement, the reaction time gap, and the pattern of repetition.
First wave.
Then second.
Lian noticed that when the pillars changed direction, they lost their stability for a fraction of a second.
The third wave began.
The flames moved to block the forward path.
In that very short pause, Thunder Step activated.
Lightning passed through the fire.
He came out of the fiery prison and appeared right in the center of the seven Mages’ circle.
He raised both fists.
Thunder Calamity gathered on both arms, and then he struck both fists to the ground at the same time.
Lightning spread over the bridge’s surface.

All seven bodies shook at the same time and their focus broke.
Sevenfold Ember Prison went out and the Mages fell to the ground one after another.

He was furious.
The first row was broken.

The main Mages were out of the field.
