"Most of them have been corrupted, their power level gets higher every year, some of them no longer look like their original species."
"Our last exploration group had seventy-three people and only three returned."
The room became silent and Maelor continued.

"And all three died a few days later, one burned from the inside, one of their bodies turned into roots, the third tried to kill everyone in the medical center before dying, we do not know what happened to them."
"So you did not send anyone else." Serafina asked heavily.
"No, if getting close was possible, we would have found a way to heal the tree ourselves, no one dares to enter that area anymore."
Lian looked at the map, there was no ready answer in Vhalaris.
Neither Maelor knew the reason why the tree was drying up, nor did the city’s Archives record a way to heal it.
And the Cindari groups had not been able to enter the Death Zone either.
There was no other way left, he had to reach the Forgotten Tree himself.

chapters.title: Chapter 313: Evolution Quest Is Now Available
paragraphs: The interrogation ended shortly after, two Awakeners entered the room and lifted Maelor from the chair.
The Suppression chains were checked again.
One of the Mages placed a new seal on the back of his neck to keep any possible connection to the city’s Network cut off, and when Maelor left the room, Rindo looked at Lian.
"What are you going to do now?"
"Naturally, we’re going to the Forgotten Tree." Lian answered.
"Are you sure you don’t want me to come?" Serafina immediately said.
"It’s dangerous there."
"This isn’t the first dangerous place I’ve gone to."
"I know, but they need your help here." Lian added seriously and pointed at the map of Cinderhold.
"The closest military city is two days away, they might even send their first forces sooner."
"If you, Seris and I leave at the same time, Ashfall will lose its most important defensive forces."
"Rindo, Marcus, Ethan and the others are here." Serafina answered.
"But none of them are you, they need someone here who can hold the defensive line if the enemy army attacks." Then his tone became a little softer.
"And I don’t want you to enter that infected area either."
Serafina had not expected the last part of his sentence, her expression changed for a moment.
Lian usually did not directly talk about his worries for others, most of the time he simply made decisions and expected the others to follow.
"I understand." She sighed at last, then continued unwillingly.
"But if you take too long, I’ll come after you myself."
"We won’t be late." Lian said.
Before leaving, a final meeting was held in the council building, all the main members were present.
Rindo stood at the head of the table and explained the situation of the city.
"All three main bridges are under our control, the Cindari soldiers have been disarmed and moved to three separate prisons."
"Kael, Maelor and Tharos are in separate cells, Maelor has no access to his power."
"The civilians?" Cassian asked.
"They have a curfew, but their food and water will not be cut off, no house will be searched without a reason, if they cooperate, no one will hurt them." Then he looked at the map of the east.
"Several Awakeners have been sent toward Cinderhold, if reinforcements have already started moving, we need to know before they arrive."
"The western bridge is ready, we built several new Barriers and turned the working Ballista toward outside the city." Marcus added.
"Good." Rindo nodded and then looked at Ethan.
"The strike forces only attack when ordered, understood?"
"This is the third time you’ve said that." Ethan, who was sitting in the back, said.
"Because I’m still not sure you heard me the first time."
Marcus laughed quietly and Cassian placed several documents on the table.
"The Archive is currently under our control, we moved some of the documents to the safe room, but we need time to check everything."
"Anything you find about the Forgotten Tree, Cindar Vael or the other cities has priority." Rindo said.
Cassian nodded.
Liana had spoken less than the others since the beginning of the meeting, Shadow Wolf was lying on the ground beside her, but the worry on her face was clear.
"Still no news about Selina?" she finally asked.
Everyone became silent for a moment and she continued.
"If we complete the mission without finding her, what will happen to her?"
"The Main Quest reward is the escape of all Awakeners inside the Special Area, if we complete the mission, she will leave too." Lian answered.
Liana became a little calmer.
"If she’s still alive." But Ethan said without thinking.
The atmosphere in the room became cold at that moment.
Liana stared at him and Marcus hit Ethan hard in the side with his elbow.
"You didn’t need to say that."
"I only meant that—" Ethan’s expression changed.
"Think before you open your mouth next time." Seris, who was standing beside the window, said coldly.
Ethan closed his mouth.
Lian looked at Liana for several seconds, he had no proof and did not know where Selina was or what danger she had faced.
But he would not allow this worry to destroy the group’s focus.
"Selina is alive, trust her."
He said the sentence with such certainty that even Ethan could not find anything to say against it.
Liana looked at him and slowly breathed out, then nodded.
The meeting ended with the responsibilities being divided, Serafina took command of the central defense of Ashfall.
Marcus controlled the western bridge.
Ethan became responsible for the strike force, of course, with direct restrictions from Rindo.
Cassian continued checking the documents and the Archive.
Liana controlled the inner paths together with Shadow Wolf.
And Rindo became responsible for the overall management of the fortress, the prisoners and possible negotiations with the other cities.
Before leaving Vhalaris, Lian, Seris and Aren went toward Beastward.
Beastward was outside the city.
It was a large area between several huge roots, built to keep Mounts, War Beasts and captured creatures.
After the siege began, the Cindari guards moved One to the deepest area and locked him with several chains.
Even from a distance, signs of his restlessness could be seen, one of the walls had cracks and part of the outer gate had been chewed.
Several surface chains were bent, the disarmed Beastward guards were standing in front of the entrance.
"That creature hasn’t calmed down since you were taken." One of them said when he saw Lian.
"Did anyone hurt him?" Lian asked coldly.
"No one is brave enough to do that." The guard pointed at the broken wall.
"If the chains were not stronger, he probably would have destroyed half of Beastward."
They opened the seals on the gate, before the last door opened, the sound of heavy impacts could be heard from inside.
Something large hit the wall several times.
"The creature you mentioned is inside?" Aren asked with concern.
Lian nodded.
"One."
"His name is One?"
"Yes."
At that moment, the impacts stopped, a sudden silence formed inside the area.
Lian felt One’s presence through the Hive Link, first disbelief, then a strong wave of recognition.
Anger.
Worry.
Longing.
And a pure happiness that entered his mind without words.
A loud sound came from inside the area, a sound that was more like a mix of warning and excitement.
The last gate opened.
One came out of the darkness at high speed, the huge ant’s body covered almost the entire width of the path.
His jaws were open, his antennae were moving quickly, several broken chains were still hanging from his legs and body armor.
Aren thought the creature was going to attack, despite his weakness, he tried to move back.
Seris did not put her hand on her sword, she only watched.
One stopped right in front of Lian, his front legs dragged across the ground, and he lowered his large head.
Then he strongly pushed his chest against Lian, the force almost made him take one step back.
One’s antennae moved around his shoulder, neck and arm, through the Hive Link, the creature’s emotions entered Lian’s mind more strongly.
One was angry.
Not at Lian, but at those who had taken him, at the walls that had stopped him from reaching him.
Because he had been separated from Lian again for a long time, deep inside, there was a childish fear.
The fear that he had been abandoned, Lian placed his hand on One’s hard head armor.
"Calm down."
One made a protesting sound and pushed his head against his chest again.
This time Lian held his position more firmly.
"I think he missed you more than your family." Seris said from beside them.
Lian looked at One, the huge ant was still moving his antennae around his arm to make sure he was really standing in front of him.
"I missed you too."
The sentence was short, but its honesty reached One through the Hive Link.
The creature’s anger became weaker, his antennae moved more slowly and the young Vorhelm gently hit his head armor.
"It’s time to go."
One lowered his body so they could get on.
"We’re going to ride that?" Aren looked at the creature’s wide and armored back with doubt.
One turned his head toward him, his large jaws opened for a moment.
Seris sat on One’s back without saying anything and Lian helped Aren get on.
The eastern gate of Vhalaris was opened by Rindo’s order, Awakeners were standing on the walls, towers and bridges around it.
Some had come to see them off, others were there to protect the exit path.
Serafina was standing on one of the high platforms, the warm wind of the city moved her hair.
Liana was standing beside Shadow Wolf, Marcus was near the gate and Rindo was a few steps behind him.
"The direct path to Rootcrown is probably being watched by the Cindari, be careful." Rindo also shouted at the last moment.
Lian nodded from a distance and One started moving.
At first, he slowly passed through the gate, his feet made regular impacts on the bridge.
After completely passing the last defensive roots of Vhalaris, his speed increased.
The city behind them became smaller, the towers and golden bridges remained between the roots of Emberroot.
Lian looked back for a moment, Ashfall was now under human control, but there was no guarantee it would still remain that way when they returned, so they had to finish the mission sooner.
One entered the forest path, the sound of his footsteps spread between the trees.
At that moment, the System reacted and a blue panel appeared in front of Lian’s eyes.
[Emergency Quest Completed.]
[Quest: Escape Vhalaris.]
Lian looked at the notification for a moment.
He had not only escaped the prison, but had defeated the city’s army and captured an important part of Vhalaris.
However, according to the System, the Quest had only been completed now.
Until he had left the city’s actual boundary, the Escape Quest had not ended yet.
The next notifications appeared.
[Reward Granted: +1 Level.]
[Reward Granted: 10 Fragments.]
[Reward Granted: 100 Free Stat Points.]
[Level Increased.]
[You Have Reached Level 20.]
Lian felt something deep inside his body and his Class react.
The notifications stopped for several seconds, then a different panel appeared in front of him.
Its border was not blue like the normal Quests, it was dark and golden.
[Evolution Threshold Reached.]
[Evolution Quest Is Now Available.]

chapters.title: Chapter 314: First Evolution Quest
paragraphs: [Evolution Threshold Reached.]
[Evolution Quest Is Now Available.]
The dark golden panel was still floating in front of Lian’s eyes, he stared at the notification in front of him for several seconds.
Level 20.
He had finally reached the first real boundary of his Class, during all his previous Levels, he only needed to kill Monsters.
Bloodlust absorbed all the EXP.
Glutton sometimes gave him a new Skill or Talent.
The more he killed, the faster he grew, but now he had reached a boundary that he could not pass just by collecting EXP and he had to complete the Evolution Quest.
This Quest could be anything and it was different for everyone and it could be very easy or very difficult.
Maybe killing several Fallen Monsters, maybe collecting a certain number of Monster Cores, or reaching a certain Stat value.
Even if the System asked him to kill a Monster several Levels above him, it would not be strange.
But those things were for normal Classes, for him, whose Class was one of the unknown ones... how was this going to work?
Lian focused on the notification with a relatively calm mind, the panel became larger.
[First Evolution Quest]
[Current Evolution: Dormant Monster]
[Next Evolution: Fallen Monster]
His eyes stayed on the second line for a moment.
Fallen Monster.
That name alone was enough to get his attention and confirm one of his guesses, but before he had a chance to think, the Requirement section appeared.
[Requirement: Devour One of the Five Calamities.]
[Available Calamity Detected: The Black Silence]
[Objective: Devour The Black Silence.]
[Completion Reward: Class Evolution: Dormant Monster → Fallen Monster]
[Class Evolution Unlocked.]
For a moment, Lian thought he had read it wrong, he remained still for several seconds and showed no reaction.
He only looked at the panel, several seconds passed and then he read it again from the beginning to make sure he had not misunderstood it.
[Devour One of the Five Calamities.]
His eyes moved to the next line.
[Devour The Black Silence.]
For several moments, he could not even hear One’s movement, the wind between the branches or Aren’s chains hitting the huge ant’s armor.
Only one word repeated in his mind.
Devour.
’Devour?’ he said quietly in his mind.
He understood devouring a Monster, Glutton had absorbed the Skills and Talents of different creatures many times.
Even if the System asked him to Devour a Monster’s Soul or Bloodline, at least the meaning would be clear.
But The Black Silence? He did not even know what The Black Silence exactly was.
A disease? An infection? A Curse? Some kind of air? A living creature? Or something that none of these definitions could describe?
The System itself had called it a Calamity.
A disaster.
"Exactly how am I supposed to eat a disaster?" Lian narrowed his eyes slightly.
No answer came. The panel continued to show the same Objective, he moved his hand away from One’s armor and focused on the Quest again.
Maybe there was an option to change the Requirement or at least find more information about it.
A few moments later, the System reacted.
[Would You Like to Replace the Evolution Quest?]
Lian’s eyes became slightly brighter.
"Yes."
[Request Denied.]
The short smile that was about to appear on his face disappeared at that exact moment.
Lian looked at the answer for several seconds.
"Then why did you ask? Are you making fun of me?"
The System gave no answer, and he focused on the Quest again.
"Give me another Quest."
[Request Denied.]
"Give me something more logical." This time his eyebrows came together.
[The Evolution Requirement Cannot Be Changed.]
’This System is crazy.’ Lian stayed silent for a moment and then said it in his mind.
The panel immediately responded.
[Evolution Quest Remains Active.]
He stared for several seconds, he was not even sure if the System had intentionally answered his words or had only displayed the normal notification.
However, the result was clear, there was no replacement Quest, and there was no way to escape it either.
If he wanted to complete his first Evolution, he really had to Devour one of the Five Calamities.
And among those five, the only available Calamity was The Black Silence.
But how? How exactly was he supposed to devour a damn disaster? He doubted that something like this had ever happened in human history!
He had only just learned that something called Calamities and the Five Calamities existed and he still did not exactly know what the hell they were or how he was supposed to deal with them.
And now the System was telling him that he had to Devour one of them?
Lian read the panel again.
[Current Evolution: Dormant Monster]
[Next Evolution: Fallen Monster]
At least this part was interesting.
Until today, he had seen his own Class as a Monster, but the System had now shown that this Class had not only Levels, but also a real Evolution path.
Dormant Monster.
Fallen Monster.
He put together the Monster classification path he had heard about in his mind.
Dormant/Normal.
Fallen.
Unholy.
Demon.
Supreme.
’If my Class’s Evolution path is the same...’ his eyes changed slightly.
It was an interesting thought, right now, even at the Dormant stage, his Stats and Skills were not something that could be compared with normal Awakeners.
If the first Evolution really changed his body, Class and Soul, Fallen Monster could be a very large jump in power.
Then Unholy.
Demon.
And finally Supreme.
If every stage created a difference similar to the distance between Monster Tiers, reaching Supreme would be much more than simply becoming stronger.
It might reach a point where he could no longer be measured by the standards of a human Awakener.
’This part isn’t bad.’ The corner of Lian’s mouth rose for a moment.
But his eyes moved down again.
[Objective: Devour The Black Silence.]
’I just need to find out how to eat a damn Calamity first.’ The smile disappeared.
He did not know why, but for some reason he felt like the System was putting him on the path to becoming the final boss.
"What happened?" Seris’s voice came from behind him.
Lian closed the panel.
Seris had been looking at him for several minutes.
Lian usually did not change his expression much when the System gave him an important notification.
But this time he had frowned several times, smiled once and then made an expression like someone who had just realized that a much bigger problem than expected was in front of him.
"Why have you been staring at the air for several minutes?" Seris asked.
"I got an Evolution Quest." Lian answered calmly.
"Oh? Congratulations." Real interest appeared on Seris’s face.
"I don’t think it’s possible to complete it." Lian gave a bitter smile.
"Why?"
He thought for a moment, if he said that the Quest wanted him to eat The Black Silence, Seris’s next question was almost obvious and he had no answer, so he only said.
"Nothing."
"Are you sure?" Seris stared at his back for several seconds.
"It’s not a problem for now."
"Whatever you say." The young Pendragon shrugged.
Aren, who was sitting farther back on One, did not understand their language and only understood a few scattered words through Lian’s translation.
He leaned forward.
"Did something happen?"
"No. We’re continuing."
One kept his speed without needing another command.
The farther they moved from Vhalaris, the fewer signs of Cindari civilization they saw.
At first, the path still looked like a road, small roots had been cut away from its sides.
Several Ember Crystals had been placed on the trunks of the trees and gave the path a weak red light.
But after several hours, even these signs disappeared.
The road became narrow, then completely disappeared.
One had to move between roots that were sometimes taller than a human.
The Emberroot trees were much larger in this area.
Trunks with diameters of dozens of meters rose into the darkness and their branches met at such a great height that almost no natural light could pass through from above.
Fortunately, they still did not reach the huge size of the Giant Forest and did not cause extra confusion or trouble.
Wild Ember Crystals had grown inside the cracks of the trunks.
But unlike the cultivated Crystals of Vhalaris, their light was unstable.
Sometimes they became bright for several seconds and then turned off again, the air had become more humid, the smell of soil, tree bark and something like rusty iron filled the forest.
In some places, low fog moved between the roots.
Aren held tightly to the raised parts of One’s armor with both hands.
With the speed One was running between the trees, his body moved up and down with every jump.
After getting too close to the edge of the ant’s back, he quickly held himself tighter.
"You’ll get used to it after a few hours." Lian said without turning around.
"I hope I stay alive long enough to have the chance to get used to it." Aren controlled his breathing and looked around.
"This path wasn’t this dense before."
"What do you mean?" Lian asked.
"When I passed through this area before I was captured, there were many trees, but the ground wasn’t covered with this many roots." He pointed at one of the huge roots beside the path.
"These have grown a lot." Then he looked at the weak light of the Ember Crystals.
"And the lights have also become fewer."
Lian said nothing.
If Maelor was right, the Forgotten Tree had been drying up for years.
But it was strange that some parts of Emberroot had grown more wildly instead of drying up.
This growth was not natural...

Lian focused on the notification with a relatively calm mind, the panel became larger.
[First Evolution Quest]
[Current Evolution: Dormant Monster]
[Next Evolution: Fallen Monster]
His eyes stayed on the second line for a moment.
Fallen Monster.
That name alone was enough to get his attention and confirm one of his guesses, but before he had a chance to think, the Requirement section appeared.
[Requirement: Devour One of the Five Calamities.]
[Available Calamity Detected: The Black Silence]
[Objective: Devour The Black Silence.]
[Completion Reward: Class Evolution: Dormant Monster → Fallen Monster]
[Class Evolution Unlocked.]
For a moment, Lian thought he had read it wrong, he remained still for several seconds and showed no reaction.
He only looked at the panel, several seconds passed and then he read it again from the beginning to make sure he had not misunderstood it.
[Devour One of the Five Calamities.]
His eyes moved to the next line.
[Devour The Black Silence.]
For several moments, he could not even hear One’s movement, the wind between the branches or Aren’s chains hitting the huge ant’s armor.
Only one word repeated in his mind.
Devour.
’Devour?’ he said quietly in his mind.
He understood devouring a Monster, Glutton had absorbed the Skills and Talents of different creatures many times.
Even if the System asked him to Devour a Monster’s Soul or Bloodline, at least the meaning would be clear.
But The Black Silence?
He did not even know what The Black Silence exactly was.
A disease?
An infection?
A Curse?
Some kind of air?
A living creature?
Or something that none of these definitions could describe?
The System itself had called it a Calamity.
A disaster.
"Exactly how am I supposed to eat a disaster?" Lian narrowed his eyes slightly.
No answer came.
The panel continued to show the same Objective, he moved his hand away from One’s armor and focused on the Quest again.
Maybe there was an option to change the Requirement or at least find more information about it.
A few moments later, the System reacted.
[Would You Like to Replace the Evolution Quest?]
Lian’s eyes became slightly brighter.
"Yes."
[Request Denied.]
The short smile that was about to appear on his face disappeared at that exact moment.
Lian looked at the answer for several seconds.
"Then why did you ask?
Are you making fun of me?"
The System gave no answer, and he focused on the Quest again.
"Give me another Quest."
[Request Denied.]
"Give me something more logical." This time his eyebrows came together.
[The Evolution Requirement Cannot Be Changed.]
’This System is crazy.’ Lian stayed silent for a moment and then said it in his mind.
The panel immediately responded.
[Evolution Quest Remains Active.]
He stared for several seconds, he was not even sure if the System had intentionally answered his words or had only displayed the normal notification.
However, the result was clear, there was no replacement Quest, and there was no way to escape it either.
If he wanted to complete his first Evolution, he really had to Devour one of the Five Calamities.
And among those five, the only available Calamity was The Black Silence.
But how?
How exactly was he supposed to devour a damn disaster?
He doubted that something like this had ever happened in human history!
He had only just learned that something called Calamities and the Five Calamities existed and he still did not exactly know what the hell they were or how he was supposed to deal with them.
And now the System was telling him that he had to Devour one of them?
Lian read the panel again.
[Current Evolution: Dormant Monster]
[Next Evolution: Fallen Monster]
At least this part was interesting.
Until today, he had seen his own Class as a Monster, but the System had now shown that this Class had not only Levels, but also a real Evolution path.
Dormant Monster.
Fallen Monster.
He put together the Monster classification path he had heard about in his mind.
Dormant/Normal.
Fallen.
Unholy.
Demon.
Supreme.
’If my Class’s Evolution path is the same...’ his eyes changed slightly.
It was an interesting thought, right now, even at the Dormant stage, his Stats and Skills were not something that could be compared with normal Awakeners.
If the first Evolution really changed his body, Class and Soul, Fallen Monster could be a very large jump in power.
Then Unholy.
Demon.
And finally Supreme.
If every stage created a difference similar to the distance between Monster Tiers, reaching Supreme would be much more than simply becoming stronger.
It might reach a point where he could no longer be measured by the standards of a human Awakener.
’This part isn’t bad.’ The corner of Lian’s mouth rose for a moment.
But his eyes moved down again.
[Objective: Devour The Black Silence.]
’I just need to find out how to eat a damn Calamity first.’ The smile disappeared.
He did not know why, but for some reason he felt like the System was putting him on the path to becoming the final boss.
"What happened?" Seris’s voice came from behind him.
Lian closed the panel.
Seris had been looking at him for several minutes.
Lian usually did not change his expression much when the System gave him an important notification.
But this time he had frowned several times, smiled once and then made an expression like someone who had just realized that a much bigger problem than expected was in front of him.
"Why have you been staring at the air for several minutes?" Seris asked.
"I got an Evolution Quest." Lian answered calmly.
"Oh?
Congratulations." Real interest appeared on Seris’s face.
"I don’t think it’s possible to complete it." Lian gave a bitter smile.
"Why?"
He thought for a moment, if he said that the Quest wanted him to eat The Black Silence, Seris’s next question was almost obvious and he had no answer, so he only said.
"Nothing."
"Are you sure?" Seris stared at his back for several seconds.
"It’s not a problem for now."
"Whatever you say." The young Pendragon shrugged.
Aren, who was sitting farther back on One, did not understand their language and only understood a few scattered words through Lian’s translation.
He leaned forward.
"Did something happen?"
"No.
We’re continuing."
One kept his speed without needing another command.
The farther they moved from Vhalaris, the fewer signs of Cindari civilization they saw.
At first, the path still looked like a road, small roots had been cut away from its sides.
Several Ember Crystals had been placed on the trunks of the trees and gave the path a weak red light.
But after several hours, even these signs disappeared.
The road became narrow, then completely disappeared.
One had to move between roots that were sometimes taller than a human.
The Emberroot trees were much larger in this area.
Trunks with diameters of dozens of meters rose into the darkness and their branches met at such a great height that almost no natural light could pass through from above.
Fortunately, they still did not reach the huge size of the Giant Forest and did not cause extra confusion or trouble.
Wild Ember Crystals had grown inside the cracks of the trunks.
But unlike the cultivated Crystals of Vhalaris, their light was unstable.
Sometimes they became bright for several seconds and then turned off again, the air had become more humid, the smell of soil, tree bark and something like rusty iron filled the forest.
In some places, low fog moved between the roots.
Aren held tightly to the raised parts of One’s armor with both hands.
With the speed One was running between the trees, his body moved up and down with every jump.
After getting too close to the edge of the ant’s back, he quickly held himself tighter.
"You’ll get used to it after a few hours." Lian said without turning around.
"I hope I stay alive long enough to have the chance to get used to it." Aren controlled his breathing and looked around.
"This path wasn’t this dense before."
"What do you mean?" Lian asked.
"When I passed through this area before I was captured, there were many trees, but the ground wasn’t covered with this many roots." He pointed at one of the huge roots beside the path.
"These have grown a lot." Then he looked at the weak light of the Ember Crystals.
"And the lights have also become fewer."
Lian said nothing.
If Maelor was right, the Forgotten Tree had been drying up for years.
But it was strange that some parts of Emberroot had grown more wildly instead of drying up.
This growth was not natural...

chapters.title: Chapter 315: The Forest Has Changed
paragraphs: Lian looked around, this matter did not bother him that much because there could be any reason for it, this forest was so strange that practically nothing else could surprise him anymore.
And before he could finish his thought, Predator’s Instincts reacted.
A short warning moved along his spine.
One also slowed down almost at the same time, the giant ant moved a few more steps forward and then stopped completely, its antennae rising.
"Do you feel it?" Seris put her hand on the handle of her sword, she also felt a sense of danger.
Lian looked to the right, a very quiet sound came from among the black leaves.
Rustle.
Then a similar sound came from the left.
"How many?" Aren quickly made himself stable on One’s back.
Lian did not answer, Predator’s Instincts was warning him from several directions this time.
In the darkness, two red eyes appeared.
Then four.
Eight.
Twelve.
Four-legged monsters came out from between the roots one after another.
They had long bodies covered with thick black skin, red lines moved along their legs and spines, and their jaws were longer than normal.
Sharp teeth could be seen inside their mouths.
System panels appeared one after another.
[Emberhide Stalker — Lv.17]
[Emberhide Stalker — Lv.18]
[Emberhide Stalker — Lv.17]
[Emberhide Stalker — Lv.19]
At least eighteen creatures.
One of the Stalkers jumped onto a high root, a rough sound came from its throat, and then the entire pack attacked at the same time.
One did not even wait for an order, it lowered its head and slammed directly into the first creature.
The sound of armor and bones hitting each other rang out.
The Stalker was lifted off the ground.
One closed its jaws around its body and slammed the creature into the tree trunk like a piece of cloth.
The sound of several bones breaking could be heard.
Seris jumped down from One’s back, her sword was not even fully out of its sheath when the first Stalker reached her.
The blade came out in one horizontal movement, a thin line appeared on the monster’s front leg.
The Stalker lost its balance.
And the young Pendragon moved behind it with a short turn and cut its neck with the second strike.
Two more monsters approached her from both sides at the same time.
Lian jumped off One, Thunder Calamity formed around his fists, blue lightning lit up the darkness of the forest for a moment.
He landed in the middle of the pack, the first Stalker jumped toward him.
Lian moved his right fist forward, the direct hit against the monster’s jaw made a heavy sound, and lightning passed through the bones of its head.
Its body spun through the air and fell several meters away on the ground.
[You Have Killed Emberhide Stalker Lv.17.]
[Bloodlust Activated, 100% EXP Acquired.]
The second one jumped toward Lian’s shoulder from behind, Predator’s Instincts warned him before it reached him.
He did not even turn completely, his body made a half-turn and his elbow covered with Thunder Calamity hit the side of the monster’s head directly.
The Stalker’s skull broke with a dull sound, its body fell to the ground.
[You Have Killed Emberhide Stalker Lv.18.]
[Bloodlust Activated, 100% EXP Acquired.]
A new panel immediately appeared below the EXP notification.
[Level 20 Evolution Threshold Reached.]
[Further Level Advancement Locked Until Evolution.]
[Excess EXP Will Be Stored.]
Not only was the Evolution Quest unreasonable, but the next Levels were also locked behind it.
Even if he killed a thousand Monsters, Level 21 would not be available until he evolved, although he already knew about this.
Another Stalker attacked him.
Lian released his anger on it, Thunder Calamity gathered on his left fist and the punch hit the monster’s chest.
A wave of electricity came out from the back of its body and the creature was thrown several meters through the roots.
One slammed two more Stalkers under its body with its front legs.
Seris moved through three monsters.
The first blade cut off one of their legs, the second strike split the jaw of another, and the third did not even have time to react, the only thing it saw was blue lightning.
Thunder Step.
Lian appeared in front of it, struck its head with his palm, lightning covered the monster’s entire body and knocked it to the ground.
The battle did not even last five minutes, when the last Stalker tried to escape, One reached it from behind.
The giant ant’s jaws closed around the middle of the monster’s body, the sound of breaking bones spread through the forest.
One released the creature, the forest became quiet again and System notifications appeared one after another.
[You Have Killed Emberhide Stalker Lv.18.]
[EXP Stored.]
[You Have Killed Emberhide Stalker Lv.17.]
[EXP Stored.]
[You Have Killed Emberhide Stalker Lv.19.]
[EXP Stored.]
Lian looked at the word Stored, the EXP was not disappearing, this was at least good news, after Evolution, the stored amount would probably be applied.
But until then, his Level progress was completely stopped.

Besides that, he was still gaining Stats Points, apart from the 100 he had received as the reward for the Emergency Quest, and after this battle, he needed nearly 600 more Stats Points to reach his limit.
"Why do you look so upset?" Seris looked at him and asked.
"I can’t increase my Level until I evolve my Class."
"Then you should complete your Quest sooner." Seris laughed.
"If you knew what it asked for, you wouldn’t say that." Lian looked at her for a few seconds.
The young Pendragon became more curious, she knew this boy, even in the worst situations, he never made things this difficult and always did his best to reach his goal.
But the way he was talking now made it sound like he was facing an impossible goal, but this time she did not ask.
After a short inspection of the corpses and Lian collecting all of them as usual, they got back on One.
"These creatures were not here before." Aren gave the Stalker bodies a quick look as they passed them.

"Maybe they migrated, probably the drying of the Forgotten Tree is causing changes in the entire ecosystem of the forests and even causing problems for the Monsters." Lian thought for a moment and answered.
This possibility was much more reasonable and Aren did not disagree, he also thought such an answer was possible.
The journey continued and several more hours passed without any incident, but the farther east they went, the more the forest changed.
Some trees were completely dry, while the trees beside them had extremely swollen and twisted roots.
In several places, the water in the pools had become a very dark brown color.
Every time One got close to the water, it changed its path by itself, its instincts did not trust it.
Lian did not force it either, finally, One suddenly stopped again.
This time Predator’s Instincts sent a very different warning.
It was not like the presence of the Stalkers, the warning was heavier.
An unpleasant feeling formed deep inside Lian’s body, something like getting close to a creature whose nature was wrong.
One placed its legs firmly on the ground, a quiet sound came from its jaws.
Aren smelled the environment at the same moment, his expression changed.
"That smell..."
Lian also sensed it, it was sweet, too sweet, like a fruit that had been rotting in the heat for a long time, but beneath it was the smell of blood and rotten meat.
The sound of a tree breaking came from far away, then a huge root moved away from the path and a large creature came out of the darkness.
It had four legs, but that was its only similarity to normal animals, its body was as large as a small house.
Its thick gray skin had split in several places and black roots were coming out from the wounds.
Some of the roots were still moving.
A black liquid dripped from the creature’s mouth and every drop that fell on the ground turned the small plants around it black within a few seconds.
One of its eyes was completely gone, while the other shone with a yellow and sick-looking light.
[Corrupted Hollowroot Behemoth]
[Rank: Mutated]
Aren immediately moved back, real fear could be seen on his face.
"That blackness..."
Lian looked at the sticky liquid on the monster’s body.
"The Black Silence?"
"No... at least not completely, these are creatures that should live around the Forgotten Tree, so why is one of them here?" Aren answered quickly, then paused for a moment.
This was the reason this creature was Mutated, something had caused its mutation and it seemed that a small amount of The Black Silence here had caused it.
"You have encountered them before?"
"A few times, yes, I have been wandering in this forest for a long time, but as I said, I always saw them in the areas near the tree, the drying and death of the tree has also affected them."
"Is it possible that the tree’s condition has become so bad that even these creatures have been driven away?" Lian frowned.

chapters.title: Chapter 316: The Ruined Realm Before Fall
paragraphs: There was no answer anymore, because there was no answer to give, Aren also did not know what he should say.
The Corrupted Behemoth roared, its mouth opened and black strands stretched between its teeth.
Then it charged toward One, its weight making the ground shake.
One also moved forward, the two creatures collided with each other and the sound of the impact spread through the trees.
One, the giant ant was pushed back several meters across the ground, its legs leaving deep lines in the soil.
Aren held himself more tightly with worry.
«Right leg.» Seris jumped from behind One.
Lian understood what she meant, the young Pendragon quickly moved around the Behemoth.
Her sword struck the joint of the creature’s back leg, the blade did not completely cut through the thick skin, but it created a deep wound.
The Behemoth roared and one of the black roots on its body moved toward Seris like a whip.
She bent down, the root passed over her head and broke the trunk of the tree behind her.
Lian activated Thunder Step, appearing in front of the injured leg.
[Glacial Reaper Claw.]
A claw formed on his right hand, he placed his hand directly on the wound created by Seris.
Extreme cold entered the flesh and the Behemoth screamed.
The ice spread inside the wound, blood, muscle, black roots and finally the entire joint, the creature’s leg was completely frozen.
The Behemoth tried to move, the huge weight of its body fell onto the frozen leg, a cracking sound was heard and the monster lost its balance and fell onto one side of its body.
The ground shook.
One immediately moved forward, closing its jaws around the creature’s neck, but black roots came out of the Behemoth’s body and struck One’s armor.
Two roots entered through the gaps between the armor plates and the ant pulled back angrily.
Lian saw it, he gathered Thunder Calamity on his left hand and this time the lightning became much more concentrated.
He jumped onto the Behemoth’s head, the creature turned its yellow eye toward him, its mouth opened and black liquid was sprayed toward him.
Predator’s Instincts gave a strong warning, Lian turned his body in the air and the liquid passed beside his side and landed on the root behind him.
The surface of the root turned black at that moment.
The young Vorhelm landed, his lightning-covered fist struck directly at the top of the Behemoth’s skull.
[Thunder Calamity.]
The sound of thunder mixed with the sound of breaking bones, the monster’s head was smashed into the ground, stones and dirt flew around and the lightning entered the spine through its skull.
The huge body shook for several seconds, then became completely still.
[You Have Killed Corrupted Hollowroot Behemoth Lv.23.]
[Because this was a group kill, the reward has been reduced by half.]
Lian looked at the notifications, aside from the reduced EXP and Stats Points he received, he had finally obtained a new Skill after a long time!
[You Have Obtained a New Skill.]
[Behemoth’s Roar]
[Rank: Common (+)]
[Description: Each roar is a soul attack against targets within a 5-meter radius, it can cause shock, disruption and stop them for several seconds.]
[It does not work on targets that are much stronger than the user.]
[The maximum number of targets is 3, and the fewer targets there are, the stronger it becomes.]
[Consumes 25 Mana each time it is activated.]
After taking a short look at the Skill, it was clear that he had obtained a useful Skill, he could easily use it at important moments in a battle and completely change the result through surprise.
In addition, this was his first soul attack Skill.
«It was not much different from normal monsters.» Seris, who had come closer, looked at the corpse.

Lian got down from the corpse and nodded, he also had not felt any special difference, of course, considering that this monster was far too weak for them, it was possible that they would not notice anything in any case.
Aren got down from behind One and stood at a great distance from the corpse.
Even getting close to the corruption made him uncomfortable.
Lian covered his hand with the ice of Glacial Reaper Claw and froze the remaining black liquid on his palm and then removed the piece of ice from his hand and dropped it on the ground.
«Aren.»
The gray-haired man looked at him.
«Have you heard anything about the origin of the Black Silence?»
«The origin?»
«A Core, a main creature, an Artifact, anything that could be the source of the corruption.»
«No.» Aren thought for a few moments and then shook his head, he looked at the Behemoth’s corpse again.
«Even in my time, no one knew what the Black Silence really was, even the natives of this world don’t know.»
They sat on One again and continued their journey and after some time Aren said
«I heard many things from the Cindari during these twenty-five years.»
«I also found a few old writings, but none of them had a clear answer.»
«What did they think?» Lian asked, he hoped he could find a clue about the origin of this calamity, whatever it was, maybe this way he could find a way to complete the Quest.
«Some said it was a disease, something that changes the bodies of living creatures.»
«Some said it was a Curse, a punishment sent down by the gods.» He paused for a moment.
«And some said it was a creature itself.»
«A creature without a body?» Seris whispered with some surprise.
«Almost, more exactly, a creature that spreads itself inside other things.» Aren nodded.
Lian stared at the forest for a moment, this theory was more interesting than the others.
If the Black Silence really was a creature without a body or a scattered consciousness, maybe Devouring it would not be completely impossible, but there was still no proof.

Lian understood what she meant, the young Pendragon quickly moved around the Behemoth.

Lian activated Thunder Step, appearing in front of the injured leg.

A claw formed on his right hand, he placed his hand directly on the wound created by Seris.
Extreme cold entered the flesh and the Behemoth screamed.
The ice spread inside the wound, blood, muscle, black roots and finally the entire joint, the creature’s leg was completely frozen.

The ground shook.
One immediately moved forward, closing its jaws around the creature’s neck, but black roots came out of the Behemoth’s body and struck One’s armor.

Lian saw it, he gathered Thunder Calamity on his left hand and this time the lightning became much more concentrated.

chapters.title: Chapter 317: We Call Them Demon
paragraphs: «We call those types of monsters Demons now.» Lian said.
«Demon.» Aren looked at him for several seconds and then repeated the word very quietly.
It was as if his tongue was tasting a word for the first time, a word that should have always existed.
«Demon...»
The old fear appeared in his eyes again, for Lian, Demon was a Tier, a class of Monsters.
Very strong, very dangerous, but still something that could be measured.
For Aren, this word reminded him of creatures that had destroyed nations and Kingdoms.
«What happened next?» Seris asked, it was clear that she was curious about the experience of a civilization.
Aren looked forward for a while.
«When we all thought it was over...the gods finally answered.»
«In several places around the world, pillars of light came down from the sky.» The lands touched by those lights changed.
«Huge Barriers formed around the areas, the Monsters could not pass through them.»
«At first no one believed it, people were afraid to enter the light, but when the first groups found out that the Monsters could not pass through the Barrier, everything changed.»
Millions of survivors from all over the world moved toward those areas.
Some died on the way, some never arrived, but those who arrived found a place where they could sleep at night without fear of being attacked for the first time in years.
«If I remember correctly, then seven areas like this were formed.» Lian added.
«That’s right.» Aren nodded.
Seven Blessed Regions, the last seven shelters of humanity.
Inside the Barriers, civilization began again, survivors from different Kingdoms gathered together.
New walls were built, armies were organized, food was rationed, and combat training began.
«Everything happened very quickly, people who had been farmers, merchants or even children suddenly had no choice but to fight the Monsters.»
«We thought that maybe one day we could take our world back.» Then that smile also disappeared.
«We were still in the early stages of rebuilding when a new Rift appeared.»
«The one that led here.» Lian said.
«Yes.»
This Rift was different from the others, no Monster came out of it, no corrupted energy came from it and at first some people even thought it might be another gift from the gods.
But when several people tried to enter, another problem became clear.
«The Barrier at the entrance only allowed people within a certain age range to enter, the younger generation, people almost my age.»
Older people could not pass through, so the commanders and scientists of the Seven Regions decided to choose talented young people.
Aren was one of them, the mission was simple.
Enter the Rift, investigate the other side, collect possible resources, record the way back and return.
«The last part never happened.» Aren gave a short, bitter laugh.
Lian said nothing, this was exactly the Special Area, but the natives of the Ruined Realm did not know what they were facing at that time and did not know how they could find a way out.
Unfortunately, they also did not have a System like them that could explain all of this to them.
«When we entered, the Rift remained behind us, but from this side there was no way to pass through it.» Aren continued.
At first they thought the problem was temporary.
They waited for days, then weeks, then they tried to find another way and encountered the Cindari.
Tension began, then conflict, then war, the humans’ supplies ran out, some attacked Cindari cities to steal resources.
The main group broke apart.
Some went to the Giant’s Forest.
Some went to Emberroot.
The rest went to Glassthorn.
Each group hoped to find another way back, most of them never returned.
«Twenty-five years have passed for me, but two hundred and fifty years have passed for home.» A short silence appeared and Aren gave a bitter smile.
«I guess the world has nothing in common with what I remember now.»
Then a calmer expression appeared on his face.
«But at least I’m glad that the Seven Regions are still standing.»
Lian said nothing, Aren had learned this from the information that Lian had intentionally given him before in a vague way.
The problem was that the truth was different, he was not from the Seven Regions, even Aren’s world was not his world.
But even so, he felt a little sorry for the natives of the Ruined Realm, they had faced a disaster almost like theirs.
But unfortunately, they were not as lucky as them to have a System called The Will come to help them and save them from falling and collapsing.
Even so, they learned to adapt and found a way to survive, on the other hand, it seemed that they had also been given a blessing.
Those same seven safe regions that the Monsters could not enter.
Aren stayed silent for a few moments, then looked at Lian, then curiosity replaced nostalgia.
«Now you tell me, what happened while I was gone? How did the Seven Regions change? Do the Demons still attack?»
This time Lian really had no answer.
But this was a question about a world that he knew nothing about. A simple lie could be exposed in the second sentence.
If he said the wrong Region name, if he talked about something that had already been destroyed.
If Aren asked a more detailed question, the trust he had worked to gain would disappear at that moment.
Lian stayed silent for several seconds, Seris also noticed his silence and gave a short look at his face.
«Lian?» Aren raised his eyebrows slightly.
Lian opened his mouth, trying to build a vague answer.
Something like «Many things have changed.» or «I’ll explain everything later.»
But before a single word came out, One suddenly stopped, the stop was so fast that Aren was thrown forward.
Lian grabbed him and stopped him from falling.
Seris kept her balance on One’s armor at the same moment, her hand moved to the handle of her sword.
«What happened?»
One made no sound, its antennae were completely fixed toward the front.
Lian checked Predator’s Instincts, there was no warning of immediate danger.
So there was nothing nearby, but One had sensed something from far away.
The young Vorhelm stood on its back, the forest ahead of them was dark, at first nothing could be seen but then an orange point moved between the tree trunks.
Then a second one.
A third.
Dozens of lights.
They were not the natural light of Ember Crystal, their movement was organized, Lian narrowed his eyes, a sound could also slowly be heard.
Footsteps.
Hundreds of footsteps.
Metal hitting metal.
The sound of wheels.
And the roar of several large creatures.
«An army?» Seris had heard it too.
Lian got down from One without answering, the group moved toward a higher path on the right.
A huge root stood several meters above the ground like a natural wall. He climbed up first.
Seris followed him, Aren pulled himself up with the help of One and Lian.
From that point, they had a wider view, at first only columns of light could be seen but after waiting for several minutes, the first lines of the army appeared from between the trees.
Cindari.
Hundreds of them.
Rootbound Wardens moved in organized lines.
Large shields were attached to their backs, spears were pointed upward and archers moved on both sides of the column.
Behind them, Flame mages wearing red robes could be seen.
Several armored War Beasts pulled heavy carts.
The bodies of the Beasts were covered with Steel plates and their horns had been reinforced.
Three moving Ballista were also visible among the army, each one was mounted on a large cart and pulled by several Beasts.
It was not a small force, the military column was moving for a real battle.
«How many are there?» Aren asked in shock.
Lian checked the approximate number, at least several hundred, maybe more than six hundred.
And then he saw the flag above the main line, a golden Forge was placed on a black background.
Two separate flames rose upward from the center of the Forge, the symbol Maelor had talked about several hours earlier.
Cinderhold.
«Are they going to the place I think they’re going to?»
Seris checked the direction of the column, the army was moving from east to west.
Not toward the Forgotten Tree or toward Rootcrown, but directly toward Vhalaris.
«They’re going to the city.» Then she looked at Lian and said.
Lian said nothing, news of Vhalaris’s fall had reached Cinderhold.
Or maybe this force had moved before the battle ended.
Maelor had said Cinderhold was two days away, but fast units could arrive earlier.
This army was probably the same advance force that had been sent to free the city.
«If they reach Vhalaris, Rindo and the others will enter another war before we reach the Forgotten Tree.» Seris said.
«With this number, it might be more than just a war.» Aren looked at the number of soldiers.
Lian took his eyes away from the army and looked east, toward the place where the Forgotten Tree was waiting for them.
Main Quest.
Corrupted Titan.
The Black Silence.
Evolution Quest.
Everything that could truly decide the fate of this Special Area and even Earth was in that direction.
Then he looked west again, Vhalaris was behind them.
Rindo.
Serafina.
Liana.
Marcus.
Ethan.
Cassian.
Dozens of Awakeners.
And an army that was now moving directly toward them.
The Forgotten Tree was waiting in front of them.
Vhalaris was behind them.
And between the two, an army of several hundred people from Cinderhold was moving toward Lian’s friends.
For several seconds, he only stared at the military column and then lightning slowly began to form between his fingers.
Maybe this was a chance that could help him reach his maximum Stats...

Three moving Ballista were also visible among the army, each one was mounted on a large cart and pulled by several Beasts.
It was not a small force, the military column was moving for a real battle.
«How many are there?» Aren asked in shock.
Lian checked the approximate number, at least several hundred, maybe more than six hundred.
And then he saw the flag above the main line, a golden Forge was placed on a black background.
Two separate flames rose upward from the center of the Forge, the symbol Maelor had talked about several hours earlier.
Cinderhold.
«Are they going to the place I think they’re going to?»
Seris checked the direction of the column, the army was moving from east to west.
Not toward the Forgotten Tree or toward Rootcrown, but directly toward Vhalaris.
«They’re going to the city.» Then she looked at Lian and said.
Lian said nothing, news of Vhalaris’s fall had reached Cinderhold.
Or maybe this force had moved before the battle ended.
Maelor had said Cinderhold was two days away, but fast units could arrive earlier.
This army was probably the same advance force that had been sent to free the city.
«If they reach Vhalaris, Rindo and the others will enter another war before we reach the Forgotten Tree.» Seris said.
«With this number, it might be more than just a war.» Aren looked at the number of soldiers.
Lian took his eyes away from the army and looked east, toward the place where the Forgotten Tree was waiting for them.
Main Quest.
Corrupted Titan.
The Black Silence.
Evolution Quest.
Everything that could truly decide the fate of this Special Area and even Earth was in that direction.
Then he looked west again, Vhalaris was behind them.
Rindo.
Serafina.
Liana.
Marcus.
Ethan.
Cassian.
Dozens of Awakeners.
And an army that was now moving directly toward them.
The Forgotten Tree was waiting in front of them.
Vhalaris was behind them.
And between the two, an army of several hundred people from Cinderhold was moving toward Lian’s friends.
For several seconds, he only stared at the military column and then lightning slowly began to form between his fingers.
Maybe this was a chance that could help him reach his maximum Stats...

chapters.title: Chapter 318: Battle With Another Army
paragraphs: The lightning was still moving quietly between Lian’s fingers.
From the top of a huge root that came out of the Emberroot like a natural rock, he watched the army of Cinderhold.
More than six hundred Cindari were moving through the trees.
The Rootbound Wardens were moving in organized lines. Large and heavy shields were attached to their backs, and the tips of their spears reflected the red light of the Ember Crystals.
The archers were spread on both sides of the column.
The Flame Mages were moving slightly behind the front line, and their red robes dragged across the ground with every step.
The Healers were near the center of the army, and several command units with heavier armor and golden marks could be seen among them.
Three mobile Ballistae were also with the army, each one placed on a heavy carriage and pulled by two armored War Beasts.
This army had not come for patrol, it was moving for war and its destination was completely clear.
Vhalaris.
He looked at them without moving for a few seconds.
If this army reached the city, Rindo and the others would be forced to enter another full-scale battle.
Serafina and Marcus could probably hold the defensive lines.
Cassian could target the commanders.
Ethan would definitely welcome the battle.
But the problem was not the main fighters.
There were more than forty Awakeners in Ashfall and a large part of them had not even gotten close to Level 20.
Some of them had no experience fighting a regular army.
And if Cinderhold launched a direct attack, even if the humans won, casualties would be unavoidable.
Lian narrowed his eyes slightly, but there was another reason for him to pay attention to the army.
Six hundred soldiers, six hundred living beings with Stats that could be absorbed.
His Level was currently locked at 20.
EXP from every Kill was being stored and until he completed the Evolution Quest, he could not gain any new Levels.
But Stats did not depend on Level-Up until they reached their maximum, Stats growth had its own path.
Lian opened his Status Panel for a moment, then looked at the army again and this time he no longer saw only six hundred soldiers.
It was almost like looking at a moving mine full of Stats.
"Are you going after them?" Seris, who was standing beside him, saw his expression, looked at the army for a few seconds and then asked.
"Yeah."
"Do you need help?"
"No." Lian jumped down from the edge of the root.
"There are several hundred of them, are you sure?"
"That’s why I’m going."
Seris understood what he meant immediately, Lian had not chosen this battle only to protect Vhalaris.
He wanted to use it, the soldiers of Cinderhold were not only enemies to him, they were a source of power.
"Okay."
"Okay? That’s all? This is crazy!" Aren, who was still standing on top of the root, looked between the two of them.
"If he needed help, he would ask for it."
Aren stared at him.
Then he lowered his head and looked at Lian, who was walking alone toward an entire army.
For a few seconds, he really could not find anything to say.
"If all humans of the new generation have become like this, maybe Demons are no longer the biggest problem in the world." He finally muttered.
Down in the forest, the Cinderhold army still had no idea that they were there.
The main column continued at a steady speed, the wheels of the Ballistae made sounds as they moved over the dry roots.
The armored War Beasts shook the ground with every step, in the center of the army, several officers riding smaller Beasts moved together.
"We still have no response from Vhalaris." One of them held a communication Crystal in his hand.
It was a type of Crystal that contained magic and a mechanism that allowed it to communicate with another matching version of itself.
A man wearing black armor with orange lines on his shoulders looked ahead.
Commander Varesh Korr, commander of the Cinderhold Advance Legion.
"What was the last message?" he asked seriously.
The communication officer checked the Crystal.
"Rootwarden requested immediate reinforcements, then the connection was cut."
"And Kael?" Varesh frowned.
"He sent no direct message."
"Do you think the Outsiders defeated Kael?" another officer moving on the right said.
They naturally knew about the Outsiders and knew who they were, they had even found and captured some of them during these few days.
Unlike Maelor, they had only directly captured humans, they saw no need to use tricks and directly interrogated them to get the information they wanted.
Several nearby soldiers looked at them.
"It’s only a rumor." Varesh turned his head slightly.
"But the message came from Vhalaris." The younger officer said.
One of the older commanders laughed.
"Kael is the commander of the border, maybe they caught him by surprise in battle." Then he looked at the army column.
"But six hundred Cinderhold soldiers are a different matter, even if they defeated him, they have no chance against us."
Varesh said nothing, however, he increased the speed of the column.
At that moment, a very short sound came from above the trees, he raised his head and suddenly blue light cut through the space above the column for a fraction of a second.
[Thunder Step.]
Lian appeared directly in the center of the army from a distance, right in the middle of the command unit and his boots touched the ground.
Varesh only had time to see a human shadow.
Lian brought both fists down.
[Thunder Calamity.]
Lightning exploded the moment it hit the ground, a circular wave of electricity, dirt and pressure spread out from the center of the army.
The sound of the explosion shook the forest and more than twenty soldiers were thrown off the ground at the same moment.
Lightning moved from metal armor to weapons and from the weapons to the bodies of the soldiers beside them.
Several Rootbound Wardens lost control of their legs and fell to the ground.
The nearby War Beasts panicked, one of them suddenly turned to the right.
The Ballista carriage behind it left its path and crashed directly into the line of archers.
Screams came from several directions at once, the back line crashed into the soldiers in front.
A shield fell, a spear broke, the communication Crystal fell from the officer’s hand and hit the ground.
Varesh remained on his feet, but the lightning wave pushed him several meters backward.
"What—" He did not have time to finish his sentence.
Thunder Step activated again, Lian disappeared, and a moment later he appeared beside the communication officer.
A simple punch hit the center of the man’s armor, the officer was lifted from the ground and crashed into a tree trunk.
The Crystal was still on the ground and Lian crushed it with his heel.
"Attack!"
"From which direction?"
"Get into formation!"
"Mages forward!"
Orders could be heard from every direction, but no one knew how many enemies there were or where they had come from.
One of the Rootbound Wardens looked around in fear.
"Are they above us?"
"No! He’s in the middle of us!" another shouted.
Thunder Step activated for the third time.
Lian appeared on the platform of the second Ballista, the crew of the machine had just noticed his presence and one of them reached for the firing lever.
He placed his palm on the body of the machine.
[Cataclysm Pulse.]
The destructive wave entered its structure, the Ballista remained intact for a moment and then the sound of gears breaking came from inside it.
The Steel plates cracked one after another.
The Mana chamber exploded and the entire machine broke apart from the inside, throwing the crew around with the explosion.
Lian came out from among the pieces of metal, one of the War Beasts charged toward him with a roar.
The creature was more than three meters tall and its horns were covered with Ember Steel.
He did not even change his path, Thunder Calamity gathered around his right fist and at the moment of impact, his fist hit the Beast directly in the forehead.
The sound of breaking bone and lightning came together, the huge body of the creature twisted and fell to the ground.
The heavy carriage attached behind it turned out of control and moved between two lines of Flame Casters.
Several Mages were forced to abandon their half-finished Barriers to escape.
"Wait..." Varesh finally saw the enemy, his eyes narrowed and the image from the reports they had received from Vhalaris came back to his mind.
A young human, dark hair and a strange lightning power that he used.
Exactly a report about someone like this had reached them before the city’s fall, warning them about such a strange person.
"It’s him."
"Who?" the officer beside him asked.
"That human whose name is Lian!"
The name spread through the lines of soldiers, the first reaction changed and confusion was replaced by recognition.
And recognition brought back their confidence for a few seconds, because no matter how strange the reports from Vhalaris were, the enemy was still only one person.
"He’s alone!" Varesh drew his sword and his voice was strengthened by Mana.
"Surround him!"
The Rootbound Wardens began to move, the archers knelt on the ground.
The Flame Mages gathered Mana again, the rear units closed the paths.
More than one hundred soldiers moved toward the center at the same time.
If someone survived for a few minutes and remembered that sentence later, it would probably be the most bitter joke of his life.
Lian stood in the middle of the circle of soldiers, Predator’s Instincts was active, danger was coming from every direction.
A spear from the right, two arrows from above, a Fireball from behind, a sword from the front and a magical root from below the ground.
But him? He was neither worried nor afraid, in fact, he was excited, after a long time he could finally have some excitement.
Unfortunately, the Cindari did not know that they were not facing a human, but a monster in human form...

chapters.title: Chapter 319: A Massacre I
paragraphs: He moved, pulling his head slightly back, the first arrow passed in front of his face.
His left hand came up and caught the second arrow with two fingers, at the same moment, a spear came from the right.
Lian grabbed the soldier’s wrist, pulled the weapon from his hand, and without looking, turned the spear shaft to the left.
The back of it hit another Rootbound Warden in the face, the man fell to the ground with a broken nose.
A Fireball came from behind and Predator’s Instincts warned him.
But this time Lian did not dodge.
[Diamond Skin.]
The flames hit his back, the explosion spread around his body, but his hardened skin and high Resistance absorbed a large part of the damage.
"Got him!" The Mage in the distance smiled when he saw the explosion, thinking he had successfully killed the human.
The flames moved away, but Lian was no longer there.
The Mage lost his smile and before he had a chance to react, blue light appeared in front of him.
Thunder Step.
Lian was only a few centimeters away from him, the man did not even have time to step back and the lightning-covered fist hit his chest.
His body was thrown backward and crashed into several people.
The notifications started.
[You Have Killed a Cindari Lv.21.]
[Butcher Activated.]
[Stats Points Acquired.]
Lian gave the panel a quick look, a small smile appeared on his face.
Another soldier attacked, one hit.
Two more.
Lian activated Thunder Step and appeared in the middle of a group of archers, Thunder Calamity was released from his body and six people fell to the ground at the same time.
[Stat Points: 179]
Lian’s eyes stayed on the number for a moment, this was exactly what he wanted.
If his Level was currently locked, that did not mean his growth had to stop.
He clenched his fists and the lightning around both of his arms became stronger.
"If my Level is locked for now..." His eyes moved across the hundreds of soldiers in front of him.
"Then I’ll Max out my Stats."
From that moment, the speed of the battle increased, Thunder Step moved through the army like a blue line.
One moment Lian was on the left side of the column, the next moment he was in the center and then behind the third Ballista.
His palm touched the machine, he activated Cataclysm Pulse and the Ballista exploded.
Two seconds later he appeared beside the Healers, the senior Healer created a white Barrier, it seemed to have been created by an Item.
But it was useless against the monster, Lian activated Iron Fortress Charge and his body entered the Barrier with great force.
The shield resisted for a moment, then broke from the center and the Mages behind it fell to the ground.
Lian intentionally removed the Healers from the battlefield first, then the communication officers, then the long-range units.
An army without orders and healing was only a group of scattered soldiers and in less than a minute, no straight formation remained.
In the rear, some still did not know what had happened.
"Where is the Commander?" one of the soldiers asked.
"How many enemies are there?" another shouted.
The answer came from the front.
"One!"
For a moment, the man thought he had heard wrong.
"What?"
"There’s only one!"
But what he saw in front of his eyes did not match those words, the army column had been broken.
The Ballistae had been destroyed, the War Beasts were running away.
Dozens of people were lying on the ground and a complete massacre was happening right in front of their eyes!
Only one human had been able to do this to them? Fear filled their entire bodies and they finally realized what kind of threat they were facing.
And the blue light was still moving through all this chaos.
Varesh clenched his teeth, unlike many of his soldiers, he did not panic, he still believed the situation could be controlled.
He had understood the problem, gathering together, the closer the soldiers got to each other, the easier it was for Lian to attack several people at the same time.
"Spread out!" He raised his sword, his voice was strengthened by Mana so everyone could hear him.
"Groups of ten! Thirty meters between each group! Mages attack from a distance!"
"Have the remaining Ballista target the area, not the target itself!"
"But our own soldiers—" one of the officers asked in shock.
"Do it!" Varesh shouted.
The army finally took a new formation, the groups separated from each other and the archers moved behind the trees.
Flame Mages attacked from several angles, the soldiers nearby no longer tried to surround Lian closely.
Instead, they kept him inside a large area and for a few moments, the tactic actually worked.
Fireballs were fired from a long distance, Lian activated Thunder Step.
The explosion burned the ground behind him, but the next attack came from another side.
Then a third, the archers targeted the places where they thought he would move.
The Rootbound Wardens sent their roots into the ground to limit the paths.
A Ballista fired from a distance, the huge bolt did not land on Lian himself, but directly landed in an area where more than twenty Cindari were also standing.
Varesh was willing to sacrifice his own soldiers to kill this human! As a commander, it was a hard choice, but there was no other choice!
The explosion destroyed part of the forest, several tree trunks broke and flames rose into the air.
Lian came out of the smoke, his clothes were more burned and a thin line of blood could be seen on his cheek.
But he was still standing.
"Why won’t he die?" Varesh felt real worry for the first time, why did nothing they did work?
Lian looked at the scattered groups, reaching them one by one would take time.
His Stats were still increasing, but the growth speed had become slower.

The army had spread out, and they were no longer coming close to fight, if he wanted to hunt them one by one, it would take time and he had no interest in wasting time, not when the damn flow of time here was ten times slower than in his own world.
Lian took a slow breath, it was no longer time to kill them one by one.
He stood in the center of the burned ground, did not move and the archers immediately noticed.
"He stopped!" one shouted.
"Now!" Varesh also saw it.
Dozens of Mages began gathering Mana, arrows were raised, the Rootbound Wardens prepared their Skills.
For a moment, the soldiers thought Lian had finally become tired, but they were very, very wrong...
Then the Mana around him changed, the lightning disappeared and the blue electricity between his fingers vanished, the cold of Glacial Reaper Claw was also gone.
Something else came out of him.
Something that terrified the Cindari soldiers even before they could see it.
[Bloodborne Calamity Domain.]
The first sign was small, a very dark drop separated from the tip of Lian’s finger.
It looked like blood, but its color was far too black.
The drop fell onto the ground, nothing happened for a moment and then mist came out from that point.
Thin, heavy and dark red, almost black in some parts, as if a huge amount of old blood had dissolved into the air.
The mist slowly moved across the ground and that calm movement made it even more frightening.
"What is that?" one of the nearby soldiers stepped back several steps.
No one answered, because no one knew how to answer.
The mist reached the boots of the first Cindari, the man looked down, felt nothing and for a moment raised one shoulder.
But suddenly he coughed.
Once.
Twice.
On the third time, blood came out of his mouth.
"What happened?" the soldier beside him said in surprise.
The man put his hand over his nose, when he lowered his hand, his palm was full of blood.
Several meters away, another soldier put his hand on his neck and his breathing became short.
"I can’t..." Air could not enter his lungs.
A third one started shaking, dark red veins appeared under the skin of his neck.
The mist continued to spread.
"Fall back!" Varesh shouted.
But it was too late.
Bloodborne Calamity Domain was not a normal Poison.
When the mist reached the bodies of the Cindari, if they were lucky enough not to die, they would at least definitely become paralyzed.
The soldiers inside the mist felt that something was watching them.
Not from one direction, but from everywhere... illusions that they saw before their deaths!
The sound of their own heartbeats became loud in their ears, every beat sounded like the hit of a drum.
The smell of blood became stronger in their noses, some of them saw shadows inside the mist and things that did not really exist.
One soldier pointed his sword at empty space.
"He’s there!"
"Who?" his friend shouted.
The man turned around.
There was nothing.
Then a shadow moved behind him, he screamed, his breathing became more painful and the Mana inside their channels became thick and heavy.
Some Mages stopped their Skills halfway because the Mana no longer moved according to their commands.
The soldiers’ skin had become cold, but their bodies were burning from the inside.
One raised his hand, dark red veins moved under his skin.
"Don’t breathe in the mist!" he shouted in fear.
The soldier beside him put a piece of cloth over his mouth and a few seconds later, blood came down from his eyes.
"It also enters through the skin!"
Real fear began at that moment.
The senior Healer raised his hands, white light formed around a group of soldiers.
[Purification.]
The mist moved back for a few moments, the soldiers breathed in relief, but then a black and red strand reached the Barrier again.
It slowly moved across the surface of the light and the Healer opened his eyes wider.
The mist passed through the Barrier, the white light shook and went out.
The Healer did not even have time to react before he started coughing.
Inside the mist, Lian no longer looked like a normal human.
He was only a shadow, sometimes blue lightning lit up inside the mist, then came the sound of thunder, screams and silence again.
One of the soldiers saw Lian’s shadow several meters ahead.
His hand shook, he raised his spear, blinked and the shadow disappeared.
Thunder Step.
Lightning appeared behind him, the man slowly turned his head.
Lian was standing right there, a short attack and the soldier fell to the ground.
From a distance, Aren watched the scene.
The blood-colored mist had covered a large part of the forest, screams came from inside it but nothing could be seen, sometimes only blue lightning lit up the entire mist for a fraction of a second.
He swallowed his saliva in fear... he was watching one of the most terrifying things he had ever seen in his life...

But this time Lian did not dodge.
