The flames hit his back, the explosion spread around his body, but his hardened skin and high Resistance absorbed a large part of the damage.
"Got him!" The Mage in the distance smiled when he saw the explosion, thinking he had successfully killed the human.
The flames moved away, but Lian was no longer there.
The Mage lost his smile and before he had a chance to react, blue light appeared in front of him.
Thunder Step.
Lian was only a few centimeters away from him, the man did not even have time to step back and the lightning-covered fist hit his chest.
His body was thrown backward and crashed into several people.
The notifications started.
[You Have Killed a Cindari Lv.21.]
[Butcher Activated.]
[Stats Points Acquired.]
Lian gave the panel a quick look, a small smile appeared on his face.
Another soldier attacked, one hit.
Two more.
Lian activated Thunder Step and appeared in the middle of a group of archers, Thunder Calamity was released from his body and six people fell to the ground at the same time.
[Stat Points: 179]
Lian’s eyes stayed on the number for a moment, this was exactly what he wanted.
If his Level was currently locked, that did not mean his growth had to stop.
He clenched his fists and the lightning around both of his arms became stronger.
"If my Level is locked for now..." His eyes moved across the hundreds of soldiers in front of him.
"Then I’ll Max out my Stats."
From that moment, the speed of the battle increased, Thunder Step moved through the army like a blue line.
One moment Lian was on the left side of the column, the next moment he was in the center and then behind the third Ballista.
His palm touched the machine, he activated Cataclysm Pulse and the Ballista exploded.
Two seconds later he appeared beside the Healers, the senior Healer created a white Barrier, it seemed to have been created by an Item.
But it was useless against the monster, Lian activated Iron Fortress Charge and his body entered the Barrier with great force.
The shield resisted for a moment, then broke from the center and the Mages behind it fell to the ground.
Lian intentionally removed the Healers from the battlefield first, then the communication officers, then the long-range units.
An army without orders and healing was only a group of scattered soldiers and in less than a minute, no straight formation remained.
In the rear, some still did not know what had happened.
"Where is the Commander?" one of the soldiers asked.
"How many enemies are there?" another shouted.
The answer came from the front.
"One!"
For a moment, the man thought he had heard wrong.
"What?"
"There’s only one!"
But what he saw in front of his eyes did not match those words, the army column had been broken.
The Ballistae had been destroyed, the War Beasts were running away.
Dozens of people were lying on the ground and a complete massacre was happening right in front of their eyes!
Only one human had been able to do this to them?
Fear filled their entire bodies and they finally realized what kind of threat they were facing.
And the blue light was still moving through all this chaos.
Varesh clenched his teeth, unlike many of his soldiers, he did not panic, he still believed the situation could be controlled.
He had understood the problem, gathering together, the closer the soldiers got to each other, the easier it was for Lian to attack several people at the same time.
"Spread out!" He raised his sword, his voice was strengthened by Mana so everyone could hear him.
"Groups of ten!
Thirty meters between each group!
Mages attack from a distance!"
"Have the remaining Ballista target the area, not the target itself!"
"But our own soldiers—" one of the officers asked in shock.
"Do it!" Varesh shouted.
The army finally took a new formation, the groups separated from each other and the archers moved behind the trees.
Flame Mages attacked from several angles, the soldiers nearby no longer tried to surround Lian closely.
Instead, they kept him inside a large area and for a few moments, the tactic actually worked.
Fireballs were fired from a long distance, Lian activated Thunder Step.
The explosion burned the ground behind him, but the next attack came from another side.
Then a third, the archers targeted the places where they thought he would move.
The Rootbound Wardens sent their roots into the ground to limit the paths.
A Ballista fired from a distance, the huge bolt did not land on Lian himself, but directly landed in an area where more than twenty Cindari were also standing.
Varesh was willing to sacrifice his own soldiers to kill this human!
As a commander, it was a hard choice, but there was no other choice!
The explosion destroyed part of the forest, several tree trunks broke and flames rose into the air.
Lian came out of the smoke, his clothes were more burned and a thin line of blood could be seen on his cheek.
But he was still standing.
"Why won’t he die?" Varesh felt real worry for the first time, why did nothing they did work?
Lian looked at the scattered groups, reaching them one by one would take time.
His Stats were still increasing, but the growth speed had become slower.

The army had spread out, and they were no longer coming close to fight, if he wanted to hunt them one by one, it would take time and he had no interest in wasting time, not when the damn flow of time here was ten times slower than in his own world.
Lian took a slow breath, it was no longer time to kill them one by one.
He stood in the center of the burned ground, did not move and the archers immediately noticed.
"He stopped!" one shouted.
"Now!" Varesh also saw it.
Dozens of Mages began gathering Mana, arrows were raised, the Rootbound Wardens prepared their Skills.
For a moment, the soldiers thought Lian had finally become tired, but they were very, very wrong...
Then the Mana around him changed, the lightning disappeared and the blue electricity between his fingers vanished, the cold of Glacial Reaper Claw was also gone.
Something else came out of him.
Something that terrified the Cindari soldiers even before they could see it.
[Bloodborne Calamity Domain.]
The first sign was small, a very dark drop separated from the tip of Lian’s finger.
It looked like blood, but its color was far too black.
The drop fell onto the ground, nothing happened for a moment and then mist came out from that point.
Thin, heavy and dark red, almost black in some parts, as if a huge amount of old blood had dissolved into the air.
The mist slowly moved across the ground and that calm movement made it even more frightening.
"What is that?" one of the nearby soldiers stepped back several steps.
No one answered, because no one knew how to answer.
The mist reached the boots of the first Cindari, the man looked down, felt nothing and for a moment raised one shoulder.
But suddenly he coughed.
Once.
Twice.
On the third time, blood came out of his mouth.
"What happened?" the soldier beside him said in surprise.
The man put his hand over his nose, when he lowered his hand, his palm was full of blood.
Several meters away, another soldier put his hand on his neck and his breathing became short.
"I can’t..." Air could not enter his lungs.
A third one started shaking, dark red veins appeared under the skin of his neck.
The mist continued to spread.
"Fall back!" Varesh shouted.
But it was too late.
Bloodborne Calamity Domain was not a normal Poison.
When the mist reached the bodies of the Cindari, if they were lucky enough not to die, they would at least definitely become paralyzed.
The soldiers inside the mist felt that something was watching them.
Not from one direction, but from everywhere... illusions that they saw before their deaths!
The sound of their own heartbeats became loud in their ears, every beat sounded like the hit of a drum.
The smell of blood became stronger in their noses, some of them saw shadows inside the mist and things that did not really exist.
One soldier pointed his sword at empty space.
"He’s there!"
"Who?" his friend shouted.
The man turned around.
There was nothing.
Then a shadow moved behind him, he screamed, his breathing became more painful and the Mana inside their channels became thick and heavy.
Some Mages stopped their Skills halfway because the Mana no longer moved according to their commands.
The soldiers’ skin had become cold, but their bodies were burning from the inside.
One raised his hand, dark red veins moved under his skin.
"Don’t breathe in the mist!" he shouted in fear.
The soldier beside him put a piece of cloth over his mouth and a few seconds later, blood came down from his eyes.
"It also enters through the skin!"
Real fear began at that moment.
The senior Healer raised his hands, white light formed around a group of soldiers.
[Purification.]
The mist moved back for a few moments, the soldiers breathed in relief, but then a black and red strand reached the Barrier again.
It slowly moved across the surface of the light and the Healer opened his eyes wider.
The mist passed through the Barrier, the white light shook and went out.
The Healer did not even have time to react before he started coughing.
Inside the mist, Lian no longer looked like a normal human.
He was only a shadow, sometimes blue lightning lit up inside the mist, then came the sound of thunder, screams and silence again.
One of the soldiers saw Lian’s shadow several meters ahead.
His hand shook, he raised his spear, blinked and the shadow disappeared.
Thunder Step.
Lightning appeared behind him, the man slowly turned his head.
Lian was standing right there, a short attack and the soldier fell to the ground.
From a distance, Aren watched the scene.
The blood-colored mist had covered a large part of the forest, screams came from inside it but nothing could be seen, sometimes only blue lightning lit up the entire mist for a fraction of a second.
He swallowed his saliva in fear... he was watching one of the most terrifying things he had ever seen in his life...

chapters.title: Chapter 320: A Massacre II
paragraphs: Even after twenty-five years in this world, Aren had never seen anything like this.
He did not want to admit it or anything like that ... he had no such intention at all, but the scene in front of him was truly terrifying and bloody.
It even reminded him, to some extent, of those first days when the Monsters had entered human cities and started killing and destroying humans ...
"Is this... human?" he asked quietly.
Seris did not answer for a while, her eyes fixed on the mist, this was also the first time she had seen Lian use this Skill, and it was strange even for her.
She was not a kind girl who cared about the lives of Monsters or non-human races, but even for her, the scene in front of her was strange.
Of course, she could not say that she disliked it either ...
"No." she said afterward.
Aren looked at her, and in the end, both of them decided to stay silent, each with different thoughts, and it was unclear what either of them was thinking.
And he looked at the battlefield again and felt a new feeling toward Lian inside him.
Fear.
He had just understood that when Lian had said in the prison, "By breaking everything in our way," he had not only meant escaping from the prison.
This man seemed to use that strategy for almost his entire journey.
Inside the Domain, System notifications appeared at a crazy speed.
[You Have Killed a Cindari Lv.20.]
[Stat Points Acquired.]
[Stat Points: 202]
[Stat Points: 217]
Then,
[Stat Points: 273]
Lian moved through the mist, every time the Domain took another victim, Butcher reacted.
Some soldiers died directly from the Poison and pressure of the Domain, some became weak and he finished them.
Although their deaths looked painful, they actually were not, they did not even realize how they were dying.

If the poison could kill them, it only took a few seconds, and if they became paralyzed, they could not feel anything anymore, so despite how terrifying it looked, the Cindari were not really suffering pain.
A group tried to escape from the north, all of them had already given up on fighting this monster and only wanted to run away.
Thunder Step.
Lian appeared in front of them, the Domain moved with him and the mist followed behind him like a sea of blood.
Their escape route was blocked, the soldiers turned around and went in the other direction.
But there was mist there too.
[Stat Points: 301]
Varesh’s voice was heard from somewhere far away.
"Retreat!" This was the first time an official order to retreat had been given.
The same soldiers who had shouted a few minutes ago that the enemy was only one person were now throwing away their armor so they could run faster.
One Rootbound Warden dropped his shield, one archer threw away his bow, the Flame Mages removed their robes because they felt the mist sticking to the cloth.
But the Domain passed through cloth, passed through armor, and passed through Barriers.
Some only ran a few dozen meters before falling to their knees.
[Stat Points: 419]
Lian increased his speed.
He reached the remaining groups inside the mist, Thunder Calamity sometimes creating a flash of blue light for a moment.
Cataclysm Pulse broke a Barrier, Glacial Reaper Claw blocked another escape route.
The Domain itself was enough.
But Lian had turned it into a hunting ground.
Varesh watched the scene from a distance, the army he had commanded for years was no longer an army.
The soldiers no longer followed orders, the units had collapsed, there were no lines anymore.
There was no communication left, the only thing that existed was escape.
He understood that the reports from Vhalaris were not exaggerated, they might have even been incomplete.
"This creature..." The word human did not even come to his mind, he did not even know what he should call the thing in front of him.
Were all humans like this? He doubted it, they had captured and tortured several humans, and some of them had even died.
That had made him even more confident about their plan to escape to their world, if all humans were this weak, conquering their world would be easy, right?
But unfortunately, they were terribly wrong.
None of them were this powerful or this terrifying ... so why was this human so powerful?
[Stat Points: 533]
The number of notifications became smaller, not because the Skill had become weaker, but because the number of living people inside the Domain had decreased.
Lian felt this, most of the army was either dead, or had escaped and left the area.
He moved the Domain with himself and a group of thirty people was running between the trees.
Thunder Step.
The mist moved several dozen meters, and the screams started again.
[Stat Points: 601]
[Stat Points: 722]
Lian no longer felt anything like a battle, the battlefield had become completely one-sided and he was only collecting Stats.
Although he was slowly starting to feel tired.
[Stat Points: 771]
[Warning! Warning! Warning!]
[Your Remaining Mana Is Below 10 Units.]
[You Have A Maximum Of Three Minutes Of Mana Remaining.]
’So this is my current limit?’ he thought, many of the Cindari were running away and he made no effort to stop them.
He did not have the ability to do that, and besides, he could only use his Skills for a maximum of three more minutes, and he could fight for five minutes at most.
His time to end this battle was slowly running out.
At that moment, a young officer passed between two trees.
His armor was broken, he had dropped his sword, and he was only running.
Lian activated Thunder Step and appeared in front of him, the officer was so terrified that he could not even stop.
Lian hit his chest with a short strike and the man’s body fell to the ground.
[Stat Points: 792]
A new panel immediately appeared.
[Temporary Stat Growth Limit Reached.]
[Maximum Additional Stat Points Available at Current Level: 792.]
[Further Stat Acquisition Has Been Suspended.]
[Restriction Will Be Reassessed After Level Advancement / Evolution.]
Lian stood in the middle of the mist for a moment and looked at the notification.
"So this has a Limit too, my guess was right." This made sense.
If there was no limit, he could raise his Stats without limit by killing thousands of creatures.
But the System had currently placed a limit before the first Evolution, and he had reached that limit.
He looked at his panel and realized that his total unused and used Stats were exactly 4000, and this guess was also correct.
His limit was twice that of Awakened with five-star classes.
Lian looked around, there was no need to continue the killing.
He deactivated Bloodborne Calamity Domain.
The mist became calm at first, then returned toward the center like something alive and the red and black strands gathered from between the trees.
The forest became visible again and what had been hidden behind the mist appeared.
The ground was covered with corpses, armors had fallen between the roots, broken shields.
Spears, bows, overturned carts, two Ballistas were completely destroyed and the third was stuck between a broken tree.
Several War Beasts were dead or had escaped, parts of the forest had burned and some tree trunks had broken because of Cataclysm Pulse.
And a heavy silence had fallen over everything, six hundred soldiers had entered this part of Emberroot and only one person was standing against them.
Of course, this did not mean that all of them were dead, many had also managed to escape, they had spread in every direction and had used the fact that Lian was busy with the others to escape.
Of course, it did not matter, no matter how many there were, they would never dare to stand against humans again, and it was unlikely that they would recover from the trauma they had experienced.
And in short, there was now nothing left of that army in front of him, except one commander.
Lian had been watching Varesh from the beginning.
The commander’s insignia, his position in the center of the column, and the soldiers’ reactions to his orders all showed that he was the most important person in the army.
That was why, when Lian expanded the Domain, he deliberately changed the path of the mist so Varesh would not be in the center of the most dangerous area.
The commander was now lying under a broken tree trunk, his armor burned in several places.
Some of the Bloodborne Poison had entered his body and the veins on his neck had turned dark, but he was still conscious.
He heard footsteps and raised his head.
Lian was coming toward him through the last strands of mist.
Varesh looked around, there were no soldiers beside him.
No Healer, no communication officer, no Rootbound Warden to raise a shield in front of him.
Only a monster.
"What... are you?" The commander’s eyes became empty for a moment as he asked in a weak voice.

chapters.title: Chapter 321: The Enemy Called Time
paragraphs: "Right now, I’m the one asking the questions." Lian lifted the broken tree trunk with one hand and threw it aside.
Then he grabbed Varesh by the front of his armor and leaned him against another intact tree trunk, the commander groaned in pain.
"How many more armies are on their way to Vhalaris?" Lian asked.
Varesh stayed silent.
Lian waited for a few seconds, but no answer came.
[Glacial Reaper Claw.]
Coldness formed around his right hand, he placed the claw on Varesh’s injured shoulder.
Ice slowly spread across his armor and skin, the commander clenched his teeth.
The cold was more painful than his wound.
"I won’t ask again, you better answer, otherwise your death can be very painful."
Varesh looked into his eyes. Then his gaze moved toward the bodies of his army, he knew this was not an empty threat.
"This... was the Advance Legion."
"Continue." Lian kept the claw in the same place.
"The main force of Cinderhold is behind us."
"How many?"
"More than a thousand, but it’s not only us."
"How many cities sent soldiers?" Lian’s expression changed slightly.
Varesh stayed silent for a moment and at the same time, the cold of Glacial Reaper Claw became stronger and the ice moved from his shoulder toward his neck.
"Three cities sent forces, Cinderhold, Emberwell, Ashenreach."
"So your main capital? Rootcrown?" Lian asked.
"They aren’t sending the main army, most of their forces are fighting near the Death Zone, but they sent some Elites and commanders to coordinate." Varesh laughed, but his laugh turned into a cough.
"Maelor sent an emergency message before the Network was cut."
"The message didn’t only reach Cinderhold, it reached all the cities."
So Maelor had considered the possibility of Vhalaris falling even before the complete defeat.
"When the communication was completely cut off, the Cinderhold Council ordered a full mobilization." The commander looked at him for a few seconds.
"Before that, the plan was to capture the Outsiders, but after Vhalaris fell, the order changed."
"Vhalaris must be reclaimed at any cost, and all humans except their leaders must be executed immediately."
Any cost meant that if necessary, even civilians would be sacrificed, if necessary, Ashfall would be destroyed.
If necessary, the Cindari inside the city would be killed along with the humans.
"How long until they arrive?" Lian asked.
"The main force of Cinderhold... less than a day, Emberwell will probably take a day and a half, Ashenreach will take longer." Varesh answered.
"Two to three days until they all gather." The timing was exactly the worst possible.
They also needed time to reach the Forgotten Tree, if they returned and defeated the Cinderhold forces, Emberwell would arrive.
Then Ashenreach, then whatever forces the other cities had.
The war could continue for days and during all that time, the Forgotten Tree would get closer to death.
Lian was also completely sure that the Awakeners had no chance against the main army of the Cindari, even with his help, victory was impossible.
Although right now it looked like he had won easily, that was not really true, he had used the element of surprise and completely disrupted the entire army.
After he spread fear among them, he used Bloodborne and the terror increased among them and caused most of them to run away.
And in the end, he ran low on Mana, meaning that if those Cindari had not run away and had stayed until the very end, they could have defeated him.
Fortunately, they were too stupid to realize that.
The sound of One moving came from behind, Seris and Aren approached the battlefield.
When Aren entered the area, the speed of his steps became slower, until a few minutes ago he had only seen the mist from a distance.
Now he could see the result, his eyes moved across the bodies and broken equipment.
Even after twenty-five years of living in this world, he could not get used to this sight.
"Bad news?" Seris looked directly at Varesh and could feel a small amount of worry in the air.
"Three more armies are moving toward Vhalaris."
"Three?"
"The main force of Cinderhold, Emberwell and Ashenreach."
"Rootcrown also sent Elites."
"Are we going back?" Seris looked toward the west for a moment, she could understand how serious the situation was and she also knew that the Awakeners had no chance.
In fact, even with them there, the situation might not change that much.
Lian also looked in the same direction, Vhalaris could not be seen from here, only the trees of Emberroot stood between them and the city.
"No." Then he turned his gaze back toward the path to the Forgotten Tree.
Seris waited for an explanation without objecting.
"If we go back and defeat Cinderhold, Emberwell will arrive, then Ashenreach, then whatever forces the other cities have."
"So you’re going to let them attack your friends?" Aren asked.
"No, but the way to end this war is not to kill every Cindari army." Lian looked at him and stayed silent for a few seconds.
"We need to go to the Forgotten Tree and complete the Main Quest."
If the Forgotten Tree was saved and the Corrupted Titan was stopped, the Quest reward could allow all the Awakeners to leave the Special Area.
They no longer had to protect Vhalaris forever, they only needed to hold it for long enough.
At that moment, their biggest enemy was no longer the Cindari, it was time.
Aren had no idea what they were talking about and decided to stay silent and leave dealing with the situation to them.
Lian looked at Varesh again, the commander said nothing and seemed to be thinking about what would happen to him, would he die? Or would he survive?

Lian turned on the Crystal, for a few seconds there was only static and then the light inside it changed.
The connection was established.
"Vhalaris."
There was a short silence and then Rindo’s voice came.
"Lian?"
"Yeah."
"What happened?" Rindo’s voice immediately became serious, they were only supposed to communicate in the most urgent situations.
Lian looked at the destroyed battlefield.
"We found the Cinderhold advance army."
"How many?"
"About six hundred."
"And?"
"They’re no longer a problem." Lian said without changing his tone.
There was silence for a few seconds, Rindo probably decided not to ask exactly what had happened.
"What’s the bad news?"

"Three more armies are on their way, the main force of Cinderhold is less than a day away, Emberwell comes after them, Ashenreach has also moved, and Rootcrown sent several Elites." He added after explaining how serious the situation was.
"Don’t get into an open battle, hold the bridges, use Maelor and Kael for negotiations, buy as much time as you can."
"Are you coming back?" Rindo added after thinking for a moment, he knew they had no chance against an army, so buying time was the only way.
"No, if I go back, this war won’t end, besides, there are too many of them and even with me there, it wouldn’t make much difference, we’re going straight to the Forgotten Tree."

"Finish your job, leave this place to us."
"Stay alive and if things get really bad, run, you should create a way to escape and retreat from now."
"That’s already the plan." The Student Council President nodded.

It was not hard to understand that the humans seemed to think their way to survive was there.
"If it doesn’t, all of you will soon have a bigger problem than us." Lian looked at him and added with sarcasm.
Varesh understood that he meant the Corrupted Titan, he said nothing.
With a controlled strike to the side of the commander’s neck, Lian sent him to join the rest of his soldiers.
Then he turned around.
One lowered its body, Seris silently sat on its back but Aren stayed in the battlefield for a few more seconds.
His eyes were fixed on the place where the Cinderhold army had stood before the battle.
Six hundred people and ... now only silence.
He slowly mounted One, this time keeping a little more distance from Lian.
Lian noticed, but said nothing.
One started moving, first passing slowly through the broken equipment.
After leaving the battlefield, it increased its speed.
Emberroot once again turned into dark red lines around them and the wind hit their faces.
The young Vorhelm looked forward, behind them, three armies were moving toward Vhalaris.
The first main force might reach the city in less than a day, the other two armies were moving behind it.
And in front of them, the Forgotten Tree was getting closer to death every moment.
There was no time left to stop, either they had to stop the disaster before the armies arrived or when they returned, there might no longer be a fortress left to return to.

sentences.text: "Right now, I’m the one asking the questions." Lian lifted the broken tree trunk with one hand and threw it aside.
Then he grabbed Varesh by the front of his armor and leaned him against another intact tree trunk, the commander groaned in pain.
"How many more armies are on their way to Vhalaris?" Lian asked.
Varesh stayed silent.
Lian waited for a few seconds, but no answer came.
[Glacial Reaper Claw.]
Coldness formed around his right hand, he placed the claw on Varesh’s injured shoulder.
Ice slowly spread across his armor and skin, the commander clenched his teeth.
The cold was more painful than his wound.
"I won’t ask again, you better answer, otherwise your death can be very painful."
Varesh looked into his eyes.
Then his gaze moved toward the bodies of his army, he knew this was not an empty threat.
"This... was the Advance Legion."
"Continue." Lian kept the claw in the same place.
"The main force of Cinderhold is behind us."
"How many?"
"More than a thousand, but it’s not only us."
"How many cities sent soldiers?" Lian’s expression changed slightly.
Varesh stayed silent for a moment and at the same time, the cold of Glacial Reaper Claw became stronger and the ice moved from his shoulder toward his neck.
"Three cities sent forces, Cinderhold, Emberwell, Ashenreach."
"So your main capital?
Rootcrown?" Lian asked.
"They aren’t sending the main army, most of their forces are fighting near the Death Zone, but they sent some Elites and commanders to coordinate." Varesh laughed, but his laugh turned into a cough.
"Maelor sent an emergency message before the Network was cut."
"The message didn’t only reach Cinderhold, it reached all the cities."
So Maelor had considered the possibility of Vhalaris falling even before the complete defeat.
"When the communication was completely cut off, the Cinderhold Council ordered a full mobilization." The commander looked at him for a few seconds.
"Before that, the plan was to capture the Outsiders, but after Vhalaris fell, the order changed."
"Vhalaris must be reclaimed at any cost, and all humans except their leaders must be executed immediately."
Any cost meant that if necessary, even civilians would be sacrificed, if necessary, Ashfall would be destroyed.
If necessary, the Cindari inside the city would be killed along with the humans.
"How long until they arrive?" Lian asked.
"The main force of Cinderhold... less than a day, Emberwell will probably take a day and a half, Ashenreach will take longer." Varesh answered.
"Two to three days until they all gather." The timing was exactly the worst possible.
They also needed time to reach the Forgotten Tree, if they returned and defeated the Cinderhold forces, Emberwell would arrive.
Then Ashenreach, then whatever forces the other cities had.
The war could continue for days and during all that time, the Forgotten Tree would get closer to death.
Lian was also completely sure that the Awakeners had no chance against the main army of the Cindari, even with his help, victory was impossible.
Although right now it looked like he had won easily, that was not really true, he had used the element of surprise and completely disrupted the entire army.
After he spread fear among them, he used Bloodborne and the terror increased among them and caused most of them to run away.
And in the end, he ran low on Mana, meaning that if those Cindari had not run away and had stayed until the very end, they could have defeated him.
Fortunately, they were too stupid to realize that.
The sound of One moving came from behind, Seris and Aren approached the battlefield.
When Aren entered the area, the speed of his steps became slower, until a few minutes ago he had only seen the mist from a distance.
Now he could see the result, his eyes moved across the bodies and broken equipment.
Even after twenty-five years of living in this world, he could not get used to this sight.
"Bad news?" Seris looked directly at Varesh and could feel a small amount of worry in the air.
"Three more armies are moving toward Vhalaris."
"Three?"
"The main force of Cinderhold, Emberwell and Ashenreach."
"Rootcrown also sent Elites."

chapters.title: Chapter 322: The City Of Rootcrown
paragraphs: Several hours had passed since the destruction of the Advance Legion.
One was running at full speed through the eastern part of Emberroot, and every time his powerful legs hit the ground, piles of dirt and dry leaves were thrown into the air behind him.
Lian had not looked behind even once.
Vhalaris had disappeared among the huge trees hours ago.
Time was putting pressure on them from both sides, so the journey no longer looked anything like the calm trip from a few days ago.
Even at night, they did not stop for long, One would rest for a while and then they would continue the journey.
Seris was used to this rhythm, Lian had no problem with it either.
Aren had also lived in this forest for years, and a large part of that time had been spent running away from the Cindari.
Because of that, none of them had a problem with not resting or stopping, and everyone preferred to move toward the tree at full speed.
On the very first day, Predator’s Instincts gave several short warnings, in the past, Lian would have moved toward the Monsters at the first chance.
EXP.
Stats.
Skill.
Talent.
Every Kill was an opportunity for him, but things were different now.
His Level was locked at 20.
Any new EXP was only being stored.
And after massacring the Cinderhold army, he had also reached the temporary Stats limit.
For now, the Monsters they found on their way gave him almost no direct benefit.
But Seris was still not Level 20.
When Predator’s Instincts sensed the presence of several Monsters to the left of the path for the fourth time, Lian put his hand on One’s armor.
The giant ant slowed down.
"What happened?" Seris looked at him.
"Several Monsters are coming closer, I don’t need to kill them, they’re all yours, I’ll only take the corpses." Lian pointed toward the black bushes.
Even though he no longer needed to kill them, their corpses were still useful to him.
"All of them?"
"Until you reach Level 20." This girl had still not reached Level 20, and she was still a good distance away, it would be good if she could reach Level 19 or 20 before they reached the tree.
"You’re being generous." A very small smile appeared on Seris’s face.
"They’re no longer useful to me." Lian answered.
"I understand, I’ll try to finish it quickly." The young Pendragon jumped down from One.
A roar came from between the roots.
The first creature jumped out of the darkness with a high leap.
It was four-legged, its skin was black and rough, its jaw was too large compared to its skull, and orange lines moved under the skin of its neck and shoulders.
The System showed the Monster’s name.
[Ember Maw Hound]
[Rank: Normal]
More creatures appeared behind it.
[Ember Maw Hound — Lv.19]
[Ember Maw Hound — Lv.18]
[Ember Maw Hound — Lv.17]
In the end, fourteen Monsters covered the path, and among them, a larger creature with two rows of red lines on its body stepped forward.
[Ember Maw Alpha]
[Rank: Normal]
The Alpha lowered its head, and a weak flame came out from between its teeth.
Seris calmly took one step forward.
"Are you not going to help her?" Aren, who was still sitting on One, asked.
"No."
"But there are many of them, are you sure it’s not dangerous for her?"
"I know, but don’t worry, she’s strong, after me, she’s the strongest among all the humans you’ve seen."
"You two really have a different idea of what danger is." Aren looked at Seris.
The first Hound attacked.
Seris waited until the last moment.
When the Monster’s claws were almost at her face, she moved her body half a step to the side.
Her sword moved only once, the blade entered the Hound from under its jaw and came out from the top of its skull.
The Monster did not even have a chance to land.
Seris pulled out her sword and with a short turn, threw the dead body toward the second Hound.
The two creatures crashed into each other.
The young Pendragon moved forward, put her foot on the second Monster’s shoulder, pressed it against the ground and brought her sword down along its neck.
The third one came closer from the right.
Without fully looking at it, Seris pulled her blade back, the tip of the sword entered the Monster’s open mouth.
A moment later, it came out from the back of its neck, her movements were fast, but there was something more than speed in them.
Economy of movement, no extra attacks, no wasted Mana, no unnecessary moves and only the most deadly path between the starting point and the ending point.
Four more Hounds attacked at the same time.
Seris planted her feet firmly on the ground, Mana gathered around her sword and a bright arc formed in front of her.
Two Monsters were thrown back at the same time, the third received a deep wound on its chest and the fourth attacked from above her head.
She lowered her body, the Monster passed over her and she stood up at the same moment and pulled the blade from its stomach to its chest.
The Alpha finally moved, its mouth opened and Mana gathered deep inside its throat.
Seris noticed the change and changed the direction of her body.
A moment later, a concentrated flame was fired toward her.
She rolled across the ground, the explosion happened right behind her, dirt and pieces of roots were thrown into the air.
The Alpha did not wait, it came out of the flames and charged toward Seris with all its weight.
Seris held her sword in front of her body, the impact pushed her several meters back and her boots made lines in the ground.
The Alpha attacked again.
But this time Seris had understood its path, at the last moment, instead of moving backward, she moved directly toward the Monster.
She passed beside its shoulder, her sword made a deep line on its front leg.
The Alpha lost its balance.
Seris turned back, the second strike hit the same leg and the Monster fell onto one knee.
Seris put her foot on its skull, raised the sword with both hands and drove it directly into the point where the neck and skull connected.
The Alpha’s body shook for several seconds, then became still and she pulled out her sword.
The remaining Hounds lasted only a few more minutes after the Alpha died, when the last Monster fell to the ground, Seris took several calm breaths.
Blood had gathered on the edge of her sword.
System panels appeared in front of her eyes.
[You Have Killed Ember Maw Hound Lv.18.]
[EXP Acquired.]
[You Have Killed Ember Maw Hound Lv.19.]
[EXP Acquired.]
[You Have Killed Ember Maw Alpha Lv.21.]
[EXP Acquired.]
"Was that good?" Lian asked from a distance.
"I got closer." Seris closed the panel.
"Good."
Then the girl cleaned her sword and sat on One again, and the journey continued.
On the second day, the forest was still alive, but less than before, the Ember Crystals that could be seen between the trunks every few hundred meters on the first day were slowly disappearing.
The red light around them became weaker, the humidity was higher and low steam moved between the huge roots.
Around noon, a heavy sound came from ahead of them.
One stopped, ahead of them, a huge root had broken across the path.
At first, it looked like part of a fallen tree, but then that "root" moved.
The ground shook, and a huge creature rose from behind the tall plants.
Its body was as large as a two-story house, it had thick brown skin with natural iron plates growing over it.
Two huge tusks came out from both sides of its head.
[Rootbreaker Mammoth]
[Rank: Normal]
The Mammoth roared when it saw One.
One immediately lowered his body, his jaws opened, ready to move forward.
Lian gave a command through the Hive Link to stop.
One moved his antennae in annoyance, Lian gave the command again.
No.
One made a rough sound.
Seris jumped down from his back, she was going to face this one alone again.
"You’re really letting her go alone?" Aren said in disbelief.
"Yes." Lian said.
"So apparently you’re not the only crazy one." Aren looked from the Mammoth to Seris.
The Mammoth lowered its head, its tusks became covered in orange light.
Then it attacked, the ground shook under its feet.
Seris could not stop the attack with raw strength this time, at the last moment, she moved out of its path.
The Mammoth’s tusk passed only a few centimeters from her body and hit the tree trunk behind her.
Part of the trunk split, the young girl attacked its front leg at the same moment and her sword hit its thick skin.
A short spark appeared but it only created a shallow wound and the Mammoth turned its body, its heavy trunk came toward Seris like a whip.
She held her sword in front of herself, the hit lifted her off the ground.
Seris was thrown several meters through the air, before hitting the root, she turned her body and landed with her foot on its surface.
She did not retreat either, this time instead of attacking the protected skin, she moved around the Mammoth.
She looked at its joints, under its stomach, behind its legs and places where the iron plates were thinner.
The Mammoth attacked again, Seris deliberately allowed it to get close and at the moment when the tusks passed from both sides of her, she slid under the Monster’s head.
Her sword hit the soft part of its throat from below, creating a deep wound and the Monster screamed.
It raised its head, that was enough.
Seris stepped on one of the tusks, climbed up it, jumped onto the Monster’s head and held her sword with both hands.
Mana gathered on the blade, the Mammoth tried to throw her down, but the girl kept her balance.
She put the blade into the same wound under its jaw, but from a new angle.
Once.
Twice.
The third strike hit the main nerve.
The Mammoth suddenly stopped, its front legs bent and its huge body fell to the ground with a heavy sound.
Seris jumped down from the Monster’s head.
[You Have Killed Rootbreaker Mammoth Lv.24.]
[EXP Acquired.]
She looked at the panel for several seconds.
"I’m much closer, I should be able to reach Level 19 soon." She then said.
"We won’t be short of Monsters before we reach our destination." Lian answered and then got off to take the corpse.
The days continued like this.
On the first day, the forest was still green and red, on the second day, the light became fewer and on the third day, the water changed.
The narrow rivers that passed between the roots were no longer clear, their color had become dark brown.
Sometimes black spots moved across the surface.
Every time One was about to reach the water, he slowed down and chose another path.
On the fourth day, the sounds disappeared.
First the birds, then the insects, then the small creatures among the bushes.
The forest was still full of trees, but there were no sounds of life anymore.
A silence that seemed to force all living creatures to leave this area.
"I don’t remember this part." Aren looked around for a long time and then said.
"Because the path changed?" Lian asked.
"No." His eyes fell on a tree whose trunk was completely gray on one side.
"Because it was still alive back then."
That sentence made Seris also look around more carefully for a moment.
Lian also looked more carefully, now he could understand better what death meant ... they were slowly reaching areas where the forest was practically dead.
It was as if even living creatures were afraid to live in these areas.
That afternoon, Emberroot opened for the first time.
One climbed up a high slope, at the top, a huge root continued for several kilometers like a natural Ridge.
Lian stood up from One and saw the city in the distance.
Rootcrown.
Even from several kilometers away, it was clear that this city was different from Vhalaris.
Vhalaris was a living and military city, its lines were organized, its towers were active and the lines in all its walls were glowing.
But Rootcrown looked more like a part of the forest itself that had been turned into a city over hundreds of years.
Buildings had been built inside giant roots.
Some towers came out from the trunks, as if they were artificial branches made of Heartwood and stone.
Very old bridges had been built between the high roots.
In the center of the city, there was a huge Heartroot whose very weak golden light could be seen even from a distance.
"Rootcrown." Aren said quietly, it had been a long time since he had last come here, but it was still amazing as always.
Lian moved his eyes across the city, but the eastern part of Rootcrown was different from the rest.
It was darker, several towers were turned off, some walls were cracked and entire districts had no light at all.
The old gates were closed or covered by dry roots, as if part of the city was slowly being swallowed by death.
"Are we passing through here?" Seris asked.

Seris turned back, the second strike hit the same leg and the Monster fell onto one knee.
Seris put her foot on its skull, raised the sword with both hands and drove it directly into the point where the neck and skull connected.
The Alpha’s body shook for several seconds, then became still and she pulled out her sword.
The remaining Hounds lasted only a few more minutes after the Alpha died, when the last Monster fell to the ground, Seris took several calm breaths.
Blood had gathered on the edge of her sword.
System panels appeared in front of her eyes.
[You Have Killed Ember Maw Hound Lv.18.]
[EXP Acquired.]
[You Have Killed Ember Maw Hound Lv.19.]
[EXP Acquired.]
[You Have Killed Ember Maw Alpha Lv.21.]
[EXP Acquired.]
"Was that good?" Lian asked from a distance.
"I got closer." Seris closed the panel.
"Good."
Then the girl cleaned her sword and sat on One again, and the journey continued.
On the second day, the forest was still alive, but less than before, the Ember Crystals that could be seen between the trunks every few hundred meters on the first day were slowly disappearing.
The red light around them became weaker, the humidity was higher and low steam moved between the huge roots.
Around noon, a heavy sound came from ahead of them.
One stopped, ahead of them, a huge root had broken across the path.
At first, it looked like part of a fallen tree, but then that "root" moved.
The ground shook, and a huge creature rose from behind the tall plants.
Its body was as large as a two-story house, it had thick brown skin with natural iron plates growing over it.
Two huge tusks came out from both sides of its head.
[Rootbreaker Mammoth]
[Rank: Normal]
The Mammoth roared when it saw One.
One immediately lowered his body, his jaws opened, ready to move forward.
Lian gave a command through the Hive Link to stop.
One moved his antennae in annoyance, Lian gave the command again.
No.
One made a rough sound.
Seris jumped down from his back, she was going to face this one alone again.
"You’re really letting her go alone?" Aren said in disbelief.
"Yes." Lian said.
"So apparently you’re not the only crazy one." Aren looked from the Mammoth to Seris.
The Mammoth lowered its head, its tusks became covered in orange light.
Then it attacked, the ground shook under its feet.
Seris could not stop the attack with raw strength this time, at the last moment, she moved out of its path.
The Mammoth’s tusk passed only a few centimeters from her body and hit the tree trunk behind her.
Part of the trunk split, the young girl attacked its front leg at the same moment and her sword hit its thick skin.
A short spark appeared but it only created a shallow wound and the Mammoth turned its body, its heavy trunk came toward Seris like a whip.
She held her sword in front of herself, the hit lifted her off the ground.
Seris was thrown several meters through the air, before hitting the root, she turned her body and landed with her foot on its surface.
She did not retreat either, this time instead of attacking the protected skin, she moved around the Mammoth.
She looked at its joints, under its stomach, behind its legs and places where the iron plates were thinner.
The Mammoth attacked again, Seris deliberately allowed it to get close and at the moment when the tusks passed from both sides of her, she slid under the Monster’s head.
Her sword hit the soft part of its throat from below, creating a deep wound and the Monster screamed.
It raised its head, that was enough.
Seris stepped on one of the tusks, climbed up it, jumped onto the Monster’s head and held her sword with both hands.
Mana gathered on the blade, the Mammoth tried to throw her down, but the girl kept her balance.
She put the blade into the same wound under its jaw, but from a new angle.
Once.
Twice.
The third strike hit the main nerve.
The Mammoth suddenly stopped, its front legs bent and its huge body fell to the ground with a heavy sound.
Seris jumped down from the Monster’s head.
[You Have Killed Rootbreaker Mammoth Lv.24.]
[EXP Acquired.]
She looked at the panel for several seconds.
"I’m much closer, I should be able to reach Level 19 soon." She then said.
"We won’t be short of Monsters before we reach our destination." Lian answered and then got off to take the corpse.
The days continued like this.
On the first day, the forest was still green and red, on the second day, the light became fewer and on the third day, the water changed.
The narrow rivers that passed between the roots were no longer clear, their color had become dark brown.
Sometimes black spots moved across the surface.
Every time One was about to reach the water, he slowed down and chose another path.
On the fourth day, the sounds disappeared.
First the birds, then the insects, then the small creatures among the bushes.
The forest was still full of trees, but there were no sounds of life anymore.
A silence that seemed to force all living creatures to leave this area.
"I don’t remember this part." Aren looked around for a long time and then said.
"Because the path changed?" Lian asked.
"No." His eyes fell on a tree whose trunk was completely gray on one side.
"Because it was still alive back then."
That sentence made Seris also look around more carefully for a moment.
Lian also looked more carefully, now he could understand better what death meant ... they were slowly reaching areas where the forest was practically dead.
It was as if even living creatures were afraid to live in these areas.
That afternoon, Emberroot opened for the first time.
One climbed up a high slope, at the top, a huge root continued for several kilometers like a natural Ridge.
Lian stood up from One and saw the city in the distance.
Rootcrown.
Even from several kilometers away, it was clear that this city was different from Vhalaris.
Vhalaris was a living and military city, its lines were organized, its towers were active and the lines in all its walls were glowing.
But Rootcrown looked more like a part of the forest itself that had been turned into a city over hundreds of years.
Buildings had been built inside giant roots.
Some towers came out from the trunks, as if they were artificial branches made of Heartwood and stone.
Very old bridges had been built between the high roots.
In the center of the city, there was a huge Heartroot whose very weak golden light could be seen even from a distance.
"Rootcrown." Aren said quietly, it had been a long time since he had last come here, but it was still amazing as always.
Lian moved his eyes across the city, but the eastern part of Rootcrown was different from the rest.
It was darker, several towers were turned off, some walls were cracked and entire districts had no light at all.
The old gates were closed or covered by dry roots, as if part of the city was slowly being swallowed by death.
"Are we passing through here?" Seris asked.

chapters.title: Chapter 323: The Forgotten Tree I
paragraphs: Lian opened the World Memory Map, the map expanded inside his mind, the main route went through Rootcrown.
But there was another route too.
North of the city, there was a narrow path between two Root Ridges that went directly toward the Forgotten Tree area.
"No." He then answered quietly.
"Are you sure? The First Archive is there, don’t you want to take a look at it?" Aren looked at the city.
Lian said nothing for several seconds, the name Cindar Vael appeared in his mind again.
The only survivor of the final battle, the person who had built the Cindari civilization and perhaps the only person who could be connected to the secret of The Black Silence.
If they had more time, Lian would enter Rootcrown without any doubt.
"Later." But right now, every minute was important.
"Are you sure?"
"If we enter the city now, we either have to fight or hide, and both of them waste time." Lian said.
"Then we’ll go around it." Seris nodded.
One took the northern path, they went around Rootcrown.
Several times, they saw guards in the distance on the towers, but they were so far away that the group was not noticed.
After several hours, the city disappeared behind the huge roots and right after that, the world changed.
At first, the difference was small ... there were fewer leaves ... the branches became drier and then the bark of the trees changed from black and brown to gray.
The small roots on the ground disappeared, the short plants no longer existed and a few kilometers ahead, there was not even any moss.
Then the insects completely disappeared, the air also changed, the smell was weak at first but the farther they went, the stronger it became.
The smell of death.
Not just the smell of a fresh corpse but something much older, the smell of flesh, wet soil, rotten roots and something sweet that reminded them of decay.
One slowed down, his antennae kept moving.
The feelings coming through the Hive Link were clear.
Caution.
Discomfort.
The desire to turn back.
Lian put his hand on the armor on One’s head and One continued.
"This is where it starts." Aren looked at the area and the color of his face had changed.
"The Dead Zone?" Seris whispered while looking at the area in front of them.
"Yes."
They had not traveled very far when Predator’s Instincts gave a warning.
Something moved among the dry roots on the right.
Seris put her hand on her sword, a creature slowly came out from behind a gray trunk.
At first glance, it looked like some kind of large insect.
Six legs.
An extended body.
But half of its body was completely dry, as if it had been dead and mummified for years.
The other half was swollen, its skin was black and shiny and a thick liquid dripped from between its joints, white eyes without pupils were placed on its head.
[Withered Rootcrawler]
[Rank: Mutated]
Seris pulled out her sword.
"Wait." Lian said.
Seris stopped.

Lian got down from One’s back, he did not approach the Rootcrawler and only looked at the black lines on its body, this creature was like the corrupted Monster they had encountered at the beginning of their journey.
So it should be the same type of creature that had become corrupted.
But what was the reason they became corrupted? Something about this picture was not right, he looked at Aren.
"As far as I know, the Corrupted Titan carries The Black Silence and the Forgotten Tree only stops it from awakening, so what is this? Or that corrupted Monster we saw on the first day?"

"I don’t know, I don’t have any guesses either, I only know that some kind of corrupted Monsters live around the tree, and even when I saw one of them that far away from the tree, it was strange to me." Aren stayed silent for several seconds, his eyes moved toward the black liquid and then he added.
"It could be any reason, maybe what we know about the tree is not complete."
Lian did not like this answer, but there was no other answer for now and he looked at Seris.
"Now it’s yours."
Seris moved forward.
The Rootcrawler attacked, the first battle was short, but a few minutes later, more creatures appeared from the Dead Zone.
[Withered Rootcrawler — Lv.22]
[Blackened Thorn Beast — Lv.23]
[Corrupted Ember Stag — Lv.24]
Two Rootcrawlers.
Three Thorn Beasts.
One Ember Stag.
Their appearance was clearly different from normal Monsters.
Not only were their bodies corrupted, their behavior was also wrong.
The first Thorn Beast did not even stop for a moment even though Seris cut off its front leg at the knee.
It rushed toward her on three legs.
The young girl had to directly target its neck, the second one deliberately threw itself onto her sword.
The blade entered its chest, but instead of moving back, the Monster moved forward and tried to grab Seris with both hands.
She had to let go of her sword, move her body to the side and kick the creature away.
The Ember Stag was the strangest of all, its horns had turned black, it had no skin on its face but it was still moving.
Even when Seris cut off one of its horns, it showed no reaction to the pain, it attacked with its head and sent the broken horn toward her stomach like a spear.
The battle did not last long and the Monster finally fell to the ground, although suddenly a thin black root came out from the wound on its neck.
And it quickly moved toward Seris’s leg.
"Watch out!" Predator’s Instincts warned Lian.
Thunder Step.
He appeared between Seris and the corpse.
[Glacial Reaper Claw.]
An ice claw formed on his right hand.
Lian grabbed the black roots, ice spread over them in an instant and their movement stopped.
A few seconds later, the roots became fragile and broke.
"Even after death, it continues." Lian looked at the corpse, this root gave him a bad feeling, he had the feeling that if it managed to enter the body, it could take control of everything.
Is this The Black Silence? Or only a small part of it?
’If something this dangerous is only a small part of it, then how powerful is the real thing?’ He gained a better understanding of this disaster.
But he still had one question, how was he supposed to devour this damn thing? If he devoured this thing, wouldn’t he become corrupted too?
"Then it’s better to leave nothing behind." Seris raised her sword and quickly finished off the last Monster too.
They made sure that nothing was left from the Monsters, they were too dangerous to keep their corpses.
[Level Increased.]
[You Have Reached Level 20.]
Then another notification appeared.
[Evolution Threshold Reached.]
Seris looked at the panel for several seconds.
"You reached it?" Lian noticed.
"Yeah, Level 20, I also got an Evolution Quest."
"Good, what does it need? Is it easy?" Of course, the chance that an Evolution Quest for a five-star class would be easy was almost impossible, but it was definitely easier than his.
"I’ll tell you later." Seris stared at him for a moment, then closed the panel.
"Why?" Lian raised an eyebrow.
"Whenever you tell me, I’ll tell you too."
Lian said nothing, the reason she did not tell him was because the Quest was so crazy that it could not be explained, in the end, he shrugged and did not care.
From that point on, their speed decreased even more, not because of tiredness but because of the land itself.
Dry roots came out of the ground like walls, deep cracks cut across the path in some places.
Sometimes black liquid flowed through the cracks in the ground.
"Don’t touch it." Aren warned every time before they reached them.
Lian froze the narrow parts with Glacial Reaper Claw so One could pass over them.
In other places, they went around the path, the farther they went, the more they felt a strange pressure on their Mana.
It was not something like Suppression, it was more like a feeling of heaviness, as if the air itself did not want Mana to move inside it.
One had become more nervous.
None of them felt good here.
"Do you feel it?" Seris said after some time.
"Yeah, it feels bad and I don’t like it." Lian answered.
Predator’s Instincts did not show any specific enemy, but the whole area seemed wrong.
Every root, every crack, every piece of soil felt like there was something under them that had not moved yet.
After hours of slow progress, they passed the last row of dead trees.
One passed between two broken trunks, and suddenly the forest ended.
A huge gray plain was in front of them, no plants grew there.
No bushes.
No trees.
Not even grass.
The ground looked like ash.
Black cracks spread across the entire surface, a very thin mist moved close to the ground.
And in the center of this plain ... stood the Forgotten Tree.
"We finally made it ..."
One stopped right there, for several seconds no one spoke.
Even Lian, who thought he was ready for its size, raised his eyes.
The tree was so huge that the normal meaning of the word "tree" did not seem enough for it.
Its trunk was hundreds of meters wide, its surface rose like the wall of an ancient city and its branches spread toward the sky at a great height.
Some of them were so large that a small city could be built on them, but most of them were dry.
The huge branches disappeared into the mist like broken pillars of a sky temple.
The bark of the trunk was cracked, there were cracks several meters wide across its surface.
Very weak white and golden light came out from some of the cracks, a weak sign that something inside the tree was still alive.
But from some other cracks, a dark liquid came down.
Not in a large amount, only thin black lines that moved across the dry bark.
Thousands of roots came out from around the trunk, some entered the ground, while others continued across the surface like huge walls.
Some were completely broken, some were dry and gray and a small number still had very weak lines of golden light.
The tree was not dead ... not yet.
But there was no need for a System notification to understand that it was dying, it was clear even with their eyes that it was not only dying, but also suffering.
A tree that was suffering.
Aren remained completely still on One’s back, his lips opened for a moment, but no sound came out.
"Very, much worse than I thought." He stared at the Forgotten Tree for some time.
One suddenly moved his antennae forward, his body lowered slightly.
Predator’s Instincts did not give a clear warning.
"Hmm? What is that?" But Lian saw something near the base of the tree, at first he thought it was just another root.
But its shape was different from the others, at a point near the center of the trunk, thousands of smaller roots had gathered from around it.
They all reached one point, like veins connected to a heart.
Lian got down from One, Seris also came down after him.
Aren carefully got down and kept his distance.
Lian slowly moved forward, the roots in this area were different from the others, they were not completely dead, thin lines of white light moved inside them.
Some were transparent, some were golden and all of them were wrapped around something in the center.
A cocoon.
It was almost two meters long, made of white and semi-transparent strands, weak golden light passed through them.
At first glance, Lian thought it might be the real Core of the Forgotten Tree.
Or the part that was still alive, but then something inside the cocoon moved.
And the young Vorhelm stopped right there.
"What is that?" Seris took one step forward, she had also noticed the strange cocoon.
Lian did not answer, the surface of the Cocoon was so transparent in several parts that something inside could be seen.
A tall and thin shadow, shaped like a human body.
He moved closer so he could take a better look, the strands of light moved aside.
Hair appeared, then one hand, human fingers...the body of a girl was floating inside the Cocoon!
Her eyes were closed. Very thin roots were wrapped around her arms, legs and body.
Lian frowned, he had a strange feeling, her face could not be seen completely yet but she gave him a strangely familiar feeling.
He took one more step forward, golden light moved across the surface of the Cocoon and for only a moment, the white strands moved away from the girl’s face.
The girl’s face became visible and Lian became completely still, then he quietly said a name he had never expected to think of here.
"Selina...?"

chapters.title: Chapter 324: Surrounded On All Sides
paragraphs: While Lian and Seris had reached the Forgotten Tree, the situation in Vhalaris was not going well either.
The sound of hammers hitting Steel could be heard in Ashfall from sunrise until midnight.
The area that a few days ago had only been a temporary place for the Outsiders was now almost impossible to recognize.
The three main bridges were covered with several layers of Barricades, the first barriers were made of wood and metal.
Behind them were heavy Steel plates.
And behind the second layer, the Mages had built Barrier Nodes that could create several Barriers one after another if an attack happened.
The captured Cindari Ballistas had been installed on the high towers.
Some of the Mages had worked on their structures for three nights without proper rest, trying to make the Cindari targeting system work with human Mana.
Rootspire was no longer only a prison.
The upper floors had been turned into storage areas for ammunition, Potions and equipment.
The safer lower floors were being used to keep the prisoners.
Maelor, Kael and Tharos were being kept in three separate areas.
None of them were allowed to communicate with each other and they were under the strictest security, and Cassian had almost completely redesigned the map of Ashfall and the surrounding areas.
Alleys that looked normal at first were now Kill Zones.
Explosives had been placed under the stone roads.
Heavy Barricades had been prepared above some paths so they could fall by cutting a rope.
There were Formations at several entrances that could lock the legs of enemy forces for a few seconds.
For an enemy entering the city, Ashfall was no longer a district, it was a huge trap.
Marcus had divided all the Warriors and Tanks into organized groups.
Every group had a commander, every bridge had reserve forces and every Choke Point had a clear retreat path.
Ethan had formed several Strike Teams that would attack the enemy from the side paths if they passed through the defensive line.
Seraphina was in charge of the quick response force.
If any part of the defense was in danger of collapsing, she and the strongest remaining Awakeners would be sent there.
Liana and Shadow Wolf patrolled at night.
Shadow Wolf moved through the shadows of the buildings and checked paths that normal Awakeners could not safely enter.
The Healers had also built three temporary treatment centers.
The Potions had been divided and organized.
The older wounded had been treated as much as possible.
In terms of preparation, the situation was much better than what they had expected a few days ago, but there was one strange thing.
No army had arrived.
Rindo was standing in front of the map inside the council room, his finger on Cinderhold.
"Maelor said two days for the main forces, and he said the fast forces would arrive even earlier."

"And according to what Lian said, at least one of the armies should have arrived by now, it’s been three days since I talked to him! So why is there still no news?" The President of the Student Council had a bad feeling.
He did not know where this feeling came from, but he did not like it.
No one had an answer.
They knew the first force that was supposed to reach Vhalaris no longer existed.
Six hundred soldiers of the Cinderhold Advance Legion had encountered Lian in a part of Emberroot a few days ago.
And that encounter had ended so completely that not even one organized unit was left to give an exact report.
But according to what they had guessed, the main army of Cinderhold should have arrived by now.
"Every extra hour they give us is good for us." Rindo took a slow breath.
And it really was.
Every extra hour meant one more Barrier, one more Trap, one less wounded soldier, one more Potion ready.
Some Awakeners had even gotten several hours of real rest.
Food was being given out in the central area, and several Warriors were sitting beside the walls.
The Mages had slept after their long shifts, and even the city had found something close to peace for a few hours.
Ethan was sitting on one of the main Barricades and eating an apple from the Cindari storage.
"I built all these defenses so that no one would attack?" he said to Marcus, who was checking the position of the Tanks.
"You barely built anything." Marcus did not even turn around.
"I gave them moral support." Ethan took another bite of the apple.
"The biggest threat to our morale is also you." Cassian, who was passing beside them, said.
"Everyone is so ungrateful today."
For a few seconds, even Marcus smiled.
It was at that peaceful moment that the sound of fast footsteps came from the entrance of the area.
They hoped this peace could last a little longer so Lian and Seris could return with good news, but unfortunately they were not going to be that lucky.
An Awakener Scout entered at full speed.
His clothes were covered in dust, he was breathing heavily and the color of his face was also not something that looked like good news.
"President!"
"What happened?" Rindo immediately came out of the council building.
"Military movement has been seen! Enemy! Enemy!" The Scout put his hands on his knees and took several breaths.
The atmosphere around them changed at once and tension filled the entire area.
"How many?"
The Scout did not answer for a few seconds, he was still in a state of shock and did not know how he should answer.
"How many?" Rindo frowned.
"I don’t know."
That answer from a professional Scout was much worse than any number.
"What do you mean you don’t know?" Cassian took one step forward.
"There are too many." He paused for a moment and then added a sentence that destroyed all the remaining peace in the area.
"And they are not coming from only one direction."
Less than a few minutes later, Rindo, Seraphina, Cassian, Marcus, Ethan and Liana climbed the stairs of one of the highest towers in Vhalaris.
The Scout was also with them.
When they reached the upper platform, the Emberroot forest could be seen for kilometers in front of them.
At first, nothing seemed strange.
Huge trunks.
Mist.
Scattered lights.
"There." Cassian saw the first movement and pointed to the east.
Light.
One.
Then ten.
Then hundreds.
Organized flames were moving between the trees, and the Forge flags and the Cinderhold forked flame could be seen from far away.
"The main army of Cinderhold." Marcus said quietly, this was the army they had been waiting for for a long time and there was no need to worry.
"That’s only one." But the Scout spoke, and everyone turned toward the southeast.
It took a few moments for their eyes to adjust to the distance, then more lights appeared.
Another column.
War Beasts.
Carriages.
Different flags.
Emberwell!
Two of the three armies had appeared! And before they had a chance to react in any way ...
"They are there too." Liana looked toward the north.
In the northern mist, a third army was moving.
Lighter, faster, and the flags of Ashenreach could be seen above the lines.
And among one of the central columns, there were several smaller flags with the old symbol of Rootcrown, Elite forces.
None of the armies had reached the walls of Vhalaris yet, but it was clear what they were doing.
They were spreading out.
East.
North.
South.
They were slowly closing the exit routes, while armored War Beasts moved in the back lines.
Siege Engines could be seen among the columns.
Dozens of Ballistas and Mage Units whose Mana gathering could be seen even from this distance.
Rindo said nothing for a while, and Ethan, who almost always had something to say, was silent this time.
"This isn’t a Legion anymore, there are at least three thousand of them, maybe more." Marcus said quietly.
Seraphina moved her eyes across the horizon.
From east to south, from south to north.
"They are surrounding the city."
"How far are the front forces?" Rindo asked the Scout.
"About thirty minutes, if the main force keeps this speed, they will complete the circle around the city by night."

"So that’s why they didn’t come, they were waiting, they didn’t want to attack one by one, they waited for several cities to arrive at the same time." Cassian said with some mockery at their own mistake.
Now the strange delay of the past few days made sense.
They had thought they had bought time, but the Cindari had also used that time.
To gather an army that could surround all of Vhalaris instead of simply taking back one district.
Rindo looked down.
The Barricades, the captured Ballistas, the Barrier Nodes, the formation of the Warriors and everything they had built over the past few days.
Until a few minutes ago, Ashfall had looked like a strong fortress.
Now, against thousands of soldiers and several united armies, it suddenly looked much smaller.
"I think our guests have finally arrived." Ethan finally broke the silence.
No one laughed.
Seraphina said nothing and only looked toward the east, in the direction where Lian had gone, and for a moment a simple thought passed through her mind.
Come back sooner.
But almost at the same moment, she realized this wish was wrong.
Lian should not come back.
If he returned from the Forgotten Tree because of this war, they might keep Vhalaris, but they would lose the Main Quest.
And if they failed the Main Quest, the Cindari armies would become their smallest problem.
So if Lian did not return ... they would have to survive without him ...
but was that even possible? Even if Lian were here, victory against this army would be impossible.
