chapters.title: Chapter 325: The Forgotten Tree II
paragraphs: "Selina...?" The name left Lian’s mouth almost without him realizing it.
For a few seconds, he did not move, not because he was sure, but exactly the opposite.
His mind was trying to find a reason why what he was seeing could not be real.
Maybe it was only a resemblance.
Maybe the weak golden light of the Cocoon had made the face inside look familiar.
Maybe the half-transparent roots and white strands had changed the shape of the face, but the more he looked, the less likely it seemed that he was mistaken.
Lian took one step forward.
The surface of the Cocoon in front of him shone like a layer of living glass.
Thousands of thin white strands had come out from the roots of the Forgotten Tree and wrapped around it, some as thin as hair and some thicker than a human finger.
A very weak golden light moved inside them.
He looked at the girl inside the Cocoon through the strands.
Her hair.
The shape of her cheeks.
The line of her jaw.
Even part of the clothes that could still be seen under the half-transparent roots, there was no doubt left anymore.
It was the same girl.
Selina.
One of the Awakener who had entered this Special Area with them.
The same person Liana had asked about many times since the group was separated.
The same girl they had thought was probably lost somewhere in one of the forests or had been trapped with another group.
But no one had even imagined that they would find her here.
In the center of the Dead Zone and directly at the base of the Forgotten Tree, inside a Cocoon connected to thousands of the tree’s roots.
"Do you know her?" Seris stepped forward from beside Lian, her eyes fixed on the girl’s face inside the Cocoon.
She had never seen Selina before, so it was normal that she did not recognize her.
"Who is that girl?" Aren, who was standing a few meters behind them and still did not dare to get too close to the roots around them, asked.
Lian did not answer for a few seconds, then slowly nodded.
"Selina."
"The girl Liana was looking for?" Seris immediately remembered the name.
"Yeah."
The young Pendragon looked at the Cocoon again, this time the expression on her face completely changed... disbelief.
Aren also frowned, all three of them had almost reached the same conclusion at the same time.
Something about this scene was very wrong.
Selina should have been trapped somewhere in the Special Area.
Maybe injured, maybe surrounded by Monsters, maybe captured by the Cindari.
But not here, not in the heart of the most mysterious part of this world.
And definitely not inside a Cocoon that clearly seemed to have been created with the Forgotten Tree’s involvement.
"Do you have any idea what’s going on?" Lian took his eyes off the Cocoon and looked at Aren.
Aren did not answer immediately, he took a few steps forward, enough to see better, but still kept his distance from the white strands.
He looked at the roots connected to the Cocoon, then at Selina and then back at the huge trunk of the Forgotten Tree.
"No." He slowly shook his head.
"Nothing?"
"Nothing, in everything I read about the Forgotten Tree, there was no mention of anything like this, not a Cocoon, not a Human Vessel, not the tree keeping someone inside itself."
Lian did not like this answer, but the problem was that he also did not know anything more.
He moved closer to the Cocoon again, this time he was only one step away from it, and from this close, more details could be seen.
Thin roots passed through the surface of the Cocoon and rested on Selina’s skin.
Some were wrapped around her wrists, some around her neck, and several very thin strands were connected to the back of her head and spine deep inside the Cocoon.
Selina’s chest was moving up and down very slowly.
She was alive, at least from what they could see.
Lian raised his hand to touch it.
"Are you sure you want to touch it?" Seris immediately said.
"No, but I need to check it." And even so, he moved his hand forward.
His fingers touched the half-transparent surface of the Cocoon, and at that exact moment, something inside his body reacted.
Lian did not pull his hand back, but his expression changed.
The feeling he received from the Cocoon was unlike any Mana he had touched before.
Not heat, not cold, not raw energy, not corruption like the one he had seen inside the Corrupted Hollowroot Behemoth.
This thing... was alive.
But not in the same way as Selina, it felt like something was being formed.
Something that was not complete yet, something that did not have a clear name yet, but something that was becoming an independent existence.
Before he could think about it, the egg inside his Storage Space suddenly reacted and started shaking.
A feeling of hunger!
The same feeling that appeared whenever he got close to the corpses of Monsters that could be devoured.
[The Devourer Egg is hungry and thinks it has found a good meal!]
But before Lian could do anything, the egg suddenly pulled back.
It was as if the egg’s own instinct had told it, not yet.
Then the System reacted, and a panel appeared in front of his eyes.
[Unknown Lifeform Detected.]
Lian frowned.
[Identification in Progress...]
[Identification Complete.]
[Name: Black Silence Fetus]
[Host: Selina]
[Rank: ???]
[Level: ???]
[State: Gestating]
Lian became completely still, his eyes stayed on the name for a moment.
Black Silence Fetus.
A fetus... something that had not been born yet.
The System made the panel visible to Seris as well, probably because she was close enough to the Cocoon and had received the Quest related to the area.
She also said nothing for a few seconds, and then a second panel appeared.
[Calamity Gestation Detected.]
[The Black Silence Fetus Is Approaching Birth.]
[Gestation Progress: 63.7%]
The number stayed still for a moment, and then another warning appeared.
[Warning.]
[Upon Completion, a New Calamity Vessel Will Be Born.]
This line was even worse than the previous name, Lian took his eyes off the panel and looked at Selina.
New Calamity Vessel.
That meant the System was not saying that Selina was going to become The Black Silence itself.
It was saying that she was going to become a new Vessel, but a new Vessel for what?
The Corrupted Titan was still alive.
According to everything they knew until now, the Titan was considered the current Vessel of The Black Silence.
The Forgotten Tree also prevented the Titan from awakening through its existence.
So why was another Vessel being born inside the roots of the Forgotten Tree?
Lian started thinking faster, was The Black Silence reproducing itself?
Had a part of it separated from the Titan and entered Selina?
Was the Forgotten Tree itself pulling the Calamity out of the Titan and transferring it into a new body?
If that was the case... why Selina? Why a human? Why now? How was that even possible? It had barely been a month since they entered this world.
So how exactly had Selina suddenly become the Vessel of a Calamity?
Lian looked at the thousands of roots connected to the Cocoon again, all of them came from parts of the Forgotten Tree that still had light... parts that were still alive.
That meant the tree was not only allowing the Cocoon to exist, it was probably actively feeding it.
"What’s going on?" Aren, who could not see any of the System panels, finally could not hold himself back anymore.
Lian did not answer for a few seconds and pulled his hand away from the Cocoon, then finally added.
"This girl is turning into something, a Black Silence Fetus."
"What?" For a moment, Aren seemed unable to understand the meaning of the words, and then the color left his face.
"A new Calamity Holder is being formed inside this Cocoon." Seris answered simply.
"How? Didn’t you say she was your friend? Then what happened to her?" Aren immediately looked at Selina, his eyes opening wider.
"You’re asking me? Who am I supposed to ask?" Lian answered with sarcasm, but his tone showed helplessness more than sarcasm.
He really had no idea.
Nothing.
How had Selina gotten here?
Who had brought her here? Had the Forgotten Tree itself taken her?
Had The Black Silence chosen her? Had the Titan somehow affected her from beneath the Giant’s Graveyard?
There was no clear answer.
Seris’s expression also became cold, very cold, and her hand slowly moved to the handle of her sword.
The sound of the blade leaving its sheath could clearly be heard in the silence, and Lian immediately looked at her.
"Then we have to destroy it before it is complete." The girl said slowly.
"No." Lian stepped between her and the Cocoon without hesitation.
Seris stopped, her sword was lowered, but she was ready to move.
"Lian Vorhelm! This is not the place for emotions."

[Identification Complete.]
[Name: Black Silence Fetus]
[Host: Selina]
[Rank: ???]
[Level: ???]
[State: Gestating]
Lian became completely still, his eyes stayed on the name for a moment.
Black Silence Fetus.
A fetus... something that had not been born yet.
The System made the panel visible to Seris as well, probably because she was close enough to the Cocoon and had received the Quest related to the area.
She also said nothing for a few seconds, and then a second panel appeared.
[Calamity Gestation Detected.]
[The Black Silence Fetus Is Approaching Birth.]
[Gestation Progress: 63.7%]
The number stayed still for a moment, and then another warning appeared.
[Warning.]
[Upon Completion, a New Calamity Vessel Will Be Born.]
This line was even worse than the previous name, Lian took his eyes off the panel and looked at Selina.
New Calamity Vessel.
That meant the System was not saying that Selina was going to become The Black Silence itself.
It was saying that she was going to become a new Vessel, but a new Vessel for what?
The Corrupted Titan was still alive.
According to everything they knew until now, the Titan was considered the current Vessel of The Black Silence.
The Forgotten Tree also prevented the Titan from awakening through its existence.
So why was another Vessel being born inside the roots of the Forgotten Tree?
Lian started thinking faster, was The Black Silence reproducing itself?
Had a part of it separated from the Titan and entered Selina?
Was the Forgotten Tree itself pulling the Calamity out of the Titan and transferring it into a new body?
If that was the case... why Selina?
Why a human?
Why now?
How was that even possible?
It had barely been a month since they entered this world.
So how exactly had Selina suddenly become the Vessel of a Calamity?
Lian looked at the thousands of roots connected to the Cocoon again, all of them came from parts of the Forgotten Tree that still had light... parts that were still alive.
That meant the tree was not only allowing the Cocoon to exist, it was probably actively feeding it.
"What’s going on?" Aren, who could not see any of the System panels, finally could not hold himself back anymore.
Lian did not answer for a few seconds and pulled his hand away from the Cocoon, then finally added.
"This girl is turning into something, a Black Silence Fetus."
"What?" For a moment, Aren seemed unable to understand the meaning of the words, and then the color left his face.
"A new Calamity Holder is being formed inside this Cocoon." Seris answered simply.
"How?
Didn’t you say she was your friend?
Then what happened to her?" Aren immediately looked at Selina, his eyes opening wider.
"You’re asking me?
Who am I supposed to ask?" Lian answered with sarcasm, but his tone showed helplessness more than sarcasm.
He really had no idea.
Nothing.
How had Selina gotten here?
Who had brought her here?
Had the Forgotten Tree itself taken her?
Had The Black Silence chosen her?
Had the Titan somehow affected her from beneath the Giant’s Graveyard?
There was no clear answer.
Seris’s expression also became cold, very cold, and her hand slowly moved to the handle of her sword.
The sound of the blade leaving its sheath could clearly be heard in the silence, and Lian immediately looked at her.
"Then we have to destroy it before it is complete." The girl said slowly.
"No." Lian stepped between her and the Cocoon without hesitation.
Seris stopped, her sword was lowered, but she was ready to move.
"Lian Vorhelm!
This is not the place for emotions."

chapters.title: Chapter 326: The Forgotten Tree III
paragraphs: "It’s not the time for emotions." Seris’s tone was calm, but it was more serious than something that could be ignored.
"If she really is turning into a Calamity Vessel, every second she stays alive is dangerous."
Lian said nothing, and the girl continued.

"63.7%, we don’t even know how fast it is increasing, it might take a day, it might take an hour, and if it reaches one hundred percent and something comes out of that Cocoon, we may not be able to stop it anymore." Her sword rose slightly.
"We can end it now, before it is born."
Aren looked between the two of them, even without knowing Selina, he could not deny Seris’s logic.
If a creature connected to The Black Silence was being born, then from a logical point of view, destroying it before birth was the most reasonable decision.
"I told you I won’t let you kill her." But Lian did not move, his gaze became colder, his tone left no room for arguing or refusing.
Seris’s eyes also became cold for a moment, and the air between them became heavy.
Not because Seris really wanted to fight Lian, but because both of them knew that the wrong decision could cost much more than Selina’s life.
But Lian’s reason for refusing was not only their friendship, and it was not even only the possibility of saving Selina.
[Evolution Quest: Devour The Black Silence.]
He looked at the Cocoon again, if his guess was correct, The Black Silence was gathering inside Selina for some reason.
Maybe she was the next Vessel, maybe the Calamity was being transferred from the Titan into her body.
Maybe the Forgotten Tree was trying to gather the main part of The Black Silence inside a new Vessel.
Lian did not know... but he knew one thing.
If Seris destroyed the Cocoon now, several things could happen.
The Black Silence could be released.
It could return to the Titan.
It could spread through the area.
Or maybe it could be destroyed together with Selina.
That last possibility was not acceptable to Lian, he needed the Calamity, for Devouring it, and his Evolution was impossible without Devouring one of the Five Calamities.
If The Black Silence was destroyed right now, the only Calamity available to him might disappear forever.
"We still don’t know what will happen if we destroy the Cocoon." He finally said.
"And we don’t know what will happen if we leave it alive." Seris answered.

"That’s true, but if we break the Cocoon, whatever is inside might be released, The Black Silence might return to the Titan and the condition of the Forgotten Tree might become worse." He paused for a moment.
"And there may still be a way to save Selina."
Seris looked at him for a few seconds, it was clear that she felt Lian had not told her his whole reason.
But her own argument was also not complete.
Killing Selina without understanding how the Cocoon worked could be just as dangerous as keeping her alive.
In the end, the blade lowered, and she put the sword back into its sheath.
"Fine, but only for now." Her tone was still cold.
Lian said nothing, but he nodded slightly to show his thanks.
"So what are you going to do now?" Seris continued.
"I’ll find a way, but before that, I need to understand exactly what happened."
Aren put his hand on his chin, he said nothing for a while and then suddenly spoke.
"Rootcrown."
"What?" Lian looked at him.
"What you are looking for might be in the First Archive." He pointed toward the place where Rootcrown was located behind the dead forest.
"If there is any information left about the Forgotten Tree, Calamity Vessels, Cindar Vael or even this Cocoon, it will be there."

Lian thought for a few seconds, earlier he had intentionally avoided Rootcrown, they did not have the time, every encounter with the Guards, every time they had to hide and every fight could take several hours from them.
But now, without information, he could do almost nothing.
He could not destroy the Cocoon, he could not pull Selina out and he could not Devour The Black Silence.
And he did not even know what role the Forgotten Tree had in all of this.
The First Archive might be their only hope, the only place where they could find the information they needed.
"Looks like there is no other choice, I’ll go to Rootcrown."
"Should we come too?" Seris immediately asked.
"No, you stay here, if the Gestation Progress changes, if the Cocoon reacts or if more Monsters come close, someone needs to stay here." He then looked at One.
"One stays too."
The huge ant moved its antennae, a short feeling of displeasure came through the Hive Link.
Lian put his hand on its head.
"I’ll get there faster alone." He nodded.
Of course, the only reason he wanted to go alone was not this, his goal was not to fight all the Cindari in that city just to reach the Archive.
Doing that would waste too much time and could be dangerous, so he planned to use Abyss Veil.
He turned around and then started moving without saying anything.
[Fallen Wolf Speed.]
Mana gathered in his leg muscles, making his body lighter.
It had been a long time since he had used this skill, naturally, this was because with his current natural speed, he did not need speed-boosting skills.
But now it could help him again.
Lian started running, within a few seconds he moved away from the Cocoon, the Dead Zone moved backward under his feet.
At places where large cracks or dead roots blocked the path, he activated Thunder Step.
Blue light appeared among the gray land for a moment, then disappeared again.
The several-hour path that One had carefully traveled was now being crossed much faster under Lian’s Speed of more than 500 and the combination of Fallen Wolf Speed and Thunder Step.
The gray area ended, and the dead trees changed into the half-alive Emberroot.
Color returned to the forest.
First dark gray, then brown and then the red lines of Ember Crystal.
Finally, the towers of Rootcrown appeared between the branches.
Lian slowed down before reaching the city’s area, the Guards could be seen on the towers.
He stopped behind one of the huge roots and controlled his breathing.
[Abyss Veil.]

The change started from that moment, and it did not take long before his entire presence disappeared from sight, no visible trace of him remained and he had practically disappeared from everyone’s eyes.
He moved, the northern gate of Rootcrown was in front of him.
Six Guards stood on both sides, one of them turned his head toward Lian for a moment.
The Guard looked for a few seconds, his eyes passed directly over the place where Lian was standing and then he looked back at the other path.
He passed them without making a sound, and when he entered Rootcrown, the difference from Vhalaris felt much greater than it had from far away.
Old inscriptions could be seen on the walls, and even parts of them had been worn down by thousands of years.
In the small squares, there were Statues of ancient figures.
But one face appeared more often than the others.
A tall man wearing a simple robe, holding a sword in one hand and a golden root in the other.
Cindar Vael.
In most parts of the city, instead of the red Ember Flame of Vhalaris, calm white flames burned inside the lanterns.
Rootcrown felt less like a living capital and more like a huge temple for the past of the Cindari.
Lian did not slow down, he opened the World Memory Map in his mind and the main path went directly toward the center of the city.
The First Archive was located beneath a building that the map listed as.
[Lord’s Root Palace]
The home and ruling center of the ruler of Rootcrown, and naturally, one of the most protected places in the city.
Lian chose the side paths.
Abyss Veil allowed him to pass most of the Guards.
But when he reached the inner ring of the Palace, another problem appeared, there was a protective gate that seemed to be opened only by certain people.
He tried to pass through it, but it was impossible and he had to wait for a while until one of the people who seemed to have the right to open the gate finally appeared.
At the same time as that Cindari opened the gate, Lian entered the Palace.
From there, the path went downward.
Stairs, circular hallways, and the deeper he went, the fewer but stronger the Guards became.
And finally, he reached a huge door.

chapters.title: Chapter 327: The Forgotten Tree IV
paragraphs: Lian stood in front of it and looked at the large door, unfortunately, passing through this door was not easy either.
Abyss Veil could hide his presence from the Guards.
But the locking mechanisms of the gate were not living things, they did not care how hidden his presence was, and to pass through, he first had to be able to open the door.
And opening the door required him to be recognized by the locking mechanism.
"Looks like I have no choice." Lian placed his palm on one of the seals.
He activated Cataclysm Pulse.
But not like in battle. This time, he only sent a very thin wave of destruction into the structure.
The wave moved through the door.
He controlled the pressure, if he used too much power, the entire gate would explode and the Alarm would activate.
That was why, instead of breaking it, he only disrupted one of the internal connections of the locking mechanism, and the golden light shook for a moment and then went out.
The main lock became loose.
Lian opened the door only enough for himself to pass through the gap, then closed it again.
When he entered the First Archive, he stopped for a moment.
The space was huge, much larger than he had expected from outside, hundreds of pillars stood in the main hall.
Between them, shelves rose several meters high.
But the Archive did not only contain books, there were thousands of stone tablets and Crystal Memories with weak white and blue lights moving inside them.
Pieces of tree bark with ancient writings carved into them.
Maps so old that even the shapes of the three forests were different on them.
Broken Artifacts, rusty swords, and seals belonging to Kingdoms that no longer existed.
But his surprise only lasted for a few minutes and Lian quickly started searching.
First, Forgotten Tree.
He found a lot of information, its estimated age, its role in the Water Cycle of the three forests, and its connection to the world’s Mana Channels.
Its connection to Giant’s Graveyard, but there was nothing about the Cocoon.
Then Black Silence.
The results became fewer, many documents only mentioned it indirectly.
"Corruption."
"The Final Plague."
"Silence."
"The Enemy Without Form."
But there was no complete explanation, especially about the Vessel and the fetus, there was nothing.
Lian went after Cindar Vael and found more information.
First Founder.
Last Survivor.
Builder of Rootcrown.
Bearer of the First Root.

But details about the Final Battle? Almost nothing, the records were either incomplete or parts of them had been intentionally erased, as if someone did not want any trace of the final battle between the leaders of the ancient civilizations of this world and the Corrupted Titan to remain.
Hours passed.
Lian left the main hall behind and entered the second section, but still found nothing.
Then the personal Archive of the old Rootwardens.
War maps, reports about Forgotten Tree, records of Expedition deaths, but the more he searched, the clearer the problem became.
Everything that actually came close to answering his questions suddenly stopped.
It was as if someone had recorded history up to a certain point and then drawn a blade across all the important lines.
There was not even a direct mention of the Black Silence Fetus.
Even the real reason for Forgotten Tree drying up was not recorded, as if no one really knew the reason for it, so it had never been recorded.
Finally, Lian put the last book back in its place and stood there alone for a few seconds, then sighed.
"Nothing." He felt that he might have really reached a dead end.
Why was Selina there?
Why was Forgotten Tree keeping her inside the Cocoon?
How had Black Silence entered her body?
Was the Titan still the main Vessel? Was the Calamity being transferred?
Was the death of the tree caused by this transfer or was it related to something else?
And even if he understood all of them, how was he supposed to Devour The Black Silence?
The Quest appeared in his mind like a bad joke.
[Devour The Black Silence.]
Lian pressed his lips together, having an abnormal class that had never existed before also came with problems like this.
He basically did not know what he was facing or what he should do, he was completely in the dark and had no guidance, he had to discover and learn everything by himself.
For a moment, he looked at the huge shelves of the Archive, the information of hundreds of years of civilization was here.
But exactly what he needed did not exist, or worse, had been intentionally removed.
Lian decided not to waste any more time, if the First Archive had no answer, he had to return to Forgotten Tree.
Maybe the Cocoon itself would reveal more information as the Gestation progressed.
"If there is no other choice, I will have to agree to destroying the Cocoon." He thought to himself, if no one stopped him, they might face something they had no ability to resist.
As he was turning to leave, Predator’s Instincts suddenly reacted.
"This?" Lian went silent.
Three presences were approaching.
This time, the Skill was not giving him a simple warning of danger.
After Predator’s Instincts evolved, Lian could also sense the biological patterns of living creatures within a limited range.
He focused, three blood flows could be seen behind the western wall.
Not really with his eyes, but as an instinctive image in his mind.
Three Cindari, two were normal and one was stronger, but none of them were strong enough to be considered a serious threat to him.
They seemed to be here to patrol and nothing more.
He did not care much, he could move to the side of the hall and let them pass, there was no need to kill them.
But at that exact moment, he sensed something else.

Lian became completely still, Predator’s Instincts was still active, three blood flows were approaching the Archive from the hallway, after reaching a certain point and checking the surroundings, they turned around and left the area again.
Just as he had guessed, they were only a security patrol.
"But what is this?" But something else caught his attention, there was another flow.
Not in front of him or behind the wall, but below, much deeper below.
Lian slowly looked at the floor of the Archive, for a few seconds he thought he had sensed it wrong and focused again.
The flow existed.
But it was weak, very weak, something like blood was moving under the ground.
The problem was that no specific living creature could be sensed.
There was no beating heart, no breathing, only a weak flow, like veins that were still working inside a dead body.
Lian opened the World Memory Map, the map spread out in front of him.
Lord’s Root Palace.
According to the map, the lowest floor should be the Archive itself, there should be nothing deeper than this.
According to the map, the First Archive was the lowest built space in this area.
"Then what is down there?" Lian looked at the floor again.
Predator’s Instincts was not wrong, the flow existed.
Unless—
"A hidden floor." His eyes narrowed slightly.
Lian followed the underground flow, the image of blood in his mind passed under the floor and moved toward the northern part of the hall.
He slowly moved between the shelves, the flow finally became concentrated under one of the Statues.
He stood in front of it, the Statue was larger than all the other statues in the Archive.
Cindar Vael.
The Founder stood with one hand on his sword and the other around a golden root.
Lian examined the base of the Statue, there was no handle, no gap, or anything like that.
"I don’t have time for these games."
He placed his palm on the stone.
[Cataclysm Pulse.]
But this time, he did not release the wave outward, he sent it underground.
The wave passed through the layers of stone, the reflection came back and most of the floor was completely solid, but there was an empty space under the Statue!
"Found you." A short smile appeared on Lian’s lips.
He pushed his fingers into the very thin gap between the base of the Statue and the floor, the stone would not even move for a normal human.
Lian applied force, his Power increased, the muscles in his arms and shoulders tightened, and suddenly a very quiet sound came from under the stone.
Then the huge stone panel rose several centimeters.
At that exact moment, the hidden mechanisms around it lit up and golden lines spread across the floor.
The Alarm was activating.
Lian frowned, he gathered Thunder Calamity on two fingers at the lowest intensity possible.
A thin lightning bolt entered it, only one precise current, the first connection burned, the second shut down.
The third resisted for a moment, he applied more pressure, the lightning passed through it and it burned as well, in short, the Alarm never fully activated.
Lian lifted the stone panel higher, darkness could be seen underneath.
A staircase!
A narrow staircase that went straight down, deeper than anything that existed on the World Memory Map.
He entered without hesitation and lowered the panel as much as possible behind him.
Abyss Veil was still active.
Although Lian did not know that the three Cindari who had been patrolling had noticed those strange vibrations and were quickly coming to check.
At the same time, Lian was going down the stairs, after a few meters, the structure of the area changed.
The walls were made of black stone, dry white roots came out from the cracks.
There were very old writings on the walls and their language was different even from the writings in the city.
It was clear that they had been written in a much more ancient language, a language that was probably no longer used.
There was no longer any smell of the Archive, this place was not a library, it had an old smell and a slight smell of death and dead bodies.
Predator’s Instincts continued to follow the underground flow.
The deeper he went, the clearer the image became, but it also became stranger.
There was still no heart.
But something like blood was moving through the walls.
As if this entire place was the body of a dead creature whose circulation system had simply forgotten to stop.
Lian felt uncomfortable.
The hallway opened after the last step, he entered a hall that did not make sense with anything under the Palace in terms of size.
The ceiling was dozens of meters high, black pillars rose on both sides of the hall and carvings were made on every pillar.
He slowly moved forward, the first image showed a huge city that looked nothing like Cindari architecture.
The second pillar showed creatures descending from the sky.
The third, Forgotten Tree.
But the tree in that image was completely alive, its branches were full of light.
In the fourth carving, several leaders from different races and civilizations stood in front of a giant figure.
The Corrupted Titan, chains were wrapped around its body.
Something white could be seen in the center of the hall.
Lian stopped and looked more carefully, then realized that it was a coffin!
Larger than a normal coffin, made of white and black stone.
Seven golden chains were wrapped around it, each chain came from one of the seven directions of the hall and was connected to the coffin.
From under the coffin, there were also strands that looked like dried veins going into the ground.
Predator’s Instincts reacted, the blood flow he had sensed belonged to the corpse inside this coffin.
Lian slowly moved closer, each of his steps disappeared into the cold and empty hall, there was writing on the floor in front of the coffin.
Very old.
The System began translating.
[Ancient Script Detected.]
[Translation in Progress...]
Several seconds passed and then the text appeared in front of his eyes.
[Here Lies Cindar Vael.]
[The Last Survivor of the Final Battle.]
[The First Root of the Cindari.]
He stood there, his eyes first remained on the writing.
"So this is a tomb? The tomb of the Founder of the Cindari civilization?"

This time, he only sent a very thin wave of destruction into the structure.
The wave moved through the door.
He controlled the pressure, if he used too much power, the entire gate would explode and the Alarm would activate.
That was why, instead of breaking it, he only disrupted one of the internal connections of the locking mechanism, and the golden light shook for a moment and then went out.
The main lock became loose.
Lian opened the door only enough for himself to pass through the gap, then closed it again.
When he entered the First Archive, he stopped for a moment.
The space was huge, much larger than he had expected from outside, hundreds of pillars stood in the main hall.
Between them, shelves rose several meters high.
But the Archive did not only contain books, there were thousands of stone tablets and Crystal Memories with weak white and blue lights moving inside them.
Pieces of tree bark with ancient writings carved into them.
Maps so old that even the shapes of the three forests were different on them.
Broken Artifacts, rusty swords, and seals belonging to Kingdoms that no longer existed.
But his surprise only lasted for a few minutes and Lian quickly started searching.
First, Forgotten Tree.
He found a lot of information, its estimated age, its role in the Water Cycle of the three forests, and its connection to the world’s Mana Channels.
Its connection to Giant’s Graveyard, but there was nothing about the Cocoon.
Then Black Silence.
The results became fewer, many documents only mentioned it indirectly.
"Corruption."
"The Final Plague."
"Silence."
"The Enemy Without Form."
But there was no complete explanation, especially about the Vessel and the fetus, there was nothing.
Lian went after Cindar Vael and found more information.
First Founder.
Last Survivor.
Builder of Rootcrown.
Bearer of the First Root.
But details about the Final Battle?

Almost nothing, the records were either incomplete or parts of them had been intentionally erased, as if someone did not want any trace of the final battle between the leaders of the ancient civilizations of this world and the Corrupted Titan to remain.
Hours passed.
Lian left the main hall behind and entered the second section, but still found nothing.
Then the personal Archive of the old Rootwardens.
War maps, reports about Forgotten Tree, records of Expedition deaths, but the more he searched, the clearer the problem became.
Everything that actually came close to answering his questions suddenly stopped.
It was as if someone had recorded history up to a certain point and then drawn a blade across all the important lines.
There was not even a direct mention of the Black Silence Fetus.
Even the real reason for Forgotten Tree drying up was not recorded, as if no one really knew the reason for it, so it had never been recorded.
Finally, Lian put the last book back in its place and stood there alone for a few seconds, then sighed.
"Nothing." He felt that he might have really reached a dead end.
Why was Selina there?
Why was Forgotten Tree keeping her inside the Cocoon?
How had Black Silence entered her body?
Was the Titan still the main Vessel?
Was the Calamity being transferred?
Was the death of the tree caused by this transfer or was it related to something else?
And even if he understood all of them, how was he supposed to Devour The Black Silence?
The Quest appeared in his mind like a bad joke.
[Devour The Black Silence.]
Lian pressed his lips together, having an abnormal class that had never existed before also came with problems like this.
He basically did not know what he was facing or what he should do, he was completely in the dark and had no guidance, he had to discover and learn everything by himself.
For a moment, he looked at the huge shelves of the Archive, the information of hundreds of years of civilization was here.
But exactly what he needed did not exist, or worse, had been intentionally removed.
Lian decided not to waste any more time, if the First Archive had no answer, he had to return to Forgotten Tree.
Maybe the Cocoon itself would reveal more information as the Gestation progressed.
"If there is no other choice, I will have to agree to destroying the Cocoon." He thought to himself, if no one stopped him, they might face something they had no ability to resist.
As he was turning to leave, Predator’s Instincts suddenly reacted.
"This?" Lian went silent.
Three presences were approaching.
This time, the Skill was not giving him a simple warning of danger.
After Predator’s Instincts evolved, Lian could also sense the biological patterns of living creatures within a limited range.
He focused, three blood flows could be seen behind the western wall.
Not really with his eyes, but as an instinctive image in his mind.
Three Cindari, two were normal and one was stronger, but none of them were strong enough to be considered a serious threat to him.
They seemed to be here to patrol and nothing more.
He did not care much, he could move to the side of the hall and let them pass, there was no need to kill them.
But at that exact moment, he sensed something else.

Lian became completely still, Predator’s Instincts was still active, three blood flows were approaching the Archive from the hallway, after reaching a certain point and checking the surroundings, they turned around and left the area again.
Just as he had guessed, they were only a security patrol.
"But what is this?" But something else caught his attention, there was another flow.
Not in front of him or behind the wall, but below, much deeper below.
Lian slowly looked at the floor of the Archive, for a few seconds he thought he had sensed it wrong and focused again.
The flow existed.
But it was weak, very weak, something like blood was moving under the ground.
The problem was that no specific living creature could be sensed.
There was no beating heart, no breathing, only a weak flow, like veins that were still working inside a dead body.
Lian opened the World Memory Map, the map spread out in front of him.
Lord’s Root Palace.
According to the map, the lowest floor should be the Archive itself, there should be nothing deeper than this.
According to the map, the First Archive was the lowest built space in this area.
"Then what is down there?" Lian looked at the floor again.
Predator’s Instincts was not wrong, the flow existed.
Unless—
"A hidden floor." His eyes narrowed slightly.
Lian followed the underground flow, the image of blood in his mind passed under the floor and moved toward the northern part of the hall.
He slowly moved between the shelves, the flow finally became concentrated under one of the Statues.
He stood in front of it, the Statue was larger than all the other statues in the Archive.
Cindar Vael.
The Founder stood with one hand on his sword and the other around a golden root.
Lian examined the base of the Statue, there was no handle, no gap, or anything like that.
"I don’t have time for these games."
He placed his palm on the stone.
[Cataclysm Pulse.]
But this time, he did not release the wave outward, he sent it underground.
The wave passed through the layers of stone, the reflection came back and most of the floor was completely solid, but there was an empty space under the Statue!
"Found you." A short smile appeared on Lian’s lips.
He pushed his fingers into the very thin gap between the base of the Statue and the floor, the stone would not even move for a normal human.
Lian applied force, his Power increased, the muscles in his arms and shoulders tightened, and suddenly a very quiet sound came from under the stone.
Then the huge stone panel rose several centimeters.
At that exact moment, the hidden mechanisms around it lit up and golden lines spread across the floor.
The Alarm was activating.
Lian frowned, he gathered Thunder Calamity on two fingers at the lowest intensity possible.
A thin lightning bolt entered it, only one precise current, the first connection burned, the second shut down.
The third resisted for a moment, he applied more pressure, the lightning passed through it and it burned as well, in short, the Alarm never fully activated.
Lian lifted the stone panel higher, darkness could be seen underneath.
A staircase!
A narrow staircase that went straight down, deeper than anything that existed on the World Memory Map.
He entered without hesitation and lowered the panel as much as possible behind him.
Abyss Veil was still active.
Although Lian did not know that the three Cindari who had been patrolling had noticed those strange vibrations and were quickly coming to check.
At the same time, Lian was going down the stairs, after a few meters, the structure of the area changed.
The walls were made of black stone, dry white roots came out from the cracks.
There were very old writings on the walls and their language was different even from the writings in the city.
It was clear that they had been written in a much more ancient language, a language that was probably no longer used.
There was no longer any smell of the Archive, this place was not a library, it had an old smell and a slight smell of death and dead bodies.
Predator’s Instincts continued to follow the underground flow.
The deeper he went, the clearer the image became, but it also became stranger.
There was still no heart.
But something like blood was moving through the walls.
As if this entire place was the body of a dead creature whose circulation system had simply forgotten to stop.
Lian felt uncomfortable.
The hallway opened after the last step, he entered a hall that did not make sense with anything under the Palace in terms of size.
The ceiling was dozens of meters high, black pillars rose on both sides of the hall and carvings were made on every pillar.
He slowly moved forward, the first image showed a huge city that looked nothing like Cindari architecture.
The second pillar showed creatures descending from the sky.
The third, Forgotten Tree.
But the tree in that image was completely alive, its branches were full of light.
In the fourth carving, several leaders from different races and civilizations stood in front of a giant figure.
The Corrupted Titan, chains were wrapped around its body.
Something white could be seen in the center of the hall.
Lian stopped and looked more carefully, then realized that it was a coffin!
Larger than a normal coffin, made of white and black stone.
Seven golden chains were wrapped around it, each chain came from one of the seven directions of the hall and was connected to the coffin.
From under the coffin, there were also strands that looked like dried veins going into the ground.
Predator’s Instincts reacted, the blood flow he had sensed belonged to the corpse inside this coffin.
Lian slowly moved closer, each of his steps disappeared into the cold and empty hall, there was writing on the floor in front of the coffin.
Very old.
The System began translating.
[Ancient Script Detected.]
[Translation in Progress...]
Several seconds passed and then the text appeared in front of his eyes.
[Here Lies Cindar Vael.]
[The Last Survivor of the Final Battle.]
[The First Root of the Cindari.]
He stood there, his eyes first remained on the writing.
"So this is a tomb?
The tomb of the Founder of the Cindari civilization?"

chapters.title: Chapter 328: For Resurrection...?
paragraphs: [Here Lies Cindar Vael.]
[The Last Survivor of the Final Battle.]
[The First Root of the Cindari.]
Lian stood in front of the writing without moving for several seconds.
The underground hall was in complete silence, and only the weak light from the dry white roots on the walls allowed the shape of the coffin in the center of the tomb to be seen.
Cindar Vael.
A name he had heard more than any other person during the past few days.
The Founder of the Cindari.
The only survivor of a battle that had destroyed almost all the ancient civilizations of this world.
The man who had brought the First Root back from that battle and then built Rootcrown and a completely new civilization.
At first, the existence of his tomb was not strange, someone like him would naturally have a tomb.
But Lian only needed a few seconds to notice the main problem and frowned.
"Why?"
It was a simple question, but the more he looked at the surroundings, the stranger it became.
Why should the tomb of the Founder of the greatest civilization in this world be here?
Not in the center of Rootcrown, not inside a public temple, not under a huge Statue where the Cindari could visit to show their respect to him.
But on a floor that did not even exist on the World Memory Map.
Under the First Archive, under the most protected part of Lord’s Root Palace.
In a place whose entrance had been intentionally hidden and whose existence had not even been recorded by the map.
If Cindar was truly the great Hero of the Cindari, why was his tomb hidden?
If he was supposed to be respected, why did even the Archive above him have no mention of this place?
Even the fact that the existence of this tomb seemed to have been kept hidden was something that seemed worth questioning to him, even though it looked strange.
The tomb of such an important person would usually be a public place that everyone could enter, but the Cindari might simply have different traditions.
Lian moved his eyes over the seven golden chains, they were wrapped around the coffin and each one came from one of the directions of the hall and reached the center.
They were not the chains of a normal tomb, they looked more like something that was supposed to keep something in place.
But the strangest part was not that.
Predator’s Instincts was still sensing something, he slightly closed his eyes and focused more on the Skill.
The surroundings changed in his instinctive perception and blood flows appeared in his vision, but there should not have been any living creature in this hall.
However, under the coffin and among the roots connected to it, there were very weak flows.
Lian examined it more carefully for several seconds, there was no Heartbeat.
There was no breathing and no normal muscle movement but the blood was moving, so slowly that if he did not have Predator’s Instincts, he would never have noticed it.
Every few seconds, a very small amount of blood passed through one of the veins, it was almost stopped, but not completely, just enough for the body to continue being alive.
Lian looked at the coffin.
"You are not dead." His voice created a weak echo in the huge hall and then he moved forward.
This time, he did not examine the chains.
If he had found the hidden entrance to the Archive by force, there was no reason to play a game that had lasted for hundreds of years just to open a coffin.
He placed his hand on the edge of the white stone, the cover was thick, probably several tons in weight but weight was not something that could seriously stop Lian.
His fingers went under the edge of the stone and he applied pressure, at first nothing happened but then a very quiet sound came from the contact between stone and stone.
The cover moved ... several centimeters, then more and the seven golden chains shook slightly, but contrary to what he expected, they did not stop it from opening.
This made another point clear, the chains were not meant to close the coffin, they had another purpose.
Lian applied more force, the heavy cover slid over the edge and the sound of stone being dragged echoed through the dead hall.
A layer of old dust rose from its surface, at the same moment, cold air came out of the coffin, not the normal air of a tomb but a dry and lifeless cold.
He moved the cover far enough to clearly see inside the coffin and then stayed silent for a moment.
Cindar Vael was there.
Or at least what remained of his body, the body of a very thin man was lying inside the coffin.
His skin was so dry that it was almost stuck to his bones, the color of his skin was neither gray nor brown.
It looked more like very old leather that had been kept away from any moisture for centuries.
Dark veins could still be seen under the skin of his hands and neck.
His hair had almost completely turned white and was spread over the stone pillow behind his head.
His eyes were closed, his lips were dry, his cheeks were sunken.
If Lian had seen him somewhere else, he would probably have thought he was looking at the corpse of a Vampire that had slept for centuries without blood.
But something about the body was wrong.
The corpse had not rotted, there were no signs of decay, no real smell of death, no breaking down of the tissue and even the dark clothes covering Cindar’s body were almost completely intact.
He frowned and placed his hand on the man’s dry wrist, he felt no pulse.
Then he moved his hand to his neck and again found nothing but Predator’s Instincts was still showing the same very weak flow.
How could blood move inside this man’s body when it seemed that all of his organs were dead and completely stopped working? Was such a thing even possible?
"Unless the organs are working, but the evidence and what I am seeing show the opposite... unless." He thought for a moment and then checked the condition of the organs again.
Suddenly, something came to his mind but he was not sure, he checked the organs one by one to find even the smallest sign of life in them.
He placed his hand on the chest, in complete silence he focused all his attention and senses on it, waiting to catch even the smallest pulse.
One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.
Five seconds.
And finally, he succeeded.
"I see it, the heart, brain, liver, and all the other organs are almost completely inactive." Lian’s eyes narrowed slightly.
Suspended Death.
Not Alive, not Dead, something between the two.
The heart was practically not working, the lungs showed no movement. The muscles were almost completely inactive.
The nervous system showed no detectable activity, even the Mana Structure inside the body was nothing more than very weak strands.
But that was exactly the problem, almost ... not completely.
The heart had almost stopped, but not completely.
The blood flow was almost zero, but not completely.
Cellular activity was almost nonexistent, but not completely.
Lian kept his eyes on the dried body.
"If you were really supposed to be buried..." His eyes moved toward the thin roots connected to the back of the coffin.
"Why did they keep your body in this state?"
There was no logical reason for this kind of preservation.
If the Cindari only wanted their Founder’s body to remain intact, they could have mummified it.
They could have used Magic Preservation, they could have kept the body inside Crystal or ice.
But something else was happening here, the veins were still moving blood, Cellular Decay had been intentionally stopped.
A very small part of the Biological Functions had been preserved, for a corpse that was not supposed to be used again, this made no sense.
He stayed silent for a few seconds and then his expression suddenly changed, an idea came to his mind.
At first, it was so strange that even he did not accept it immediately, but the more he looked at the body, the more logical it became and he slowly whispered.
"Unless..." He paused for a few seconds, then his eyes stayed directly on Cindar’s dried face.
"You were supposed to come back." The hall became silent again.
But this time, the sentence remained in Lian’s mind, Cindar Vael was not supposed to be kept only as a respected corpse.
This body had been preserved so that one day it could be used again.
For a return, for Resurrection!

chapters.title: Chapter 329: The Forgotten Tree V
paragraphs: But this immediately created an even more dangerous question.
How?
How could a man who had died hundreds of years ago be sure that the conditions for his return would one day be ready?
No.
That was not the right question, for a few seconds, he looked at the very weak flow of blood under the man’s skin.
Then the images from the past few days appeared in his mind one after another.
Forgotten Tree.
A tree that was dying at a very fast rate.
Corrupted Titan.
A creature whose Awakening was connected to the death of the tree.
The Black Silence.
The Calamity that was inside the Titan.
Selina.
Cocoon.
[Black Silence Fetus.]
[New Calamity Vessel.]
And then the words Aurelia had said before.
"One of us allowed The Black Silence to enter."
Lian remained motionless, it only took another moment, but after that, all the information that had seemed scattered and unrelated took on a different meaning.
He looked at Cindar again.
This man did not simply know that he would come back to life!
He had planned to come back to life!
Lian’s eyes became cold, Cindar was the only survivor of the Final Battle, all the leaders of the other civilizations had died and then he built the Cindari civilization.

The main information about the Final Battle had almost been removed from history, there was no information about The Black Silence and all the records that could have been close to the truth were either damaged or deliberately erased.
And now, exactly when the Forgotten Tree was dying, Cindar’s body was still being kept in Suspended Death, as if it was meant to return one day.
Exactly when The Black Silence was finding a new Vessel, exactly when the Corrupted Titan was about to Awaken.
This many coincidences were no longer an accident.
"Bastard..." A few seconds later, another sentence quietly came out of his mouth.
"So Aurelia was talking about you.
He almost had no doubts anymore, Cindar was a traitor.

Someone who had allowed The Black Silence to enter this world and if his understanding of Aurelia’s words was correct, he might be the main reason why a Calamity was able to spread through this world.
Of course, it was still unclear how he had done it and how such a thing was even possible.
The person who became the only survivor after all the other leaders died, the person who later built a new civilization on the ruins of the old world.
And now, even after his own death, his plan was still being carried out.
For a moment, a small feeling of satisfaction appeared in Lian’s mind.
It was not satisfaction from what was happening, but from finally having one of the pieces of the puzzle fall into place.
But that feeling quickly disappeared, because the biggest question was still unanswered.
"Why?"
Lian looked at the body again, why would Cindar do something like this?
Power? Immortality? Control over a Calamity? Did he want to use The Black Silence to become a higher existence?
Or perhaps this entire cycle ... the death of the tree, the Awakening of the Titan, the creation of a new Vessel, all of it was part of his own Resurrection ritual?

If his guess was correct, then the man the Cindari considered the founder and hero of their history was actually nothing more than a fraud and a traitor who eventually caused the near-collapse of the world.

It would not even be wrong to say that the deaths of all the leaders of the ancient civilizations in that battle against the Corrupted Titan might have also been his doing, so he could remove all his rivals and obstacles from his path.
But... what the hell was his exact goal?
His eyes remained on the man’s dried chest, perhaps this body was not only waiting for Resurrection, perhaps it was waiting for something much bigger.
If Cindar had really planned for his return, he probably was not meant to return as an ordinary Cindari.
This thought was not pleasant, but there was another problem.
After a few more minutes of checking, Lian quickly reached an important conclusion, Cindar could not do anything at the moment, he was practically between life and death and had no awareness.
His body could not even move a finger.
There was no active Skill, no Mana flow that could reach the Forgotten Tree and no sign of remote control either.
"You didn’t do these things yourself." Lian pulled his hand away from the body.
This result was almost certain, if Cindar was behind everything, then his role must have been related to the original plan.
Someone else was carrying out that plan, a living person, someone who could move around Rootcrown, someone who had access to the Forgotten Tree.
Someone who probably knew what the Cocoon was, someone who could start the process of the tree’s death or at least allow it to continue.
And if the choice of Selina was also intentional, that person must also have access to or information about the Outsiders.
Lian stared at the coffin for a few seconds.
"There is someone else doing the work.
It could be a Descendant, or even someone much higher in the political structure of the Cindari than Maelor.
For now, it did not matter who, the logic was simple, if everything was progressing according to Cindar’s plan, someone had to be alive to carry out that plan.
And if the Cocoon was at 63.7% when Lian was there, that person probably had not finished their work yet.
He looked toward the entrance of the hall.
"Whoever it is... they’re either there right now, or they’re coming back very soon." For a moment, he remembered Seris and Aren, they were alone beside the Cocoon.
That thought was enough to remove all his interest in continuing to investigate the tomb.
Lian still wanted many answers.
But if his guess was correct, the person who had the answers might be near the Forgotten Tree right now.
He grabbed the heavy cover of the coffin, pulled it back into place and the sound of stone echoed through the hall, Cindar’s body slowly disappeared from view.
Lian did not touch the chains.
He still did not know exactly what they were connected to, breaking them might activate some mechanism.
It might remove the body from Suspended Death and the last thing he wanted to do was wake up a man who was probably behind the destruction of this world.
The cover closed completely and he turned around, his only goal now was to return immediately.
But he had not even reached the first step when a very distant sound came from above the tomb.
A bell, but it was weak.
Then a second bell, and this time it was louder.
Then dozens of similar sounds echoed from the higher levels of Rootcrown.
Alarm.
Lian stopped there and a few seconds later, a shout came from the hallway above.
"Infiltration confirmed!" Another voice shouted louder in response.
"First Archive breach confirmed!"
"Close all Inner Root gates!"
"Lord’s Root Palace is in complete Lockdown!"
"No one is allowed to leave!"
He closed his eyes for a moment, those three Cindari had probably finally noticed something.
Abyss Veil was still active, he was not afraid of getting trapped inside Rootcrown.
If necessary, he could force his way through the city walls.
The only problem was that outside this city, something was getting closer to its birth very quickly.

sentences.text: But this immediately created an even more dangerous question.
How?
How could a man who had died hundreds of years ago be sure that the conditions for his return would one day be ready?
No.
That was not the right question, for a few seconds, he looked at the very weak flow of blood under the man’s skin.
Then the images from the past few days appeared in his mind one after another.
Forgotten Tree.
A tree that was dying at a very fast rate.
Corrupted Titan.
A creature whose Awakening was connected to the death of the tree.
The Black Silence.
The Calamity that was inside the Titan.
Selina.
Cocoon.
[Black Silence Fetus.]
[New Calamity Vessel.]
And then the words Aurelia had said before.
"One of us allowed The Black Silence to enter."
Lian remained motionless, it only took another moment, but after that, all the information that had seemed scattered and unrelated took on a different meaning.
He looked at Cindar again.
This man did not simply know that he would come back to life!
He had planned to come back to life!
Lian’s eyes became cold, Cindar was the only survivor of the Final Battle, all the leaders of the other civilizations had died and then he built the Cindari civilization.

The main information about the Final Battle had almost been removed from history, there was no information about The Black Silence and all the records that could have been close to the truth were either damaged or deliberately erased.
And now, exactly when the Forgotten Tree was dying, Cindar’s body was still being kept in Suspended Death, as if it was meant to return one day.
Exactly when The Black Silence was finding a new Vessel, exactly when the Corrupted Titan was about to Awaken.
This many coincidences were no longer an accident.
"Bastard..." A few seconds later, another sentence quietly came out of his mouth.
"So Aurelia was talking about you.
He almost had no doubts anymore, Cindar was a traitor.

Someone who had allowed The Black Silence to enter this world and if his understanding of Aurelia’s words was correct, he might be the main reason why a Calamity was able to spread through this world.
Of course, it was still unclear how he had done it and how such a thing was even possible.
The person who became the only survivor after all the other leaders died, the person who later built a new civilization on the ruins of the old world.
And now, even after his own death, his plan was still being carried out.
For a moment, a small feeling of satisfaction appeared in Lian’s mind.
It was not satisfaction from what was happening, but from finally having one of the pieces of the puzzle fall into place.
But that feeling quickly disappeared, because the biggest question was still unanswered.
"Why?"
Lian looked at the body again, why would Cindar do something like this?
Power?
Immortality?
Control over a Calamity?
Did he want to use The Black Silence to become a higher existence?
Or perhaps this entire cycle ... the death of the tree, the Awakening of the Titan, the creation of a new Vessel, all of it was part of his own Resurrection ritual?

If his guess was correct, then the man the Cindari considered the founder and hero of their history was actually nothing more than a fraud and a traitor who eventually caused the near-collapse of the world.

It would not even be wrong to say that the deaths of all the leaders of the ancient civilizations in that battle against the Corrupted Titan might have also been his doing, so he could remove all his rivals and obstacles from his path.
But... what the hell was his exact goal?
His eyes remained on the man’s dried chest, perhaps this body was not only waiting for Resurrection, perhaps it was waiting for something much bigger.
If Cindar had really planned for his return, he probably was not meant to return as an ordinary Cindari.
This thought was not pleasant, but there was another problem.
After a few more minutes of checking, Lian quickly reached an important conclusion, Cindar could not do anything at the moment, he was practically between life and death and had no awareness.
His body could not even move a finger.
There was no active Skill, no Mana flow that could reach the Forgotten Tree and no sign of remote control either.
"You didn’t do these things yourself." Lian pulled his hand away from the body.
This result was almost certain, if Cindar was behind everything, then his role must have been related to the original plan.
Someone else was carrying out that plan, a living person, someone who could move around Rootcrown, someone who had access to the Forgotten Tree.
Someone who probably knew what the Cocoon was, someone who could start the process of the tree’s death or at least allow it to continue.
And if the choice of Selina was also intentional, that person must also have access to or information about the Outsiders.
Lian stared at the coffin for a few seconds.
"There is someone else doing the work.
It could be a Descendant, or even someone much higher in the political structure of the Cindari than Maelor.
For now, it did not matter who, the logic was simple, if everything was progressing according to Cindar’s plan, someone had to be alive to carry out that plan.
And if the Cocoon was at 63.7% when Lian was there, that person probably had not finished their work yet.
He looked toward the entrance of the hall.
"Whoever it is... they’re either there right now, or they’re coming back very soon." For a moment, he remembered Seris and Aren, they were alone beside the Cocoon.
That thought was enough to remove all his interest in continuing to investigate the tomb.
Lian still wanted many answers.
But if his guess was correct, the person who had the answers might be near the Forgotten Tree right now.
He grabbed the heavy cover of the coffin, pulled it back into place and the sound of stone echoed through the hall, Cindar’s body slowly disappeared from view.

chapters.title: Chapter 330: The Forgotten Tree VI
paragraphs: Forgotten Tree — At the Same Time
The silence around the Forgotten Tree was very different from the silence of the tomb beneath Rootcrown.
Here, the silence was not dead, it was waiting.
Seris stood beside the Cocoon.
One of her hands was near the handle of her sword and her eyes almost never left the semi-transparent surface of the Cocoon.
One stood a few meters away on its legs, its antennae moved every few seconds and from its behavior, it was clear that it did not like the area.
Aren was sitting on part of a dried root.
Almost nothing had happened since Lian left, and almost no conversation had happened either.
"Have you and Lian known each other for a long time?" Aren endured the silence for the first few minutes and finally asked.
"No." Seris said without taking her eyes off the Cocoon.
He waited for a few seconds, thinking that maybe there would be more, but there was not, it did not seem like this girl had any interest in explaining or talking more.
He looked around, a few more minutes passed and then he tried again.
"Is he always like this?"
"Yes." This time the young girl gave him a short look.
"What do you mean by like this?" Aren raised an eyebrow, he had asked this question randomly so he could start a conversation, but he received a confusing answer.
"Just like this." Seris thought for two seconds.
"I think you run out of things to say without Lian." Aren was genuinely helpless for a moment and then gave a short, dry laugh.
The young Pendragon looked at him a little longer this time, but she decided to stay silent and say nothing, she did not see a reason to answer.
Aren waited for an explanation, no explanation came and then he sighed and decided not to try anymore.
The truth was that Seris was almost always quiet.
Normally, hours could pass without her saying more than a few sentences.
Aren had understood this from the journey from Vhalaris to the Forgotten Tree.
But there was something strange, when Lian was there, Seris talked more.
She asked questions, made sarcastic comments and sometimes even made cold jokes.
He was not sure if the girl herself had noticed this difference, it was better not to say anything about it, especially because the answer would probably be the same one-word answer she always gave.
More minutes passed.
Gestation Progress had still not changed.
Seris checked the panel every few minutes, it remained stable and this stability slowly reduced some of the first pressure.
If the process could take this long to complete, maybe there was no need to worry too much, they had plenty of time to deal with the problem.
Seeing this, she did not lower her guard, but at least she felt a little better.
If the progress continued at this speed, they could follow Lian’s plan.
She personally had not planned to confront him like that at the time, and she did not want to kill this girl for no reason either.
But she had no choice, Seris knew that if someone had to do these difficult, cold, monstrous, and emotionless things, there was no one but her who could do them.
At that time, she also wanted to take the first step and destroy such a great threat, she knew that Lian would probably be angry with her and might even try to stop her from killing Selina.
But in her mind, she had already decided that if necessary, she would do it by force, too, this was something the Pendragon family had taught her since childhood.
That nothing was more important than protecting the world and her family, anything that could become a threat to either of them had to be destroyed immediately.

And when she read the System notifications about the Black Silence Fetus, she became certain that whatever was inside that Cocoon, if it was fully born, it would become a threat to their world and her family.
She wanted to destroy it according to her family’s teachings... she wanted to do it! She had to do it...

But she did not know why... why did her heart hurt when she saw Lian’s eyes become cold and heard his tone toward her... it was as if she could not stand the thought of that boy being angry with her...

But why? Why had she become like this? What kind of feeling was this? She had never experienced anything like this before... she had never cared about other people’s feelings and had always acted according to her family’s teachings and traditions.
So what was wrong with her now...
’What’s wrong with me...? Could I be sick...?’ she quietly whispered to herself.
However, before she could find an answer... suddenly, one of the white roots moved.
Seris immediately stood straight, One also raised its antennae and Aren stood up from the root.
"What happened?"
No one answered, the very weak golden light inside the roots became stronger for the first time.
The light came down from the huge trunk of the tree, flowed into the roots and went directly into the Cocoon.
The young girl took one step forward, her hand moved to the handle of her sword and then suddenly a sound came.
A sound that was almost impossible to mistake in that place.
Thump.
Aren held his breath and Seris frowned and a few seconds later it happened again.
Thump.
This was not Selina’s Heartbeat, it was much louder, much deeper, as if the Cocoon itself had gained a heart.
Seris immediately opened the panel.
[Calamity Gestation Progress: 64.1%]
Her eyes narrowed, the number had changed!
But it was still not high enough to cause panic, until it changed again.
Seris remained motionless and before she even had a chance to say anything, it increased again ...
"What happened?" Aren could not see anything, he did not have a System panel to see the percentage of the process.
She did not answer and the number increased again.
This time, her expression really changed.
"...Fuck it"
"What happened? Tell me!"
"The percentage is going up." Seris said.
"How fast?" Aren moved his eyes between her and the Cocoon.
Before the girl could answer, the System itself showed the answer.
Seris pulled her sword halfway out of its sheath.
The number changed once again.
Then it suddenly stopped...
She looked at the panel alone for a few seconds to make sure it would not suddenly rise again, for a moment she thought they were screwed.
"How much?" Aren asked in a more serious voice.

chapters.title: Chapter 331: The Forgotten Tree VII
paragraphs: "Eighty-one."
"How long did it take?"
"A few seconds." Seris did not take her eyes off the Cocoon.
This answer worried both of them, if the increase was linear, maybe they still had time.
But now it was clear that the Progress could suddenly jump.
63.7 to 81, in only a few seconds and if another similar jump happened, the Cocoon could reach 100% before Lian returned.
Seris moved closer, the changes in the Cocoon could be clearly seen, the white roots on its surface were no longer still, they slowly contracted and relaxed, like veins.
The golden light inside them was no longer pure either, black lines were moving through the light.
Inside the Cocoon, Selina still had her eyes closed, but the fingers of her right hand suddenly moved.
Seris stopped there.
"Did she move...?" Aren saw it too.
A black vein appeared under Selina’s skin, it moved up from the bottom of her neck, reached the side of her jaw and then disappeared again.
The young Pendragon pulled her sword a little farther out, this time she herself did not know what decision she would make if the percentage increased again.
Lian had told her not to destroy the Cocoon, but Lian was not there.
And if the Progress reached 90, 95 or even 99, there might be no chance left to make a decision.
"What are you going to do?" Aren looked at her sword.
"I don’t know."
This was probably the longest honest answer Aren had heard from her since Lian left and a few seconds later Seris added.
"If it jumps again... we may have no choice." She did not finish the sentence, there was no need.
Aren understood what she meant, but before they could make a decision.
One’s entire body suddenly became completely still, its antennae, which had been pointing toward the Cocoon until that moment, suddenly turned toward the west.
Seris immediately turned her head, she had sensed something, a strange and special smell, a powerful presence was getting close.
Not a Monster, but a smell that was similar to the Cindari, while still being different from them.
Aren also heard the sound of footsteps a few seconds later.
Slow, regular, without hurry, someone was moving through the Dead Zone.
This alone was strange, the Cindari were afraid of this area.
Even Maelor had said that an Expedition of seventy-three people had only three survivors.
But the person coming toward them was not running, was not hiding and did not even seem to be careful around the area.
The footsteps came closer, the sound of shoes touching the gray ground and suddenly a shadow appeared in the thin mist ... then a man came out of it.

Seris immediately frowned and pulled out her sword, she did not know why she suddenly felt such a terrible sense of danger, this was one of the strongest danger senses she had felt in this entire Special Area.
Whatever was coming closer... was very powerful even though it was a Cindari.
And his appearance was different from everyone they had seen until now, he was wearing a long robe that was white and black.
Golden lines ran along his collar and sleeves, he had no heavy armor.
No shield, no large weapon, only a thin sword with a white sheath could be seen at his waist.
A small white crown was on his head, not a fancy crown, more like a very old ring that represented his position.
His long dark hair reached his shoulders, his face was calm, too calm.
The worst part was the way the Dead Zone reacted to him.
The black liquid that was flowing through one of the cracks in the ground seemed to naturally change its path when he got close.
It did not come closer to him.
"Who are you?" Seris pointed her sword forward.
The man did not answer, he did not even look at her and his eyes were fixed directly on the Cocoon.
Aren was also staring at the man, he felt that the face was familiar, as if he had seen him before.
He tried to remember but nothing came to his mind ... then his eyes fell on the white crown.
His eyes opened a little wider.
"Wait ..."
Seris gave him a short look.
"That..." Aren took one step back and for a moment it seemed like even he did not want to believe what he had realized.
"He is the current leader of all Cindari." He said with disbelief.
Seris immediately looked back at the man and the System reacted at the same moment.
[Race: Cindari]
[Level: 35]
Level 35.
Maelor with Level 30 had reached that level of power alone inside Vhalaris with the Territorial Covenant.
Kael was also one of the strongest Cindari commanders.
But the man in front of them was Level 35 and had entered an area alone that most Cindari and no one else even dared to get close to.
Seris held her sword tighter and understood why she had such a terrible feeling of danger, a damn Level 35 was here!
’This could be troublesome...’ A frown appeared on her face.
She had never fought a Monster, an Awakened, or anything else at Level 35 before, and she did not think she could defeat one of them at her current level.

But that did not make her want to back down and run away, until Lian returned, she would continue protecting the Cocoon, no matter the cost... giving up and running away were not part of her teachings or traditions.
But the person they had been talking about was only focused on the Cocoon and then the corner of the man’s lips moved slightly upward.
His eyes remained on the roots that were now pulsing with golden and black light.
"Finally, the fetus is becoming complete." He said very calmly.
And that was when the two of them, Seris and Aren, understood that the real problem was that the leader of the Cindari knew exactly what was being born inside that Cocoon.
And he probably had the answers to all the secrets and mysteries ...
